en: Brought iron, goldsmith's shop, ceramics, stone and glass of art, tombolo; on Sunday the local products market in Piazza San Francesco and on the last Saturday of the month the antique market.
Documented as early as 1426, it has twelve bronze masks of satyrs and fauns around the Rising Knight in stone, emblem of the city.

Fraction on the slopes of Mount Misma with origins in the twelfth century and the church of the Holy Trinity of the fifteenth century. The young Pierina Morosini, beatified in 1987, rests in the parish of Sant'Antonio da Padova; a small exhibition space is dedicated to her life.
A century of motors and mechanics.
The altar of the Longobard kings.
An almost intact Renaissance city, almost 9 km long, now a park that can be walked and cycled.

In Casa Buffa Giacantoni, inhabited by generations of print sellers and empty since the 1960s, tells the street papers that sold art prints in the world, opening shops and becoming publishers, and the families remained in the country. It is run by the Trentina Alcide De Gasperi Foundation.
The mountain of Cavalese by cable car.

At 411 meters, probably born as a castrum in the war against Hannibal (217 BC); from the twelfth century under Perugia and entrusted to the Vincioli, occupied in 1390 by Michelozzo Michelotti, rebuilt at the end of the fourteenth century and destroyed again in 1642. Palazzo Vincioli (XIII-XIV century) is an important example of medieval civil architecture.
Enter one of the highest nuragic domes on the island.

The bell tower in Romanesque-Lucchese style next to the church was built in 1280 and, with its wounds, also had defensive function: it still looks like a medieval fortress. It hosts the bell "La Smarrita" which every night at the night of the dark sounded to guide the pilgrims to the hospital.
The museum of the Foundation Plart with the collection of objects and plastic works built in thirty years by Maria Pia Incutti, an international benchmark for polymer design.
Where the writer was born.

Inaugurated in 1994 and managed by the CISNIAR (Italian Centre for Artificial Nest Studies): seven rooms, the first on geology, paleontology and ecology, the others with panels, aquaterrariums and dioramas that reconstruct the environments from the Apennines to the Modena plain. Mineral, paleontological and zoological collections with thousands of specimens from all over Europe, the herbarium Branchetti and sections of mycology and lichenology; laboratory with microscopes and naturalistic library.
the MiC card indicates the foundation closed every day, how to visit to verify
A mountain chapel at 1500 meters.
An intact cryptoporic in a former convent.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 7 of the 13 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

Natural walls on the slopes of Bracco, frequented also in winter thanks to the exposure to the sun, with the Ninfe Falesia and other routes from 4a to 7c+; there is also a boulder area with 11 blocks and over 90 passages.
It preserves the bezel with the Coronation of the Virgin of Nicola da Guardiagrele, once on the portal of the collegiate.
The large park behind the Castle to the Arch of Peace, one of the most important neoclassical monuments in the city.

The historic centre preserves the palaces De Filippis, Donati and Schettini and the artisan workshops; in Piazza Italia a sculpture of Maurizio Carnivali from the eighties recalls the hypothesis that the isthmus of Catanzaro was the Umerica Scheria dei Feaci. From the village you can see the Tyrrhenian and Ionian.
The Baroque pulpit of Auregio Termine and the view from the viewpoint.
The world of a great family of puppet masters.
The oratory of the village.

Ring of ups and downs suitable for running and walking: from Piazza Don Zunino to Via Persego (information totem) to Casa Boragni, on mule track between the olive trees around the Cima della Brona to the balcony of Monte Grosso with a small wooden cross and picnic area, then down in the valley Bottassano, up to Bardino Vecchio to the ruins of the castle of Folchi and back to the village of Poggio. PDF map on the site of the Municipality.
Five natural rooms of the Apennines, with an 18th century herbarium.

Romanesque church of the 11th century, rebuilt in the Baroque period, with interior renovated in neo-Gothic style and neo-Romanesque façade of 1965; it contains frescoes, a altarpiece of the Assumption and eighteenth-century statues.
Visitable only in the extraordinary openings of the Superintendence (in 2026 in July and August); guided tours through the Pro Loco

Natural park in the center of the village: the waterfall, about 4 meters high, is a jump of the river San Leonardo, tributary of Belice, which has dug a pool among limestone rocks; glauconic yellow and green walls with rock vegetation and remains of an ancient aqueduct, and above the canyon. The steep path starts from the Benedictine monastery of the SS. Salvatore and climb to the Rocca dei Maschi, with views of the canyon, the Saracen Tower, the Hermitage of San Bernardo and the Rocca Busambra.
Paolo Veneziano, Cima and Bellini are just a few steps from the cathedral.

Worker's district built in the late nineteenth century by the Swiss entrepreneur Napoleone Leumann and designed to be self-sufficient: houses, boarding house for workers, public baths, theater, surgery, post office, hotel, kindergarten, schools, church, club and dealership. It preserves the historic station of the Turin-Rivoli line, the old primary school and several restored Art Nouveau buildings, and is still inhabited by a hundred families. Guided tours on scheduled dates (with entrance to the Village Museum): €17, reduced €8.
The cradle of the Malatesta and, many centuries before, the center of the Villanovian civilization: the Rocca del Sasso and the Archaeological Museum. Orange Flag since 2005.

Orvinio is the highest village in the park; around the village a garden of spontaneous orchids and medicinal herbs, walking, cycling and horseback riding routes, and the passage of the Way of St. Benedict.

It rises on the site of a church already existing in the fourteenth century (Saint Peter in Pincoli, then dedicated to the Saints Grateful and Rocco) and became parish in 1765, separating from Lanzo. At the main altar eighteenth-century altar with the Virgin and the patrons; at the altar of the Rosary a crucifix of the sixteenth century, with paintings of the Madonna del Rosario and purgant souls surrounded by Mysteries.

In front of the Matrix Church, it exhibits liturgical silvers of the XVI-XIX centuries (calics, pissides, monstrances) and vestments of the XVIII-XIX centuries, paliotti and pivials in precious fabrics embroidered in gold thread, coming from the main church of the country. Tel. +39 329 437 8774.
Four centuries of academy.
The oldest road in the valley.
Walking through the streets of a Roman city stopped at 79 A.D.
The pisan mast on the granite cliff.
The ferruginous waters known from the seventeenth century.

55 meters high, started in 1555 under Venice in the center of the Citadel; in the Venetian era it hosted the men's prison. In 1880 the metal dome was replaced by the medieval crenellated crown of Antonio Tagliaferri; it has three bells dedicated to the patrons and the mechanism of the clock is visible inside.
The sunset over the cove from the bridge.

The first nucleus of the year Maybe Mille, linked to the defensive towers of San Clemente in Casauria; the present building was born from the works started on 17 December 1719 by the Mazara di Sulmona (Marchesa Smeralda) and lost a floor with the earthquake of 1915. Acquired by the Gizzi family in 1967, since 1979 it hosts the Institute of Studies and Research Casa di Dante in Abruzzo with Dante's Museum, Caldora Library, annual exhibitions on Divine Comedy, the tower and a panoramic park.

On a south-east height of the city, the italian temple of Minerva destroyed at the end of the 5th century AD and above it a central-planted early Christian basilica, the most imposing of its kind in Puglia, with polychrome mosaics such as the 'mosaico del pavone', the Antiquarium, opened in 2008, exhibits its findings.
The view of Taormina and the coast.
Understand the 1976 earthquake and reconstruction.

Established in 1972 and today in Palazzo Margiotta: on the first floor the history of the diocese up to the nineteenth century with sacred works, the second renewal of the cult of St. Richard, with the relics of the saint in the golden wooden urn, the silver bust, the mitre and the pastoral.

Facade with horizontal white and black bands of the early thirteenth century, dome completed at the end of the sixteenth century; in the ancient crypt the Treasury Museum set up in 1956 by Franco Albini, next to the Diocesan Museum.
Romanesque chapel of the 12th century.
The garden is a movie set.
The fountain of the legend of Zizza and Lembasi.

The archaeological area of Agrigento, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997, considered one of the most beautiful archaeological parks in the world for vastness and conservation; it also includes the Hellenistic-Roman quarter.

Country of Lessinia between stone districts and pastures: in Camposilvano the Geopaleontological Museum, with admonites, dinosaur footprints and a skeleton of the cave bear, gives access to the Covolo, karst cavity more than 80 meters deep. Above the village the church of the Transfiguration on Mount Purga, at 1257 meters, looks up to the Po Valley.
€12, reduced €6

The village retains a medieval appearance with paved streets in limestone; in the streets Landone, Scarpitti and Trinità you can see stone portals, wrought iron balconies, cisterns and residences of the Jewish families, De Paulis and Del Giudice. The village was probably born around a fortress: the remains of the Longobard castle are visible near the Upper Gate.
in the MuSa complex, closed from 5 October 2026 for works, reopened scheduled in spring 2027
The church reached from Via Orto di Schiavonia, just outside the homonymous gate, in the northwest district of the center.
The oldest sacred theatre.

Inaugurated in 2004 in the Prince's Palace, where many finds had emerged during the restoration of 1999, followed by excavations at the University of Lecce. It exhibits objects, ceramics and instruments from the Messapian age to the Middle Ages and the Renaissance, with in the center of the hall a plastic of the village; it was the first example in Salento of valorization of an ancient village through its archaeological evidences. Open every day 9-13 and 16-20, closed on Tuesdays; access ramp, Braille guides, audioguides and tactile path.
€5, reduced available
With the kids after Farnese.
The parish church of the valley and its very high bell tower.
Centuries of music in the showcase.
Churches and festivals of the country.
Terraced garden on the hill of Costa San Giorgio, with a pergola of wisteria, a baroque staircase and one of the most beautiful views of Florence.
Set up at the headquarters of the Pro Loco, it collects objects, tools and furniture of the ethnic area.
The historic heart of the city.
visit only with guided tour to book at the Tourist Office of Montieri
A sheltered beach suitable for children.
The park is temporarily closed for work, the garden remains open
The Museum of Lombroso.
View of the sea and the prehistory of the coast.
Church of the sixteenth century in red trachyte, rebuilt in modern times; the stone comes from the local quarries of red trachyte, green and grey worked by the stonemasons of the village.
The Etruscan necropolis and the ancient Etruscan and medieval walls of the village.
Municipal exhibition space with gipsoteca and art exhibitions.

The first testimonies date back to the thirteenth century, but the foundation is considered to be earlier. It preserves valuable mural paintings in the presbytery and, of the same period, the wooden furnishings of the sacristy.

It was mentioned since 1313, it became a parish in the 16th century and a parish church in 1593; transformed in the 17th and 19th centuries, a restoration has recreated nineteenth century decorations and colours. The fourteenth century remains traces in the outer walls and in the stone bell tower; the interior with three naves has the central covered by false domes, marble balustrade and square choir with dome. Around the parish church there is the medieval village.
Baths and kayaks under the village.
The September festival that recalls the whole Ionian Riviera.

Ancient parish church mentioned in 1186, rebuilt several times: the current church, designed in 1728 by Giuseppe Castelli and completed in 1778 by his son Filippo, has a single nave with side chapels and a pronao of four Corinthian columns on six steps. It preserves paintings attributed to Giorgio Alberini (1620 about), palaces by Bernardino Galliari (1776), a wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century and the silver reliquary of San Lorenzo, of the Roman school of the eighteenth century.

Set up in the eighties in the former Maglio Beltrami, it tells the system of sweats moved from the waters of Nossana: the iron of the mines of Scalve and Bondione was worked at the Maglio Fusore and then forged in the lesser, large and larger sweats to obtain nails, spades, shovels and hoes. The forges of Ponte Nossa are documented from the fifteenth century; the ciodarol lived there with the family until the seventies. Visits only by reservation (035 704388, info@comune.pontenossa.bg.it).
An easy walk among the carved creatures of the woods.

Ancient village of the Valchiusella at 827 m, with stone houses, wooden balconies for drying chestnuts and corn and roofs in lose; its mining past is recounted in the mineralogical museum of the Ecomuseo "Il ferro e la diorite" with galleries of the Geoparco, while the paths lead to the rock engravings of the Path of the Souls and the cantons of the Via dei Cantoni.
Out of season is closed
Convent where St Bernardino retired at the beginning of the fifteenth century; in front of the entrance the linden planted on that occasion.

The panoramic avenue called "tradone" follows the semicircular course of the Angevin-Aragonese walls, with the defensive towers and the two surviving doors, Porta Nova and Porta San Demetrio; on the other side the view extends over the Plain of Olives and, on clear days, over the Adriatic.
The story of salami where they have been for 140 years.
Defensive ditch of the 4th millennium BC (Eneolithic), whose materials are exhibited in the State Archaeological Museum; the site is visitable and equipped with educational panels.
Just outside the village, at the entrance of the ancient mule track for Caprauna and near the cemetery, it preserves a fresco from the 15th century.
The Baroque church in the center of the village.
The Roman Codroipo.
The stage of the Passion, in the year of the new edition.

Around Larino there are hundreds of kilometers of ancient tracts, the streets of transhumance used by the shepherds to move the flocks between Abruzzo and Puglia: there are still and you can walk, among wheat fields and olive groves of Gentile di Larino.
Square feudal stone tower, probably before the viceroyal era, backward from the coast along the river Lipuda, which probably served to control.
A vineyard in town.
A triptych by Ambrogio Lorenzetti in a village of Amiata.

13th century hydraulic complex, important technological innovation: in the Middle Ages the mills grind the wheat for the population, exploiting the spring water of the Lattari Mountains which fell by gravity from one mill to another at different altitudes, with a domino effect. The valley is part of an ancient route that connected Castellammare di Stabia to Amalfi and in the Seven and nineteenth centuries was painted by the artists of the Grand Tour.
The territory told in twelve sections.
The loggia from the Conero in Loreto.
The panorama from the Aeolian to the Etna.
The hills have grown around the castle of the federiciano; there are the Mancinelli palaces, Lancellotti (with the family chapel), Pizzuti and Errico, and the fountains of the historic center.

Remains of the monastery built by the Benedictines around the year 1000, a couple of kilometers from the village outside the walls, called "a small San Galgano" with the sky for roof. In Romanesque style with Gothic elements and original Latin cross plan, they retain the semicircular apse, the transept walls and arches that held the dome, with foliage capitals and anthropomorphic heads similar to those of San Rabano.
The shrine on the lake and the Procession of Christs.
An ancient little church on the hill of Malnate.
The Lucan peasant life in 255 objects.
The peasant life of Cilento in a thousand objects.
A thousand years of history between church and cloister.
The reliquary of San Bernardino.
Borgo on a spur at 603 meters on the valley of the Tenna, in front of the Sibillini: in the church of San Martino Bishop three polyptychs of the Crivelli brothers.
The gorges of the Ayasse.
The tools of the dairy and the shops.

On the ground floor of Villa Kupfer, in the municipal park of the Three Villas, collects since 2004, thanks to the volunteers of the association Il Sestante, relics and models linked to the sea from the eighteenth to the twentieth century: great naval models like the H.M.S. Victory and the Polar Star, nautical charts, vintage flags, sextant, compass, axe master tools and objects of the Amerigo Vespucci school ship. The source does not indicate timetables: contact the contact person of the association.
Road crafts on two wheels.
The great early Christian mosaic.

Late church built in the late fifteenth century by the Friars Minor observing together with a convent. Inside there is a wooden group of the Madonna with the Child (Madonna of the Angels) of the sixteenth century, probably arrived from southern Italy.

In the Val di Saént, a side valley towards the pass of the same name, the ring tour of medium difficulty leads to see two waterfalls and is also suitable for children; the waterfalls are among the most famous destinations of the valley and can be reached also from the suspended bridge passing through the area of the Coler and Stablasolo mountain hut.
A tour of the noble palaces of the village.

Municipality of the lower Camonica Valley with a series of fifteenth-century churches and the late Baroque parish church of Saints Cornelius and Cipriano, with works by Andrea Fantoni, Giacomo Ceruti and Gaspare Diziani; it houses the Museum of Print "Lodovico Pavoni" and, at altitude, shares with Pian Camuno the station of Montecampione.

Country on the Varese shore of Lake Maggiore, with beaches, parks and numerous erratic boulders left by glaciers: the largest is the Sasso Cavallazzo, on the shore of the Gulf of Quassa Park that shares with Ispra.
Porta cinquecentesca a Citadella designed by Giulio Romano.

The village above Merano is dominated by Castel Schenna, from the 14th century, still home to the Counts of Merano; next to the neo-Gothic mausoleum of Archduke John of Austria and a hill with churches of eight different centuries, from the Romanesque Saint Martin to the new parish, while in San Giorgio a rare round church contains frescoes of the fourteenth century.

Medieval village on a spur among the woods near Mount Cuccola. The facade of the Palazzo dei Capitani della Montagna brings 96 coats of arms in stone and polychrome terracotta left by the Captains in memory of the mandate; it is admired from the fifteenth-century loggia in front, near the fountain and the church of the Madonna di Piazza.

The door of the Roman Castles overlooking Rome: the Tuscan villas of the popes and cardinals with Villa Aldobrandini on the head, the Stables with the Tuscolano Museum, the Cathedral of St. Peter and, above the city, the ruins of Tuscolo with the Roman theatre.

The streets of the palaces and noble towers: Palletta House, Natta Tower and Palace, Asinari-Verasis Palace, Della Rovere Palace, Strata Palace with its tower and Bune Palace, bishop's seat from the 15th century.
Deer, mouflons and an arc of pink granite.
At altitude above the Finalese.
On the road to Montelaterone, among the chestnut groves: built in 1268 on the remains of an older building, it is considered one of the most significant Romanesque buildings in southern Tuscany.

The sixteenth-century Palazzo Varo, Renaissance, preserves the portal with a noble coat of arms, the internal stone staircase and the cellars; purchased by the Diocese of Troy at the beginning of the twentieth century, on the first floor houses the museum, with archaeological finds, works of art and objects of use from the Neolithic to the twentieth century.

Bishop's seat since 1066, inaugurated in 1627 and severely damaged by the eruption of Vesuvius in 1631; the seventeenth-century coffered ceiling of Angelo and Francesco Solimena has 21 canvases, the cone of the presbytery depicts Saint Michael who defeats Lucifer.

Palace designed by Marcello Piacentini on Piazza De Nava, one of the rare buildings created to accommodate museum collections. At level D the Bronzes of Riace, masterpieces of the Greek bronze of the fifth century BC found in 1972, with the Kouros, the Head of the philosopher, the Head of Basel, the Dioscuri and the pinakes.

In a former sawmill of 1919 near the lake of Forte Buso, tells the Forest of the violins, whose red firs give wood to the lute lute; not far away the deer fence and the path Marcì, without barriers, in the forest.

Country shrine between San Nazzaro Sesia and Villata, with devotion attested from 1591 and pilgrimages from the seventeenth century; the church was rebuilt in 1752-68 on a previous structure. Under the marble altar, with a palotto made of hard stones and a rococo eraser made of wrought iron, a spring gushes out; it preserves frescoes of Peracino (1767) and G. Avondo (1817) and a small 16th century painting of the Miracle.

It is reached from the hamlet of Foce: at 1.940 meters, it is the only natural basin of glacial origin of the Marche. Medieval legends placed the bones of the Roman prosecutor who condemned Jesus; in his living waters the Cirocephalus marcasonii, a small crustacean that does not exist anywhere else in the world.
An underground mill of the eighteenth century with a view of the plain towards the sea.
The port and the cathedral.

Village of alleys, stairs and stone houses on the Brescia shore of Garda, once the most northern commercial citrus growing area in the world; to see the eighteenth-century Limonaia del Castèl, the marina, the Museo dei Pescatori in the park of Villa Boghi and the cycle path suspended on the lake.

Award with the Vele Legambiente: in Caminia a long stretch of free beach alternates with establishments up to the promontory of Copanello, with calm sea and protected from the rocks, suitable for diving by day and night. Copanello is suitable for sailing.
the source indicates important renovations in progress on the dock

Village inhabited by the Sicans since the second millennium BC and destroyed by a sudden event at the end of the Bronze Age: fifteen circular huts with an entrance "a forcepe" are seen; from hut 15 are the skeleton of a young woman, called Nina, and over one hundred almost intact vases. Visit by appointment with the archaeological park of Segesta.

The medieval village, an ancient settlement in the battles between Montefeltro and Malatesta, has a spiral system with narrow roads that go up the hill, about 300 meters above the valley of the Conca. Two gates mark the ancient gates of the castle, disappeared with the drawbridge; the walls were incorporated into the houses in the seventeenth century, while the current wall dates back to the early twentieth century. At the entrance the seventeenth-century Palazzo Massaioli, seat of the Town Hall; Piazza Garibaldi, for its acoustics, hosts concerts and events.

Mother church in the medieval village, with three asymmetric aisles on a Latin cross plan resting on the rock. Destroyed by the 1720 earthquake, it was rebuilt in 1725 by Duke Nicola Petra, whose tomb was found in 2000 under the organ, and enlarged in 1762. It preserves the statue of St. Prospero, patron saint of the village, carved in 1764 by Silverio Giovannitto di Oratino, with the relic of the saint brought in 1743 by Cardinal Vincenzo Petra, the organ of 1769 of the D'Onofrio family, restored, a stone aquasantiera of 1795, the Last Supper of 1890, works of Neapolitan school between the end of the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries and a group in mache of St. Anne, St. Joachim and the Virgin child.

The 14th century monastic complex on a promontory overlooking the sea along the road to Portofino, founded by the Carthusians of San Bartolomeo di Rivarolo; in the 15th century it was the seat of an important Benedictine congregation and was locked in the tower-prison Francesco I of Valois after the defeat of Pavia. National monument since 1912, restored in 1990, is now private and hosts events. The visit includes a seventeenth-century portal, a 16th-century defence tower, a lower cloister with a foundation epigraph, a chapel, a top garden with sixty pillars covered with vegetation and a bouganville pergola and a terrace overlooking the monumental Italian garden, with views from the Cinque Terre in Portofino.
Romanesque church of the 12th century with cloister and fountain of Brigliadore; it houses the Franciscan Library and the Museum of Gremi and Candelieri.

A stone village of northern Barbagia, more than 500 meters in a valley 40 km from Nuoro, home of the tenor singing (UNESCO intangible heritage) told in a multimedia museum; in the territory the nuragic village-sanctuary of Romanzesu.
15th century frescoes in the woods.

The brewery, founded in 1897, has rooms with painted walls, staircases, columns and copper mescita counters, and a large park with tennis courts and bowls; it houses exhibitions, tournaments, concerts and outdoor shows. A cycle path along the Colmeda stream takes about 10 minutes to the center.
The history of Valtellina in a palace.

Coastal lighthouse, visible from the outside; archaeological investigations of the last twenty years have found traces of human attendance from the age of Copper to the Greek era in the area. The MiC indicates opening every day 8-18, without reservation.

Opened in 2012 by the MAG Museo Alto Garda in the seventeenth-century Palazzo dei Panni, it is dedicated to Giovanni Segantini (Arco 1858-1899), one of the major exponents of divisionism: paintings, sculptures and works on his own paper and contemporary Trentino and Veneto such as Eugenio Prati, Vittore Grubicy and Alessandro Milesi, works by Leonardo Bistolfi, a documentary section and interactive posts. Since November 2024 he has exhibited "Autumn sun," not visible to the public since 1954. Free entrance with Garda Trentino Guest Card and Museum Pass.

It preserves pottery of Magna Grecia, a high relief of the Ninfa Zizza and a collection of bans from the seventeenth century to the Anglo-American occupation; it also exhibits paintings of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, including a work by Sciuti and works by the local Sebastiano Guzzone, Giuseppe Barone and Santo Marino.
The coral chapel.
A little green on the pelvis.

13th century church in late Romanesque style, with a large nave and semicircular apse; outside three Romanesque monofores and an arched portal to the sixth. Next, connected by a tunnel, the environment that was the home of Blessed James Papocchi; on the altar a 1618 painting depicts Jesus speaking with the blessed in his penitential cell.
The missing city from which Philadelphia was born.
times not indicated by the MiC card; optional booking, tel. 328 1175155
The village of the Malatesta peace treaties, with the Palaeontological Museum, the majolica and the botanical garden of the Arboreto of nine hectares.

Complex of rocky walls of different difficulty for free climbing, indicated by italia.it as a destination for those who love untouched nature, with wild rocks and ancient stalactites. Hiking on horseback, hiking and hang gliding are practiced around.
Church of the thirteenth century dedicated to the Assumption, already cathedral, in the heart of the historical center beyond the Arch of Marchesale, on the same square of the Palazzo dell'Orologio.

Born in 1935 as a gallery founded by Riccardo Assanti and Pietro Gaudenzi with 20 works created on site and became a museum in 2001, it occupies on three floors the Brancaccio Palace in the area of the ancient castle then a baronial palace. About 700 works including drawings, paintings, sculptures and prints from the late nineteenth century to the seventies, donated by artists related to the country: Kokoschka, Felice Carena, Arturo Martini, Adolfo De Carolis, Giulio Aristide Sartorio, Augusto Corelli, Pietro Gaudenzi, Giuseppe Capogrossi, Fausto Pirandello, Rafael Alberti and the model became painter Pasqualosa Marcelli Bertoletti.

Of probable Longobard origin, under control of the Volturno valley against Saracen incursions, it had a walls in Norman times; from 1503 to 1668 it was the D'Afvolta, then the Pignatelli, who transformed it into residence. A door with a Renaissance balcony and a staircase lead to the loggia; on the first floor the hall of representation has a large marble fireplace, a terracotta floor with the coat of arms of the Pignatelli (three 'pignate's) and a wooden ceiling of the eighteenth century painted in tempera with chivalry motifs, while a tower preserves a room covered with majolica. On the second floor it runs the way of rounds with slits and cadio; on the ground floor kitchens, ovens and cellars with large barrels. Visits on Saturday and Sunday (10:30-12:30 and 17:00-18:30) only by reservation at least 2 days before, on phone 0865 491586.

Inaugurated on April 26, 2003 for the feast of Our Lady of the Heart: the central room exhibits historical documents and ancient tools of the master inflorers, with the techniques and flowers used over time; another room collects the photographic archive of inflorate of Gerano, Italy and abroad, and a section is dedicated to traditional crafts and archaeological finds.
Church of the patron, rebuilt after 1908 on a project by Camillo Author: Latin cross plan, facade with a Roman triumph arch and dome on high drum, mosaic in the apse.
The Baroque of Via Roma.
Two of the medieval military towers of the city, visible above the Trajan Markets.

Borgo Ciociano from the medieval center closed by walls with eighteen towers and three doors; in the Palazzo Filonardi, redesigned by the Vignola, the abbey of San Pietro Ispano houses the Angel of Giotto, a mosaic fragment of the ancient basilica of San Pietro, and a early Christian sarcophagus with one of the oldest Nativity carved.
The center with three doors, Piazza San Dalmatio, the house Mugnaini-Ricci of the twelfth century, the 14th century municipal palace and the church with works of the Pomarancio.

Cities between the Gulf of Palermo and Termini Imerese, known for the villas of the Palermitan nobility built between the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries: Villa Palagonia with its stone monsters, Villa Cattolica with the Museum Renato Guttuso, Villa Valguarnera and Palazzo Butera; home of Guttuso and set of the films of Giuseppe Tornatore (Baarìa) and New Cinema Paradiso (New Cinema Paradiso).
The ethnographic museum in Piazza della Gambarina dedicated to the life and work of the past.
The relics and memories of Saint Ignatius.
The Tomb of the Biga and the colored Roman glass.
Galatina's art and memory in a former convent.
The facade with 250 coats of arms and the history of new cities.

In the former convent of the Clarisse di Santa Chiara, restored after the earthquake of 1997-98: on the ground floor the gallery around the courtyard, with works by Vittore Crivelli (Madonna with Child) and Simone De Magistris; on the upper floor the collections of weapons, avifauna and hammers and the collection of modern art by Mariano Gavasci.
The sea of the white city.
Complained €8 whole / €5 reduced. Free with BW Card and Card Culture
The Bujese medal school, unique in its kind.
A Roman bridge in the woods, on a road from 2,000 years ago.
A nineteenth-century theatre with a mobile audience.

The circular mast of the fortress, probably from the second half of the fifteenth century and attributed in a hypothetical way to Francesco di Giorgio Martini, on four levels: the guards on the ground floor, the prison on the second (up to the eighteenth century, with graffiti of the prisoners), residences on the high floors, where today the School Orchestra is located. The gardens, perhaps the work of Giacomo del Duca with Jacopo Barbone since 1579, are open every day 8-20; from the top of the tower you can see the lake and the Marmot area. The tower is visited by appointment with the City Culture Office.
In May there is the Strawberry Festival

Space in the ancient part of the village, open to the public free of charge, with household objects, agricultural and work equipment, traditional costumes and a stone mill collected by Rocco Derosa and Antonio Fanelli; it includes a restored country house and a documentation centre with texts and images of local and regional history.
A neoclassical and mysterious temple in the woods.

The oldest nucleus of the city, Romanesque with Gothic elements: façade in lunar white marble with bands of black marble of Colonnata with rosette, the wheel of the city's coat of arms and the motto "Fortitudo mea in rota"; bell tower of the fourteenth century 33 meters high, frescoes and sculptures of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries and pulpit in marble.

The art of potters is documented in Montottone already between 1200 and 1300; the emigration of the Sixties and Seventies drastically reduced the number and today only one workshop, that of the family Bozzi. The clay is handmade, the objects are modeled on the footwork and baked in a wood-burning oven with traditional paints.

Ancient capital of the Principality Ultra in the land of the Greek of Tufo: to see the castle with the Bourbon prison called  the "Spielberg" of Irpinia, today museum, the Oratory of St. James frescoed, Palazzo Giordano, the churches of St. John of Vaglio, St. Francis and St. Bartholomew and the Woods of Montefusco.
Understand the park between lake and mountain.

Country of the Asti Monferrato, already mentioned in a document of 948 and home of the writer and partisan Davide Lajolo ("Ulysses") who dedicates to him the multimedia museum "Vinchio" is my nest. Between Vinchio, Vaglio Serra and Incisa Scapaccino stretches the special nature reserve of Val Sarmassa, established in 1993, and the hills produce the Barbera d'Asti Nice and the precious Saracen asparagus.
An Arab-Norman temple in the countryside.

Dedicated to the painter and fresco artist Liberty Angelo Comolli, active in Milan between the eight and twentieth centuries: he exhibits the great preparatory cartoons to charcoal of sacred subject, found in the abbey after 1982, with sketches, paintings, furniture and photographs. Visit accompanied by about half an hour, by reservation or in the free openings scheduled.
The medieval streets and walkways of a UNESCO village.

Nineteenth-century civic tower, symbol of the village, built where in the Middle Ages was the municipal palace; it bears the coat of arms of the Municipality and the clock facing the square, with crenellated top that encloses the bell cell and details inspired by the Tower of Mangia di Siena. There are few remains of the medieval castle around which Cinigiano was born.
Four hundred medicinal plants on a hill.
A farmhouse at court and a ruined mill in the countryside.
The city of the majolica: the oldest ceramic museum in Italy in the former convent of San Francesco and the sanctuary of the Madonna dei Bagni covered with a former ceramic vote.

A square tower in Maggiana, 40 arms high, with ogival windows and slits overlooking the lake: according to tradition in 1158 the Mandelli family hosted Frederick Barbarossa, who from here would observe the naval battles between Milan and Como; a granite plaque with date 1158, found in 1828, was lost. Owned by the Amici di Maggiana Group from 1976, it houses an ethnographic museum with objects and images from the end of the nineteenth century to the middle of the twentieth century on the life and work of the hamlet.

About 5 km of sandy beaches with pine forests behind, several times Blue Flag; the white colour of the coast of Rosignano Solvay derives from the calcareous residues of baking soda processing and bathing is not allowed in all stretches.

Città degli Ernici sulli Monti Ernici, with polygonal walls, medieval alleys and seventeenth-century palaces: the Basilica of Santa Maria Salome with the Scala Santa and, in plain, the Cistercian abbey of Casamari.
The symbol of Portovenere.

Documented from 967 and collegiate since 1541, it rises on the remains of the Roman forum; rebuilt from 1741 in Baroque forms and decorated with stucco after 1857, it is called the church of the cherubs for its 108 angel heads. He preserves a cycle on the life of Our Lady and paintings by Nicola Peccheneda di Polla, including eight apostles of 1751.
Garnier City.
The cove that can only be reached by sea.
Two thousand years in a palace.

Municipality at the entrance of the Val d'Ega, above Bolzano: the castle of Cornedo, of the twelfth century, dominates the gorge; in Collepietra the museum of Tyrolean rural life and in San Valentino in Campo the only astronomical observatory of South Tyrol and the Planetarium.
The ambo of 1180.
A mountain canyon near the springs.
The twentieth century in a Venetian palace.
In the hamlet of Casona, a panoramic path between calanchi and oak woods.

Documented from 1324, but the current building is from the seventeenth century, with Baroque façade dated 1607; it preserves stuccoes of Ambrosio Piazza and a silver reliquary of St. Christopher of 1780.
The octagon frescoed.
A day with children, even with rain.
Bologna Welcome indicates it as currently not visitable

Oratory near the Passo di San Lucio, at 1,542 meters on the Swiss border, attested in the thirteenth century: Carlo Borromeo stopped there to pray almost a day in the visit of 1582, Federico Borromeo described it in 1606 and had painted the frescoes for centuries. Inside the frescoes of the saints Lorenzo, Lucio, Vincenzo and Antonio Abate, a God Father in almond attributed to the school of Giovan Battista Pozzo and a fifteenth-century wooden statue of the patron saint of the housewives; tradition wants him to keep the remains of Lucio di Cavargna. You can walk on a dirt road from the provincial road to the Val Rezzo; on August 16, a big party attracts visitors from Italy and Switzerland.
The church of relics, with the crypt.
The Medici fortress in red bricks designed by Buontalenti against pirates, today a public park for cultural events.

Two exhibition sites with the Lucanian finds (IV-III century BC) of necropolis, inhabited and sacred areas: the Antiquarium in Piazza del Popolo preserves monumental tombs, such as the 19 and 24 tombs of the Scala with vases with red figures and metal ornaments; the museum of Borgo Sant'Antonio funerary furnishings, gold jewels, bronze mirrors, terracotta statuettes and bronze sheets with inscriptions in Greek and Osco, in addition to the Roccagloriosa's tomb 9 gold ornaments. From 1 July to 15 September every day 10-13 and 17-20, with reservation required (349 2201533, 349 1111491, 347 6321268); in other periods guided tours of the Pro Loco by reservation for groups of at least 4.
Matisse, Chagall and Picasso in the art collection of a Pope.

An island of about 37 hectares on the Po between Ostiglia and Revere, with forests and golenal habitats, described as a rare example of hanging marsh; it is reached by boat or on foot when the river is dry.
A historic stop on Cassia.
Over a century of Alfa Romeo where the cars were built.
Napoleon's theater.

Built in the sixteenth century in twelve months by Judge Hans Fieger, of the family of bankers who had received the castle from Massimiliano: Renaissance forms with four round corner towers on a square base, erker and steep roof. It is a private residence and can only be seen from the outside.
In 2024 the Region approved permanent safety works of the sub-area Thapsos (D.D.G. 582/2024): verify access

Founded in 1870 in the fifteenth-century Palazzo Antignano of Catalan taste: the Matres Matutae, votive statues in tuff from the VII to the first century BC, vases from the Iron Age to the Attic Ceramics, terracotta, bronzes, coins, epigraphs, mosaics from Sant'Angelo in Formis and Nola, the federician room with the remains of the towers of Frederick II and the Bourbon, Liani and Savoy rooms.

The only remains of the ancient castle of Cuorgnè, probably built in the 11th century, according to some scholars on the foundations of a late Roman watchtower. It is built in river pebbles laid with fishbone; the popular name comes from a legend set around the year 1000, on a poor young man who returns rich and is welcomed by an old friend.
dirt and steep path, unprotected cliffs, wells hidden from vegetation and unstable terrain: hiking shoes, avoid rainy days

Built by the Normans in the 11th century at the end of the conquest of Calabria, it occupies the highest point of the hill; the polygonal tower on the east side probably owes to Frederick II. He passed to the Lancia, Monfort, Del Balzo and Marzano, then to the Aragonese and in 1494 to the Borgia, whose marble coat of arms is on the portal, for the marriage between Goffredo Borgia and Sancha d'Aragona; the earthquake of 1783 destroyed the village.
On the shores of the homonymous lake.
The games of the past painted on the walls.

Mountain village in the heart of the Sibillini Mountains and seat of the National Park, with walls, towers and Renaissance palaces around Piazza dei Martiri Vissani, seriously affected by the earthquake of 2016; in the surroundings the Renaissance sanctuary of Macereto.
An oasis for fauna in the plain.
The Sicilian cart and the nature of the island, free of charge, on the sea.

It was built between 1840 and 1848 under the guidance of Pietrantonio Schettini, as a graveyard that bypassed the Bourbon ban to bury in churches; it was used until 1910.
The small church next to the ancient shrine of Capo Colonna, the destination of the May pilgrimage with the icon of Our Lady brought from the cathedral.
Walk in the villa where Horace wrote many of his works.

Symbol of Vallecrosia, it is a circular fortification of the sixteenth century, of more than ten meters of diameter, built to spot the Turkish-barbarish pirates plundering the western Liguria; it is the oldest monument of the village after the church of San Rocco. You can see it from the waterfront.
Frescoes over a thousand years ago in a small church among the apple trees.
The mother church of the village, with its sundials.
Baths included in a complex of industrial archaeology, among sources of sulphur gas that the ancients called "Acque Sante" .

Neo-Gothic Palace built by Ignazio della Bella at the beginning of the twentieth century on the model of Palazzo Vecchio in Florence, with dove-tailed battlements and corner tower with double-fores; restored, houses events and cultural activities.

At the entrance of the Vermenagna Valley, Roccavione has a historic centre at the foot of the cliff of the Santo Sudario, inhabited since the Bronze Age, with the Confraternity of Santa Croce and votive chapels from the 16th to the 18th century; also worth seeing is the Ethnographic Museum Vecchio Mulino and two monumental sequoias.
The Calabrian greenhouses told in multimedia.
The church of Trastevere that houses the Ecstasy of Blessed Ludovica Albertoni by Gian Lorenzo Bernini.

Symbol of the city in the center of the main square: the current castle, of Catalan character of the early fourteenth century, incorporates an earlier Norman castle tower built on a Saracen tower; Count Giovanni Tommaso Moncada (1461-1501) surrounded it with a bastion with four corner towers. Damaged by the earthquake of 1693 and used for a long time as a prison, it was restored from the fifties of the twentieth century and destined for a museum. The museum, entitled to Luigi Bernabò Brea and Saro Franco, tells about 5,000 years of history on five floors, from the Neolithic (6500-3500 BC) to the Middle Ages: prehistoric materials of the Ethnea area, the capitals of lava stone and ceramics of the Sicilian town of Mendolito, the Greek city of Adranon, Roman finds, ethno-anthropological collections and the "Fondo Imbarrato" of ancient books from the 16th to the 19th century. Open Monday-Saturday 9-18, Sunday 9-13.
Rural archaeology towards the sea.
A rude guard on the Ionian coast.

The village preserves the Old Gate of the 13th century and a watchtower of the time when it was fortified against the Saracen threat from the sea; among the churches Santa Lucia, Santa Caterina with the Oratory of Sant'Anna, San Giovanni from the high bell tower and Sant'Antonio with the convent of the Capuchins.
The sacred river at home.

Didactic path of 4.4 km and 556 m of difference in altitude (between 1,515 and 2,062 m) that climbs from the gallery of Sant'Ignazio to the Cross of the Red Valley: it touches the gallery of San Giorgio, excavated shortly after 1528, the remains of the Jakober Stuben at the gallery of San Giacomo, where it was found mineral already in the fifteenth century, and the gallery of San Guglielmo, the "forziere" of the mine; the landscape is largely man's work, excavated also with gunpowder in the eighteenth century.
Villages on the sea from above.

On the ground floor of the Palazzo Comunale, more than one hundred works by the sculptor from 1947 to 1984 between sculptures, prints, engravings, coins and medals, including the Central Gate of the Cathedral of Orvieto and the Grande Bagnante n. 1, with the artist's private archive.
A Visconti fortress with frescoed rooms of the Medici di Marignano.

Walled village founded between the 12th and 13th centuries as a bulwark against Pavia, now a lively town in Val Tidone: the 14th century Collegiate Church with the Crucifix of Del Maino and the Spousalizio attributed to Bernardino Luini, the church of San Rocco and Villa Braghieri with the Ethnographic Museum.
Since 1844 it hosts shows and concerts in a neoclassical temple inspired by the Teatro alla Scala.

A small village on a hill about 500 metres, near the Valle d'Ansanto sung by Virgilio: thermal resort for the Terme di San Teodoro, known since the second half of the seventeenth century, is home to the botanist Giovanni Gussone and houses a museum collection of prehistoric, Sanniti and Roman finds.
Emerald water in the woods of Carnia.
The door of the village with the signs of drawbridges.
The largest pine forest in the Alps, a base of excursions and walks starting from Casteldelfino.
The network of nuraghi of bass Sulcis.

Palace built between 1700 and 1720 on a project by Giovanni Battista Contini, with the Hall of the Eneide on the noble floor; it houses the Museum of the Carriages, ancient art rooms inaugurated in 2014 and works of the Eight and twentieth century.
The treasures of the shrine in cave and Pani Loriga.
Exhibits the excavations of the district of Fiorano.
The forum of a Roman colony of 194 BC on the shore of Lake Patria.
The fortress of the lords of Vico.
Roman amphitheatre built in 32 AD in cross-linked work, well preserved, visitable by appointment, which in summer hosts shows and events; testimonies the ancient Interamna.

Built probably between 1340 and 1350 by Enrico and Federico Chiaramonte, it is named after the Counts of Modica who owned it from 1410 to 1812; it resisted also the assault of the corsair Barbarossa and in the nineteenth century passed to the Municipality. Rhomboidal plant with four alternating towers, two cylindrical and two square, double and Gothic triple windows in the courtyard and staircase in red marble of Monte Bonifato. It hosts the Regional Enoteca of Western Sicily, with tastings, and the Museum of Popular Traditions, which reconstructs rural interiors with tools, tools and costumes and documents the production of wine. It overlooks Piazza della Repubblica, one of the city's largest green spaces. Open Tuesday-Sunday 9:30-12:30 and 15:30-18:30, closed on Monday.
The parish church (prepositural) of Leffe, which houses the Sorrowful Madonna of the Fantoni.

15th century church with high bell tower and portal of the fifteenth century; on the façade an eighteenth-century fresco of Purgant Souls and Annunciation, probably linked to pestilences, when the building was used as a lazzaretto. Inside the fourteenth-century frescoes, among ex-vote, a Saint Christopher with the Child and a Martyrdom of Saint Andrew of the early sixteenth century.
Heirlooms and images of the front of the Karst next to the fallen.

Castle over the city built around 1250, ruined by a fire in 1671, rebuilt by Otto Piper since 1895 and completed by Karl Traut, who made it a meeting place of artists, musicians and writers until 1929.

It exhibits the materials of the excavations of Zuc Scjaramont, the Castelraimondo hill, telling the story in four phases: pre-Roman (the first fortified village), Roman, late medieval and medieval-Renaissance; among the finds coins and pre-Roman ceramics. Open Mon-Sat 9-12, Wednesday until 6pm, closed on Sundays.

Lake elongated in the shape of a fjord among wooded hills, Blue Flag for the quality of the waters and services, reachable on foot from the center: lido, meadows, rent of rowing boats or electric, canoe and kayak, and the flat

Just outside the village, next to the Capuchin monastery of the sixteenth century then suppressed. The main altar is a retablo inlaid, carved and painted, with nine tables of Neapolitan Mannerist school of the seventeenth century.
MiC card indicates the castle closed every day (tel. Common 0881 984007)
The system of urban escalators that connects the parts of the city "verticale" indicated by italia.it as the longest in Europe.
The best view from the bridge called Tre Ponti.
Walking on the medieval road between Emilia and Tuscany.
Protected area that includes the sandy coast, the dunes and the natural pine forest at the foot of the Torre del Cerrano, where the management consortium is located.
Private residence: the source describes the visit accompanied by the owner during an exit organized by Touring

Outdoor museum of twelve hectares of excavations in the locality Mid-August: the Roman colony founded at the end of the II century BC and inhabited until the XII century, with domus with mosaic floors and a large early medieval church.
The natural jewel of Cimini.

In 1524 the Pordenone frescoed the façade for 45 ducats (San Cristoforo, Adoration of the Magi, Madonna enthroned with the Savorgnan coat of arms, Ecce Homo): damaged by the earthquake, the frescoes were detached and brought inside, while outside they remain copies drawn. Inside also an Escape in Egypt, perhaps in 1524, and the Nativity of 1527, in excellent condition after the restoration.
It preserves a wooden crucifix of the fourteenth century, a Byzantine fresco of the fourteenth century and an eighteenth-century wooden statue of the saint.
The unique museum at the outlet of via Umberto I on Prato della Valle, which exhibits magic lanterns and precursor tools of cinema.
The Crucifix of the Good Friday Rite.
Visit in the company of a guide (Trentino Grande Guerra); the page does not include updated opening periods
The square overlooks the Basilica of Santi Siro and Materno, symbol of the city, with the bell tower of the early fifteenth century, and the monument to Pope Pius XI, born in Desio.
The backstage of an opera house.
Waterfall along the Via dei Masi della Val d'Ultimo, a few minutes walk from the millenarian larch trees; recommended especially from May.

The church is part of a harmonious set of buildings and is marked by a tall and slender bell tower in the Ionic style; next to it is the Angolo Paglialunga, a characteristic glimpse dedicated to the master of wrought iron Ettore Paglialunga.
To see a Titian in a small village in Mantovano.
The village of the infernot in the heart of the Monferrato degli Infernot UNESCO, among the most beautiful villages in Italy and the Orange Flag, built of stone from cantons.
Museum dedicated to the motorism of the city.
The Marian shrine of former vows.
In the belly of the mountain by train.
From 21 September 2026 to 28 March 2027 the acropolis closes before the site (until 1 January at 16:00, then gradually later); after that time you visit only the lower city.
Imperial thermal baths become fortress.

The greatest and best known of the Majella hermitages: in 1053 the monk Desiderio, then Pope Victor III, who built a small church there; Pietro da Morrone found it destroyed in 1246 and started the restoration by adding an oratory and a cell. Today it includes church, sacristy, guesthouse and monastic complex, with wooden choir, paintings of the Madonna and the Descent of the Holy Spirit; under the church the cave of the first hermits, the room of the Crucifix and the cell where Celestine V prayed, and the Santa Scala rises to the oratory of the Maddalena, overlooking the valley. A community of young friars lives there; from August 29th to the first Sunday of October every Sunday forgiveness is celebrated with plenary indulgence.

In the municipal territory there are about one hundred Apulian farms built between the fifteenth and nineteenth centuries, different in size, style and use, some fortified against pirate raids. Many have been restored and welcome guests for food and wine tourism and wellness, others remain agricultural centers; Masseria Lupoli has a museum of peasant civilization. In December 2015, the European Commission (EDEN project) recognised the area         . Cento Masserie . European destination of excellence; among the oil products, Negroamaro and Primitivo wine and yellow-red tomato, Slow Food garrison.
The parish church overlooking Piazza Pepe.

Discovered by chance on September 30, 1994 by a school girl, are the first footprints of the theropod dinosaur found in the Park, imprinted in the Dolomia Principale del Triassico, more than 200 million years ago, on a rock of the Ciol de Ciasavent stream; the route is marked with signs and panels. It is the most visited site in the country.
The 14th-century Gothic of Lodi.
Green in the city.
The king's crystals.
Small church on the sea with crypt, overlooking the rocks, point for sunset.
Roman wall structures emerged in 1995 during work in a house in the village.
In 1177, commissioned by Ruggero d'Aquila and belonged to the Order of Malta, it was the first large building built outside the walls and one of the richest Commendes in Sicily.

It rises on a hill in the center of the village; documented since 1186, when they built it Siclerio dell'Andito (Landi) and Savino Vicedomino, it was infeudated to the Visconti in 1405, transformed into a residential palace by the Landi in the eighteenth century and passed to the Sforza Fogliani in the nineteenth century.

Ancient merchant village of the Upper Canavese on the Orco: the medieval nucleus winds along the portico via Arduino, with the Gothic house called King Arduino and the two towers of discord, the roundabout and the square; in the former Manifattura of via Ivrea are located the Archaeological Museum of the Upper Canavese and the art museum dedicated to caricaturist Carlin Bergoglio.

The "Monte delle Boche" (mountain of boats), almost 900 metres away, is the "Vetta delle Langhe" (vegetable of the Langhe): almost vertical village of stairs and sternìe, of which there remains an arch of the ancient walls of the fourteenth century, with views of the Langhe and the Ligurian Sea. Outside the center the chapel of San Rocco with the 'Cavalcata dei Vizi' and, in the hamlet Lunetta, the medieval bridge near the Reserve Belbo.

At 1,718 m, the northernmost hamlet of Piedmont and the oldest Walser settlement, on the border with the Goms, the land of origin of the Walser: stone and wood huts, the Ski Museum open for the centenary of the Formazza Ski Club and, on a hill, the nineteenth-century oratory of Sant'Anna, erected in memory of the church of Morasco submerged by the lake, with a sign that recalls the snow of 1951.

More than 20 km of white beach under the dunes covered with vegetation and Mediterranean maquis, with long stretches of free beach reached by wooden walkways; Sabaudia has obtained the Blue Flag several times. The dunes appear in Alberto Sordi's film "Amore mio assistimi" (1969) with Monica Vitti.
The 1884 station preserves the room used by Umberto I and Margherita di Savoia in the summer stays at the Villa Reale.
It preserves paintings attributed to the Bresciano and the Lucan Gian Lorenzo Cardone and a wooden statue of the saint.
The square with the fountain inside the walls.
A neo-Gothic garden with the old stone icebox.

The settlement of Santu Teru (Teodoro), about 2 km from the village at the confluence of two streams, was founded at the end of the 6th century BC as a Carthaginian outpost and developed as an agricultural center between the 5th and the 3rd century BC, when it was abandoned: the acropolis, a walls, houses outside the walls and perhaps fusion workshops remain. On the slopes of Monte Luna, a few tens of meters, more than 120 tombs have been identified, mostly a well with side rooms, but also a pit, a chest, loculus and enchytrismos for children, with votive trays and niches with traces of geometric paintings in red ochre. In Roman times Monte Luna became the most important center of the area.
The material culture of the mountain.
Cala can only be reached on foot with the guides in summer, with the Grand Ducal customs of the late eighteenth century behind.

The Oratory of the Assumption was born from the will of Antoniotto Ghiringhelli on March 18, 1488 and was consecrated by Carlo Borromeo on June 27, 1574; abandoned by the patrons and reduced to woodshed, returned to the parish around 1900 and was restored on several occasions, from the years of Guido Cagnola mayor until the works completed in 1996 and the final restoration started in 2006. It preserves a cycle of frescoes from the fifteenth century attributed to Galdino da Varese and his school.
The Lucani of the Basento under the painted ceilings of the dukes.
On Caravaggio's trail.

Borgo dell'Alto Ionio Cosentino was born in the 10th century, with a medieval centre surrounded by walls and panoramic views; on the sea the Castello Federiciano, symbol of the village, and along the coast the remains of the tower of Capo Spulico, with the Blue Flag promenade.
The large water mirror of the average Val di Sangro.
One of the oldest churches in Fermano.
A millenarian church with works by Cambiaso and Margliano.
The passo-santuario heart of the valley, on the border with Switzerland.
The sanctuary wanted by the saint in his country.
Private villa, in the past venue of exhibitions: check if it is visitable inside

Sabina town on the valley of the Tiber, with the historic center of Palazzo Vannicelli and the Bishop's Palace, the cathedral of San Liberatore, the Romanesque San Pietro and the Civic Archaeological Museum in Palazzo Gori; the hamlet of Foglia, on a cliff on the left bank of the Tiber, is among the most beautiful villages of Italy.
the source warns that the path is subject to falling boulders

Also known as San Michele Arcangelo or Sant'Angelo del Mirteto, it is a karst cave transformed into a church in 1183, in an uninhabited area on the slope that looks at Ninfa; it inspired the abbey of Santa Maria di Monte Mirteto founded by Gregorio IX. On the rock are still frescoes, including a Madonna enthroned between St. Michael and St. Lucia, and a primitive altar; it is curated by volunteers of the association "Opera di Sant'Angelo" in Monte Mirteto.
The street of the artisan workshops of the nativity scenes, with the church of San Gregorio Armeno.
A remarkable example of theatrical architecture of the eighteenth century.

Water sawmills that document the passage from the force of two or three men to the hydraulic force, with only one sufficient worker; the working sawmill is visited with guides organized by the Park. The Bègoi road is on the forest road from Plan to the Ragaiolo bridge.
The Great War in the Dolomites at 2,239 meters.
A torrent that crosses narrow gorges and wide clearings, with a rich variety of flora and fauna.

Nodo viario romano in the locality of Sant'Eleuterio, where the Via Aemilia, Via Traiana (109 A.D.) and the Herculia passed: first century A.D. baths with black and white mosaics, rooms of the second century, a large room with polychrome mosaic and medieval blocks around a courtyard with well; an earthquake damaged it in 346 A.D.

Housed in the Medici Loggia (1472-75), which dominates Piazza Garibaldi, ancient market square, and still bears the Medici coat of arms on a column, documents the history of Altopascio. It exhibits mainly Renaissance ceramics and stone fragments of medieval buildings from the excavations of the eighties and nineties, from the large fifteenth-century orcs for wheat to daily dishes; born in the municipal library, it is an exhibition ordered since 1990 and documentation center since 1991.
The blades of the Italian Toledo, forged before you.
A ghost village with its legend.

The town of Capo di Leuca was born from the union of Presicce and Acquarica del Capo: in Presicce a Doge's Palace on Piazza del Popolo, the late Baroque church of Sant'Andrea, noble palaces from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century and an underground network of 23 oil mills; in Acquarica the remains of the medieval castle and the Masseria di Celsorizzo with the Norman tower.

Small village of the Val Maira at 1,637 meters, reachable from Stroppo or from the hill of Sampeyre: in the village Serre the parish church of Santa Maria Assunta keeps the frescoes of 1493 by Hans Clemer, the "Maestro d'Elva" and the Casa della Meridiana hosts the museum of the guinea pigs, the hair collectors; just above, the Fremo Cuncunà dominates the valley.
The towers of a strong house in the Brescia countryside.

Itinerary in the places that inspired Grazia Deledda, Nobel Prize winner, the novel "Canne al vento" , set at . The museum Sa Domo 'e sos Marras organizes excursions in the park in May (ticket €3, reduced €2.50).

A single nave church with portal of 1677 in serene stone; a Latin plaque recalls the ancient church of Santa Maria della Rocca of 1189. Country of the Alexandrian plain near the Scrivia, dominated by the castle born as a fortress around the 11th century and now seat of the Town Hall, with fifteenth-century frescoes by the Boxilio brothers.

Just outside the village, on a rocky spur above the valley of the Carrucana river, probably dates back to the first quarter of the 14th century and is indicated as the most significant example of Italian Gothic in Sardinia before the spread of the Catalan style. It has a basilica plan with three naves with cruising vaults and arches with acute sixth, quadrangular apse on the edge of the rock, facade with portal and rosette with bichrome cones of black trachite and light limestone and bell tower partly rebuilt in the sixteenth century. It was deconsecrated in 1920 due to the risk of collapse; since 1988 works of stabilization of the church and the rock have been underway.

The first nucleus dates back to about 1100; the mother house of the counts of Tyrol, which gave the name to the region, passed to the Habsburgs in 1363 and fell from the fifteenth century, when the government moved to Innsbruck; plundered and put to auction by the Bavarian occupants around 1800, it was bought by Merano and donated to the emperor Francesco I, then restored. It contains Romanesque sculptures, marble portals, protogothic frescoes, a copy of the Gothic altar (the original is in Innsbruck) and the oldest Tyrolean windows; it houses the provincial museum of history and culture, with the permanent exhibition in a renewed wing. You can only reach it on foot, 25-30 minutes from the village; closed on Mondays; not suitable for wheelchairs.

Large erratic rock near Cascina Tavolara (about 7.2 x 3.25 m, 1.25 m tall) with a rectangular cavity similar to a tomb on top and, along the edges, seven round cups and two rectangular ones. Archaeological museum opened in 1995 and re-arranged in 2023 with the support of the Cariparo Foundation, in a brick building next to the church of San Basilio. The chronological route tells of St. Basil as a center of exchanges from the Etruscan to the Roman age up to the early Middle Ages: the oldest finds are ceramics of a settlement of the VI-V century BC, sign of contacts between Paleovenets, Greeks and Etruscans; the main collection comes from the excavations of a nearby Roman villa, documented up to the fifth century A.D. (architectonic elements, skylights, pottery, blown glass, needles and pins in bone or horn), with a numismatic section dedicated to a treasure of coins. Multimedia supports and a covered courtyard for temporary exhibitions; collaborates with the Regional Park of the Po Delta.

On the plateau of the Colle dell'Orso, the beech forests of Monte Marchetta and Colle dell'Orso grow over 1,000 meters in a difficult mountain climate; here you will find the beech tree "Pedalone" over 40 meters high and over 100 years old. 167 meters high, born as a synagogue and symbol of the city, hosts the National Cinema Museum from its origins to today; the dome can be reached on foot or with the panoramic elevator.

In a valley of the Iglesiente dominated by Mount Conca s'Omu, about 10 km from the village: sacred place already in the Nuragic age, with a necropolis with wells and a bronze of male deity, then punic sanctuary of Sid Addir (V century BC, renovated at the end IV) and finally Roman temple of Augustian age dedicated to the Sardus Pater Babai, restored under Caracalla in 213-217 A.D. as the epigraph of the pediment recalls. The pronao has ionic columns about eight meters high; the cell, eleven meters deep, preserves traces of white mosaic and the dyton two tanks for purification rites. Rediscovered by La Marmora in 1836 and restored in 1967; about 20 minutes walk to the Roman quarry and an ancient path to Su Mannau.

Borgo refounded in 1633 by Prince Alessandro Pignone del Carretto, the only Italian town to bear the name and surname of the founder. The complex combines a military fortress with a seventeenth-century residence, in a park of plane trees and lindens of 25,000 m2. According to popular tradition an underground passage connected the tower to the castle of Soncino, but attempts to explore it failed and the entrance was walled.

The center can be walked with a series of churches and military and civil buildings, shops and restaurants; the main monuments have panels in Italian, English and Greek, with a poem in Greek to listen to.

The portal with girals and animals recalls the Master Acuto (XII century); the interior with three naves with raised transept has a plant similar to San Clemente to Casauria, triabsidata crypt and altar on four columns with capitals of the X century. The Gemelli Palaces, two square buildings with double-lighted loggias and tower, were originally three brand buildings built between the sixteenth and seventeenth century by the Fieschi along the mule track for Vobbia; after the fire of one in the eighteenth century the two remaining were residence of the podestà, and today one houses town hall and library, the other private houses. The parish church of Santa Croce was built in 1578 and resumed in 1686.

Abbey founded in the 12th century to the north-east of the village, then one of the most important of the Reggiano territory; it remains a small church obtained from the right aisle of the original building, inserted in a rural courtyard.

Mountain town at the Chienti springs, on the Colfiorito plateau on the border with Umbria: small churches scattered among the pastures, the Botte dei Varano and a museum of fossils of the Pleistocene.
Stone core of the thirteenth century, portico and portal in marble of the seventeenth century; interior with three naves with ancient frescoes.
History and painting of the village in a single museum.
A 17th century church in the center.

The capital of Marsica overlooking the Fucino plain, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1915: the Orsini-Colonna castle with the Pinacoteca d'arte moderna, the cathedral of the Marsi, the Hague of museums on the draining of the lake and the Roman tunnels wanted by the emperor Claudio.
A Gothic portal in the heart of the village.

Bridge of 1792 in stone of Furlo covered with bricks, with a single round arch; destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt in 1947. The reflection in the Metauro draws a very photographed oval and is the starting point for canoeing and kayaking towards the Giant Marmittes.

Rebuilt in the upper part of the village, it has three naves and houses a marble altarpiece of the 16th century Deposition of Christ, brought back to the school of Michelangelo and defined an authentic masterpiece of which Calabria is proud.
On both sides of the fishing port: the long pebble beach of Saxony, with a large promenade, south-east of the railway, and the shorter beach of the Lido to the north-west.
Sunny terrace 1200 metres above Aosta, the birthplace of Abbot Cerlogne, father of the poetry in patois.
not open to the public: only guided tours and special openings upon reservation
The ancient reclamation plant, which was abandoned in 1986, houses the herbarium of the territory and a documentation centre accessible to people with motor and visual disabilities.
Borgo della Val di Merse known for the homeless abbey of San Galgano.
The knight with the silver horse.

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Brancaleoni in Piazza del Duomo (formerly MUSAF, renamed in 2024; until 2001 it was at the abbey of Farfa) exhibits artifacts from prehistory to the Roman age: the materials of the ancient Cures, the Sabino Cippo of Cures of the second half of the third century BC, the furnishings of the necropolis of Eretum with the Chariot of the Prince of the Tomb XI, stolen and returned in 2024 by the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek of Copenhagen, and in the Throne Hall the terracotta throne of the XXXVI tomb of Colle del Forno.

In the historic centre stands the Palazzo Beato Jacopo da Varazze, already seat of the civic administration, with the statue of the Blessed on the internal facade; near the Oratory of San Bartolomeo it houses a processional case of the school of Margliano. The medieval ramparts and the ruins of the Romanesque church of Sant'Ambrogio remain.
The civic bell tower.

Built at the end of the fourteenth century, probably for the Jacobucci family, as oratory for strangers and pilgrims, and national monument since 1926. It has an ogival portal and walls almost entirely covered by late-Gothic frescoes of the first decade of the fifteenth century, in two cycles: the first tells the history and miracles of St. Biagio, bishop and martyr.
Borgo della Valdera, open-air museum of contemporary art between the village and the hamlets.
The mountain culture of the upper valley in 500 objects.
15th-century building along State 16, what remains of an ancient mail station for changing horses on the coastal road.
The painter of the Madonnas in his country.
The oldest and most important of the city, born together with the village, with an interesting Romanesque façade.

The municipality of the Silano plateau, in the Sila National Park, which includes Camigliatello Silano. On the shores of Lake Cecita the Cupone Visitor Centre combines geological garden, botanical garden and paths; at the Torre dei Camigliati the Museum of Emigration La Nave della Sila; in the reserve of Fallistro the secular larch pine trees of the Giants of Sila, well of FAI.
The old town hall on the square.

Established in 2004 in the Palazzo San Domenico, a former Dominican convent of the end of the sixteenth century with the church of Santa Maria del Rosario, it preserves hundreds of whistles made by Italian artists for the National Competition linked to the whistle fair in January, for the feast of Saint Anthony Abate. Visit only by reservation (Pro Loco).
Built between 1741 and 1743 with an octagonal plan, it is accessed by an elegant double staircase; inside the frescoes by Giuseppe Trisca of 1744.

The village was born in 1337 by the will of Judge Mariano IV of Arborea, who sent a colony of 24 families at the foot of the castle; next to the new part it preserves a medieval nucleus near the fortress, with narrow streets and double sloping roofs.

C-shaped building with back courtyard and Venetian loggia of 1610; inside the Salone del Consiglio Maggiore and the Salone del Consiglio dei Ten, decorated with stuccoes and medallions of the Doges, and on the staircase the original fountain of Hercules and Hydra.
The history of community.
Ancient monastery outside the village, of medieval origin, founded by Benedictine monks.
For those who follow the art of today.
MiC card indicates the museum closed every day (tel. 0881 964064)

Well-preserved medieval complex, surrounded by the Duomo and public buildings: the Palazzo del Popolo (1214-1228), among the oldest civic buildings in Italy, the Palazzo del Capitano of the late thirteenth century and the Gothic Palazzo dei Priori (1334-1347) with the square tower.

Country of the Vermenagna Valley known as the village of Pinocchio for the more than 150 murals taken from the illustrations of Attilio Mussino, who lived here the last years; above the village the ruins of the castle of Tourousela and, in the surroundings, the reserve of Palanfré in the Park of the Maritime Alps.
The Gothic in the oven.

The most important monument of the village, of the XII century and of Norman origin: Romanesque capitals, a wooden throne carved with the coat of arms of the Archimandrita and late medieval mural paintings, including a San Giovanni Chrysostomo. Mummification of the dead was practiced in underground rooms.

Small town on the border between the provinces of Bergamo, Brescia and Cremona, along the Oglio, linked from 1070 to the Counts Barbò; the symbol is the complex of the Tower of Tristan (XV century) and Pallavicino, immersed in a park of plane trees and lime trees of 25,000 m2; in the hamlet Santa Maria stands the sixteenth-century church of Santa Maria Assunta.

The first traces of the castrum date back to about 1115, with the Estensi, which enlarged it with curtains and residences; destroyed by Ezzelino III by Romano in 1249 and the Paduans in 1294, was rebuilt by Ubertino da Carrara from 1339 and remained at the Carraresi until the beginning of the fifteenth century. Today there are large towers and a wall of more than a kilometer, with the Rocca del Soccorso in the north-east, ancient entrance of the fortress, and in the mast the remains of a small church; around 1570 the Mocenigo built on the south side their palace, today home of the museum. Property of the Municipality since 1887, contains public gardens open in 1915, with trees and centuries-old plants; open every day 9-17.30.
The oldest Romanesque ruins on the island, in the middle of the countryside.
Roman mosaics and a Byzantine icon.

Exhibition on the Cold War (1949-1989), indicated as unique in Europe on the theme, in the former missile base of Passo Coe: missiles pointed to the sky, a hangar with a Nike-Hercules missile with inspection windows, electronic wagons, radar and an underground bunker. The guided tour of about one hour ends in the control room with the simulation of the launch sequence.
One of the most famous Romanesque crypts in the Marche region.
The Baroque masterpiece of Capodieci, with a canvas by Giuseppe Bonito.

Church of 1514, place of devotion for the inhabitants of Mezzano, on the meadows above the village about an hour walk from the center, with views of the Vette Feltrine and the Cimonega group. We arrive the easy walk Cordognè-San Giovanni, which departs from Poit (about 10 minutes by car) and is indicated especially during the foliage.

Impressive Austro-Hungarian construction of 1898, already obsolete at the outbreak of the Great War and therefore used only as a deposit; it is seen from the outside, next to the exhibition of Someda.
Pineta just outside the walls with lush vegetation and areas for camping, refreshment and relaxation, where the ornithological museum is located.
It tells the history and production of the Fontina DOP; the visit includes the ripening warehouses carved into the rock, one inside the ancient copper mine.
The museum of the car manufacturer, with Miura, Countach and the latest models.
Recommended
The view of the Madonie.
On foot or by bike along the big river.

Since 1999 in the sixteenth century Palazzo Vassalli, a long residence of the homonymous family and purchased by the Municipality in the sixties: rooms of archaeological finds of the territory (steles, cippi, vases, statues) and medieval, and in the underground cellar an ethnographic section on the peasant and artisan civilization of Accadia and Capitanata, with tools of carpenter, blacksmith and shoemaker. Guided visits, tel. 0881 981012.
A small Santa Casa di Loreto in the plain.
The fountain of the village, with its legend.

Posidonia meadows up to about 40 meters with over 350 species of invertebrates and fish, caves with octopus and moray eels and Roman wrecks: one in Cala Rossano in very low water, one in Punta dell'Arco and five over 100 meters between the two islands.
A sixteenth-century palace linked to the Gonzaga.

Large rustic villa discovered in 1987 and excavated between 1988 and 2000 on about 1,675 m2 of an estimated complex over 3,700 m2: medium-republic production nucleus for wine and then oil (torks, tanks, large dolia) and residential part of Augustia facing the sea, with mosaics and fragments of painting, in use until the 6th century AD. A 3D rendering of five environments was presented in 2023.
The frescoed buildings.
Neo-Gothic church annexed to the Latin Villino, in Piazza della Podesteria.

In the cemetery of Cavagliano, a single nave with semicircular apse decorated outside with terracotta tiles; inside frescoes of the Gaudenzian school of the second half of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, with the Virgin among the Apostles and a copy of that of Gaudenzio Ferrari in Varallo. Not indicated hours: information to the parish (0321 98027).

Built in 1220 on the ground of the bishopric of Lucca, before the castle, and entrusted to the regular Canons of Sant'Agostino. Rectangular plant with exposed trusses, porch and apse, central altar with eighteenth-century ciborium in white marble and two lateral altars in stone of the seventeenth century; today it is votive chapel of the fallen of the First World War.
It keeps the polyptych of the Canavesio.

The main Marian shrine of Florence, founded in 1250 by the Seven Saints Founders of the Servants of Mary, with the venerable Annunciation of the fourteenth century in Michelozzo's temple and the frescoes of Andrea del Sarto, Pontormo and Rosso Fiorentino in the cloister of the Voti.

Ten sections on the economy of the territory: the peasant house with the kitchen, the tools of the shoemaker, the blacksmith and the shepherd, the domestic utensils and the relationship between man and environment.
