The center, rebuilt after the Great War, is small and turns on foot through narrow streets and colorful buildings; the heart is Corso IV Novembre, the shopping street. From the center you can walk to Lake Lumera.
Wanted by Napoleon, reopened after a long restoration, is the main seat of the Festival Elba Isola Musicale of Europe.
Signs of war on the former border.

In the hamlet of Viepri the Abbey of San Faustino, built by the Benedictines in the 8th century on the remains of a Roman villa and on the tomb of the saint; the abbey of Santa Maria in Viepri of 1150, Romanesque with double sloping façade; Santa Maria delle Grazie of the late fifteenth century and the remains of a castle of 1380 with the church of San Giovanni.

A few steps from the Villa Comunale and near Palazzo Corvaja, one of the major Roman monuments of Sicily: a long brick wall with 18 large apse niches alternated with as many small niches; the name recalls the simulated naval battles.

Renaissance brick palace built between 1486 and 1498 on a project by Francesco di Giorgio Martini, with decorations by Michele di Giovanni da Milano and his son Alvise; the tower, designed by Andrea Sansovino, collapsed with the earthquake of 1657. It houses the Planetian Library, founded in 1859, with about 110,000 volumes, manuscripts and incunabula, including an autograph letter by Giacomo Leopardi from 1825; guided tours to the Antique Funds Rooms on Thursday at 11 am and at 12 noon.
Natural terrace just beyond the houses, reachable on foot in a few minutes leaving the car out of the center: view of the valley and the Sibillini Mountains and, on clear days, on the Adriatic.

Alto Vicentino plateau between 900 and 1,700 meters, dominated by Monte Spitz and Monte Cimone, the theatre in 1916 of one of the most famous mine wars on the front: today you can visit the shrine on the crater, the trenches recovered from the Ecomuseum of the Great War, the Austro-Hungarian cemetery and the Visitor Center in the village.
The lawyer's tower and a 17th century fresco.
XV century church that preserves a table by Niccolò Alunno with the Assumption of the Virgin surrounded by angels.

A small museum set up by the Association of Seniors. Pasanisi is located in the former church of Our Lady of Graces (1634), which has been restored and also houses a cultural centre: it exhibits ancient liturgical objects, devotional medals and artistic prints. Access with stairs. Tel. +39 329 437 8774.

Palace where Giovanni Verga lived, remembered by a plaque (in this house he lived with the creatures of his high imagination Giovanni Verga) the building is presumably between the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The upper floors are incomplete for an argument with the nearby Cannizzaro, documented in the municipal historical archive.
The tour of the ramparts on foot, starting from the western gate.
The Lucretile Territory Museum when it reopens.

Valle delle Alpi Lepontine between 300 and 2,000 meters above Menaggio, of which the Rogolone is the symbol. Along the Sanagra torrent you will meet the Mill of the Valley, the Carliseppi Mill with the donkey-back bridge, the Old Chioderia, the Fornace Galli where bricks and tiles were produced and the monolith of the Sass Corbée. The main ring from Menaggio to Loveno, Piamuro and Barna measures about 10 km (about 3 and a half hours, medium difficulty).
Church of the XIII-XIV century, reached by steep stairs that border it.

Along the ancient Via Amerina, north of the village, stands the Torricella, tower probably part of a sighting system; not far away remain the side parapets of the Bridge of Valle Gaudenzio, Etruscan bridge to a single arcade of the second century. Vasanello is the stop of the Via Amerina Way, 60 km recognized by the Lazio Roads Network.
Domus de janas a stone's throw from the village.

In a palace in the historical center renovated in the eighties, it collects the works that the Turinese artist Franco Assetto (1911-1993) donated to the Municipality, in chronological order: from surrealism to pop art to water sculptures; among the works Il Divino Bambino (1952) and Sculpture d'acqua (1971).
The shrine of the waters.
The business stone.

It is located in the birthplace of Amilcare Ponchielli, the famous composer to whom the town owes its name, transformed into a museum dedicated to him. You can see his pianos, sheet music cases and other original objects.
In the historic center of Frossasco, offers to know and discover the typical products and excellences of the territory.
Church of 1661, restored, which holds ex vows of sailors and fishermen.

Rock site around the country, along the European Path E1. At Case Vecchie there are tombs of the Bronze Age and a medieval rock settlement known for Jewish and early Christian frescoes and symbols; in the Jewish hypogeum the Aditus group in Rupe has identified engravings of menorah, documented with a 3D model.

Born to preserve and study the testimonies of rural life that has marked the history of the country, collects tools and tools of agricultural and handicraft work and testimonies of life in the farmhouse in the first decades of the twentieth century.
Petrarca's house.

Waterfall of about 14 meters falling into a tank of about 30 meters of diameter, shaped by erosion in the serpentinites. The path starts from the bridge of Sant'Anna in the square and goes up the Mass for the villages of Fucinassa and Gambabosco: about 50 minutes and 150 meters of difference in altitude.
Gorges and pots of giants in Matese.
The miraculous spring.
Two hamlets that preserve the medieval structure and offer a wide panorama, from Val di Cecina to the coast.
Middle Ages outside, baroque inside.
One of the collections of the Cittadella dei Musei, dedicated to Siamese art, next to the Archaeological Museum and the Pinacoteca.

Città della Riviera di Ponente in four parts, Finalmarina, Finalpia, Varigotti and the walled village of Finalborgo, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with the complex of Santa Caterina, the basilica of San Biagio and the Spanish forts.
The birthplace of the saint.

The company museum in a building of the late eighteenth century where Paul Alessio's tools were produced since 26 November 1819, taken over in 1955 by Silmax; restored since 1990, it exhibits on three floors lathes, cutters, sharpeners and vintage tools that reconstruct the 19th century working environment and the history of mechanics in the Lanzo Valleys. Times to check.
The oldest after the cathedral, with Baroque façade and works by Macrino d'Alba and Gandolfino da Roreto.
On a hill behind Lacona, it was founded by disciples of St. John Gualberto linked to the Abbey of Vallombrosa; the current building dates back to the sixteenth century.

Small ancient chapel in the center of the village, enlarged and partly rebuilt in the sixteenth century (1593), with bell tower probably seventeenth century; it was temporary parish during the construction of the new church and was deconsecrated after 1930. In 1971, during the transformation into a gym, there were paintings on the left wall of the second half of the fourteenth century with Christ before Pilate and Herod and other scenes of the Passion; the façade was restored in 1996.
In the village there are artisan workshops that produce hand-knotted carpets and lace embroidery.

Benedictine monastery that tradition links to an apparition of Our Lady of May 10, 715; the three-nave church and the square cloister are of the fourteenth century, the bell tower of the fifteenth. The first fourteenth-century Santa Porta is attributed to Raimondo di Poggio, school of Atri; frescoes from 1499 with the foundation and an Annunciation, stories of the Virgin in the refectory (1597) and lunettes of the cloister of Sebastiano Majewski (XVII century).
Vivarini and Moroni in the same village church.

A natural triangular swimming pool closed by the rocks, linked to the legend of Joan II d'Angiò, next to the remains of the Roman villa of Pollio Felice (1st century A.D.) on the cliff of Capo di Sorrento: six rooms turned with traces of stuccoes, a porch with marble columns, covered passages, stairs and terraces towards the sea, with views of Vesuvio, Ischia, Punta Campanella and Capri. About 30 minutes walk from the center, free access from the path; better at sunrise or sunset in high season.
Polar explorations and birds, good with the boys.
A small sanctuary under the porch.

The Marian church was built on an ancient pagan temple, linked to the legend of an apparition of the end of the sixth century and visited, according to tradition, by Popes, Frederick II and St. Francis in 1222. The name comes from the snowfall that in the spring of 1492 blocked for more than forty days Charles VIII and his soldiers; there is venerated an icon of Byzantine style of Our Lady with Child. Free and free access, reachable by wheelchair.
Ecomuseum dedicated to local culture, with historical buildings and sites of the mill, wash-house and museum of the park.
The culture of the Provençal valleys of Cuneo.

Founded between the 12th and 13th centuries and linked to a pceptory of the Knights of Malta, it preserves the arched apse and frescoes of the 14th century with angels, the archangel Michael and the Crucifixion.
On the roof of the Alps.
The museum dedicated to the peasant world of the Sienese countryside as it was until the seventies of the twentieth century.

Limonaia of the beginning of the eighteenth century on 1,633 m2 of terraces (còle) on the sides of the central casèl, with pillars and white walls exposed to the sun; purchased by the Municipality in 1995, restored and open to the public on 22 July 2004, with lemons, cedars, grapefruits, mandarins, chinotti, kumquats and other citrus fruits, didactic route and lake view. It is reached on foot from the center following the ceramic tiles; open from March to October.
Exhibitions in Via Nazionale.

Stone houses with vines bred above the doors, the "vignali" (wineyards), tradition that would date back about 400 years ago; to see the area of Casamicciola and Vico Spezzato. On the arch keys of the portals are carved apotropaic masks against the evil eye, grouped in four periods, from animal and mythical faces to serene human faces. At the entrance of the ancient village, in front of the Mother Church, the civic clock, built between 1876 and 1878 on a project by Vincenzo Ventrella.

It dominates the village of Sarezzo and the middle Valle Trompia; according to an ancient plaque the church dates back to the 13th century and the restorations have emerged the foundations of a Romanesque apse. The 18th century wooden main altar houses the statues of the Saints Emiliano and Tirso and of the Madonna del Sodalto, and the altarpiece of Giovan Battista Botti (1746) depicts the Saints Barnaba, Vincenzo Ferreri and Fermo in veneration of the Virgin. It is reached by four paths from Sarezzo, Lumezzane, Marcheno and Gardone Val Trompia, or by car from Zanano up to about 500 m from the sanctuary.

The most important sixteenth-century building in Massafra, consecrated on 11 February 1582 and renovated in the eighteenth century; the façade, with rose window and Renaissance portal surmounted by the angel called "Sant'Misiriedd" has a defensive battlements that recall the nearby castle. Inside, the main altar is framed by the Baroque wooden machine of 1783 and the Cappellone del Sacramento (1566) preserves intact the temples of the vault; under the apse, visible through a glass plate, a rock church discovered in the restorations of 1996.
The Roman countryside still visible.

Romanesque church of the 11th century dedicated to Santa Maria Assunta, outside the village, which preserves traces of ancient frescoes and a fifteenth-century Gothic sculpture of the Madonna della Misericordia; it is the final destination of the first Mantua stage of the Via Carolingia da Castiglione delle Stiviere.

In the hamlet of Toscolano, next to the castle, the church of the Santissima Annunziata with a single nave has on the base wall a newsstand (the Majesty of Toscolano) with frescoes attributed to Pier Matteo d'Amelia.
A walk between seventy works en plein air.
The seventeenth-century bell tower overlooking the village.
Among the most interesting archaeological sites in the region.
€5, reduced €4 or €3
The Baroque façade on the square.

A relief of natural and geological interest with hiking trails and panoramic views of the volcanic landscape and Tuscolo; from here a walk continues towards the Asinelli Hill, with activities for children and adults.

The village was born in the middle of the 14th century from the union of the villages of Villanova and Tulo and preserves an arch of Roman era. Among the traditional rural houses are the murals of Pinuccio Sciola inspired by the work of the poet Benvenuto Lobina (1914-93), also remembered by a bronze statue of Piergiorgio Gometz; the parish church of San Giuliano was rebuilt in 1663 in Gothic-Aragonese forms. From the center you can see the lake and the valley of the Flumendosa.
Frescoed crypts and the best view of the village of Rivolta.
One of the two oldest gates in the city, on the road to ancient Rudiae.
Closed for renovation and installation, undefined reopening (SardiniaCultura)

Borgo della piania bergamasca at the intersection of the ancient streets Cremasca and Francesca, dominated by the Rocca Albani, Visconti castle then Colleoni and Albani; in Piazza Libertà the parish church of Saints Nazario and Celso with the stone bell tower of Luigi Cagnola, just outside the small Sistine of the Holy Trinity and, in the hamlet Basella, the sanctuary and the African Museum.

In the Rivera district, three walls with white and pink marble chess with 99 carved faces from which water descends into two large tanks; traditionally recall the 99 castles that founded the city in the thirteenth century.

Cities on the Lemene river with the Gothic Town Hall in Piazza della Repubblica, the Molini and the bridge of Sant'Andrea, the National Museum of Concord with the finds of Iulia Concordia and, in Summaga, the abbey of Santa Maria Maggiore with medieval frescoes.

Village of the hinterland of Sanremo founded in Roman times as Coeliana, entered among the most beautiful villages of Italy: churches, four oratories and noble palaces among the caruggi, paths towards San Giovanni and Cima Furche.
In the Domus Magna, already home to the music school where Donizetti studied, the relics of his life: letters, family memories, autograph pages and the piano on which he composed his arias.
Fortress built by the Spaniards in the seventeenth century above Finalborgo, overlooking the sea.
One of the most important churches in the artistic evolution of Florence, overlooking the homonymous square to which the bridge also gives its name.
Reachable from the cloister, behind the eastern apse of the parish church, it preserves remains of buildings of the Iron Age and a water tank used in metal processing.

It rises on Byzantine and Arabic structures: rectangular fortress between a square tower and a Swabian pentagonal mast, with Swabian walls considered the best preserved defensive configuration of Sicily and the date 1270 engraved on the cistern. Frederick II of Aragon transformed it into a royal summer residence by opening eighteen large windows; the Byzantine royal chapel would preserve, according to some scholars, the remains of Arnaldo da Villanova. Restored in the eighties, it is municipal and hosts exhibitions and conferences.
Another piece of the monastery village.

Explored in 1850 by valleymen led by Domenico Mora and opened to the public on 2 August 1874, the first tourist cave in Italy; protected area managed by the Marguareis Park. The lower part has grandiose environments, the upper one narrow galleries on several floors, separated by the waterfall of Lake Ernestina; in the Hall of the Temple is exposed the reconstructed skeleton of a cave bear. Constant temperature of 9 °C, guided tours all year round with mandatory booking.
The Viceroy's bulwarks.
The city museum.

A small museum at the end of the second millennium in the former elementary school of St. Anne; it tells the historical context of the massacre of 12 August 1944, in which the SS killed 560 people including many children, and the contribution of Versilia to the Liberation. Outside, a plaque with the epigraph of Calamandrei in Kesselring and a carved reproduction of a detail of Picasso's "Guernica"; the exhibition space is connected to the Ossario Monument on the Col di Cava.
The theater from which the walk starts.

Borgo dei Peloritani was born, according to legend, around the Saracen castle, from whose ruins you can see the Aeolians: the sixteenth century Cathedral, the thirteenth-century church of San Francesco, the Municipal Theatre and, about 5 km, the Cistercian Abbey of Santa Maria La Noara; it is the home of the Majorchino and his Carnival tournament.
According to the MiC closed on Monday and Saturday, open on Tuesday 15-19, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday 9-13, Thursday 9-13 and 15-19; guided tours on request.

Village of Slavic origins (the ancient Pesclizzo) on a cliff of more than 70 meters overlooking the sea, in the Gargano National Park: white houses with steps, the castle and the Tower of the Bridge in the Baronial Recinct, the church of Sant'Elia Prophet and beaches Blue Flag among the most awarded of the promontory.
The ancient village.
A walk through the murals after the museums.
The monument symbol of the Fourth Roman.

In the heart of the basilica, under the dome, the stone walls of the house traditionally linked to the birth and Annunciation of Mary, which studies indicate of Palestinian origin. It contains the marble fence designed by Bramante and built by Sansovino, with statues and reliefs considered a masterpiece of the 16th century sculpture.
A walk on the castle hill.
An underground world of alabaster just a stone's throw from the village.

Inaugurated on June 6, 2015 in the monastery and church of Santa Giustina, already home to the Somaschi Fathers, Salò and Garda from the Roman era to today with archaeological finds of the Civic Archaeological Museum Anton Maria Mucchi, illuminated codes, paintings and musical instruments. It includes the Pio Bettoni meteosismic observatory (1877), the anatomical preparations of Dr. Rini, the Civic Collection of the Drawing with over 800 drawings of the post-war period and from 2023 a section on the Italian Social Republic.
Fossils, fauna and peasant life of the Iblei in one museum.

Founded in 1189 by Gioacchino da Fiore as Monasterium Florense, approved in 1196 by Celestino III; the 13th-century church, renovated in the 16th-17th century and restored twice in the 20th century, has a large portal of 1220 with palm-shaped capitals and archivolti with oak leaves, which bears traces of the fire of 1799. A unique long nave in bare stone, pronounced transept, baroque altar with the wooden statue of St. John the Baptist and rosettes on the back wall; in the crypt the urn with the remains of Joachim. In the halls is the International Center for Joachimite Studies (1982). Free admission; according to italia.it open every day 9-20.

The Cinquale is a well-known locality of Versilia that attracted artists and writers such as Enrico Pea, Gabriele d'Annunzio, Carlo Carrà and Mino Maccari; here the Green Beach is a free and accessible beach, designed for people with disabilities or motor difficulties.
Destroyed by the earthquake of 1693 and rebuilt in 1730, with a remarkable Gaginesco portal.
The mill in the rock.
A baroque interior entirely painted.

The village, called Montepeloso until 1895, is surrounded by turrite walls and is rich in noble palaces, portals and sacred buildings; at the entrance of the village there is an important rock settlement. It was an important centre in Roman times and one of the most developed of the Basilicata under Longobards and Byzantines; in 1123 Callisto II made it a bishop's seat.
The mining machinery up close.

In the green of the plain at the border with Acquanegra on the Churches, it takes its name from the system of taking water on the Churches started around the 11th century by the monks of the abbey of St. Thomas to irrigate the fields with the Seriola. The building dates back to 1428; for centuries it was disputed between the Venetian Asola and Acquanegra, until in 1911 the Water Court recognized Acquanegra the right to water.
Park with tree-lined avenues suitable for walking and cycling.
It is reached from Pescolanciano crossing the river Trigno and is known for its white fir woods.
The story under the square.
The green viewpoint on Torno and the lake.
The house of the cousins of the Cat.

In the countryside of the village of Orgnese is cultivated the red onion of Cavasso Nuovo, which the cycle path Pedemontana signals as a DOP product to buy in the village; among the fields you can enjoy the view of hills and mountains and stands the church of San Leonardo, of 1544, dedicated to the patron saint of prisoners and pregnant women.
One of the most pendant towers in Italy.
The Roman villa at the Timavo sources.
Inside the walls, of uncertain origin, perhaps the second half of the twelfth century; it preserves a marble carved with lilies and an organ of the eighteenth century.
One of the four palatine palaces in Puglia.
Panoramic view over the Fiumarella valley and the Gulf of Squillace.
The village of the lords of Avise, one of the oldest families in the Val d'Aosta region, with three castles, a medieval bridge and Pierre Taillée of the Via delle Gallie.
The "thermal temple" created in 1916 by Ugo Giovannozzi evokes the Roman thermal baths with colonnades, courtyards and fountains, immersed in the park.

Roman city along the Via Flaminia founded in the second century BC, from which derives the name Fossombrone: remains of houses, public buildings and a thermal complex of the first century BC with over 20 rooms. The visit starts from the church of San Martino; reservation via the IAT Point.
The panoramic walk of Ibla.
The shrine of the rafts of the Tagliamento.
Ancient engineering on the sea.
View of the coast.
The Gothic in Sardinia.
The remains of the medieval castle dominate the village: large walls and an octagonal Norman tower that make it look like an ancient acropolis.

Medieval village of Valle Roveto, closed by well preserved walls: the ancient part rises on an isolated spur, the modern one on the other bank of the river was rebuilt after the earthquake of 1915. To be seen are the "rue" with carved portals and votive newsstands, the church of San Giovanni Battista and the Pinacoteca Enrico Mattei.

The capital of Val di Scalve is linked to the dam of Gleno, whose collapse on 1 December 1923 caused more than 500 victims: the ruins are a destination for excursions and in the village an exhibition space preserves its memory. In the surroundings the Alpine Arboretum Gleno, with over 100 species of the valley, and the eighteenth-century water forge of Teveno.

Baroque palace built around 1630 for the Marquis Taffini d'Acceglio: the Aula Regia is frescoed with the military campaigns of Vittorio Amedeo I of Savoia by artists of the circle of Giovanni Antonio Molineri, including Jean Claret, and the Rococo salons were wanted by Isabella of Savoia-Carignano. Host Múses, a techno-sensory museum on Piedmontese aromatic herbs and the history of perfumery, with multisensory installations and works by contemporary artists. Open Thursday-Saturday 14-18, Sunday 11-13 and 14-18.

The atrium of the Compagnia dei Disciplinati di San Giovanni Battista, designed by Giuliano da Sangallo and frescoed in monochrome by Andrea del Sarto and Franciabigio with the Stories of the Baptist.
A medieval castle contested between Siena and Florence.
Area of 11 hectares with a water mirror of 7, suitable for birdwatching and sport fishing.

Walled village of the valley of Cesano, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with two walls (the second refitted by Francesco di Giorgio Martini), the church-pinacoteca of Sant'Agostino and, outside the village, the abbey of San Gervasio of Bulgaria; downstream the seaside resort of Marotta.
The cave of the monk seal.

Built between 1769 and 1775 and restored in 1975, it preserves the late Baroque high altar with a painting by Antonio Zanchi and the altar of the Madonna del Rosario attributed to the school of Andrea Brustolon. The bell tower, 65.80 meters high, was inaugurated in 1858 with bells arrived from Innsbruck.
The religious and civil center of the city.

Frazione in a small valley excavated by the stream Pedogna, just over 23 km from Lucca: simple village of stone houses where the name Puccini is documented from the sixteenth century; it was called only Celle until 1971, when the Municipality renamed it in honor of the composer.
The panoramic treeyard.
Medieval archeology outdoors on the hill of Cavaion.
open to the public in particular on the day of Saint Anne and the Assumption
The culture of mountain chestnuts.
The Srpotti's stucco and the oldest painting in the city.

Collegiate in 1478, destroyed by the earthquake of 1732 and rebuilt in the second half of the eighteenth century on a project by Ciriaco di Silva, pupil of Vaccaro; the 36-metre bell tower (1752-1766) is attributed to design by Vanvitelli. It preserves a canvas by Antonio Sarnelli (1766), the fresco of the Assumption by Matteo Vigilante (1768), a table of the Madonna del Rosario of 1573 perhaps of Flemish school, the main altar in polychrome marble (1761) and an organ by Michele Vigilante of 1779.

About 17,000 hectares between the Tyrrhenian and the river Mignone's bends, which are just over 600 meters long: pastures and forests of Mediterranean maquis, chestnut and beech, with wild orchids and rare raptors; the unpolluted sky is certified by Astronomitaly among the most beautiful skies of Italy.
Tracks of miners in the Sarentine Alps.
The ancient Augusta Praetoria, ... the Rome of the Alps: arch, port and the Roman theatre still standing, the medieval complex of Sant'Orso and the cathedral, among the mountains of the valley.

Quiet rural center of the upper Polesine, hamlet of Castelnovo Bariano near the river Tartaro-Canal Bianco. On the square there is the eighteenth-century church of San Pietro, with two twin bell towers; in the hamlet there is also the archaeological museum.

Sinis town overlooking one of the largest ponds in Europe, home of the bottarga: the ancient Tharros founded by the Phoenicians, the Giants of Mont'e Prama in the civic museum, the Byzantine church of San Giovanni di Sinis, the village of San Salvatore with its hypogeum and quartz beaches of Is Arutas in the protected marine area.

Made by Rolando Pallavicino from 1420, a rectangular plan with moat, cylindrical towers, mast and round paths; it contains a chapel with a cycle of Renaissance frescoes commissioned by Carlo Pallavicino, bishop of Lodi, attributed to Bonifacio Bembo, perhaps with his brother Benedetto (mid-15th century).
Type of visit not indicated by the source: ask the Municipality

The chestnuts of Cave, Traditional Agro-food product, are celebrated with the festival between October and November and end up in sweets; on the table dumplings with sheep sauce, tagliatelle ai porcini, polenta with cheese and walnuts, roasts of sheep and snails with Roman.
Oratory of the nineteenth century whose dome is the largest of the entire diocese of Piacenza-Bobbio.
Church of the sixteenth century in Pergnano with frescoes of the Baschenis, family of 16th century painters, including a Last Supper.

The Marina has fine sand and shallow and sloping seabed, suitable for families, with free and equipped beaches; near the beach La Crestarella dominated by the tower, the Schiarata and the free beach of Cancelluzzo, pebbles and sand, reachable only from the sea (for example by pedal boat from the Marina).

The historical nucleus of the Po river park, established as a reserve in 1979: it protects a Po's lanca, which for many years was the only nesting site of the red heron in Piedmont, and hosts nitticora, garza tuft and garzetta.
The Pitocchetto and the painting of reality.

Small height at the northern end of the Diaccia Botrona, once surrounded by the waters of Lake Prile and landing of the Etruscan boats: there arose in the first century BC a Roman villa attributed to Clodio, then incorporated in a Benedictine abbey of the early Middle Ages of which remains the Romanesque church to a nave with semicircular apse.

At the southern edge of the village remain the restored bell tower, in six-order volcanic stone cones with cat spire in Gothic-Catalan style, and part of the trachyte façade with the portal, whose arch key bears the cross of St. Andrew: it was the sixteenth-century parish church, abandoned in the early nineteenth century.
Climb into the emperor's tower and discover Maggiana's peasant life.
The oldest Romanesque church in the village.

Rude of a massive tower with bastion on a rocky spur of Monte Carmo, above the village, tied to the ancient mule track of the Passo delle Capanne. Carrega is documented since 1153; the fief passed from the bishops of Tortona to the marquises of Gavi and Parodi, then to the Malaspina; in the fifteenth century it was contested by the Fieschi. In 1475 a lightning strike struck the tower and Duke Galeazzo Sforza ordered its smoothing. The tower-tank to the south, the residence to the north and a barrel vaulted room remain; the area has been recovered from the town and from the ruin you can enjoy the view.
The new pedestrian promenade and about 15 km of beach, with free stretches of beach in San Giuliano, Rivabella, Viserbella and Torre Pedrera.
The richest art church in the historic centre.
A ridge between cherry trees and vineyards overlooking two valleys.
On foot or by bike along the old water way.

Housed in part of the church complex of the Visitation and part of the network of the Ecomuseum of Casentino since 2005-2007, it exhibits in two rooms finds of the territory from the VII century BC to the XIV century: Etruscan funeral rites, forms and uses of terracotta and history of the ancient disappeared churches of the area.
Buy a knife where it has been forged for centuries.
The white cliffs of Elba.
The Golden Room of the most beautiful palace in the Upper Lake.
Palace expanded in 1775 on the initiative of Maria Teresa of Austria, with archive, library and a collection of 18th century surgical irons.

A coastal municipality north of Syracuse, autonomous since 1979, rises around the octagonal square desired by Tommaso Gargallo in 1807; on the Magnisi Peninsula remain the remains of Thapsos, an emporium of the Bronze Age, next to the Riserva delle Saline di Priolo, where 216 species of birds have been recorded.
Rebuilt in 1931 on the remains of the original building of the thirteenth century, it preserves an ancient Christ crucified in polychrome wood of Romanesque art of the thirteenth century.
The symbol on the port.
Panoramic view over the hills and the Vena del Gesso.
In Borgo Ticino, beyond the Covered Bridge, starting point to walk along the Via Francigena.
The center dedicated to the founder of the house of tractors and cars, born in this territory.

Considered coeval at the birth of the village, wanted by the feudal lords next to the Baronial Palace and originally called Santa Maria in Castello. It collapsed in the earthquake of 1805 and rebuilt in 1826, it has three naves with three apses and frescoes by Mario De Tollis in the aisles.
The bell tower that draws the skyline of the village.
The mountain that dominates the Deiva valley, on the north side of which has emerged a medieval religious complex; around, trails for walks in the hinterland.
A Visconti castle turned farmhouse, still at work.
The medieval heart of the village, with the Dal Verme tower.
Roman artifacts.
A village of Eugubina foundation with its thirteenth-century doors.
The Viceroy's Palace.

The "city of steel" and Valentine's Day, in the basin of the Black: the Roman amphitheatre, the cultural center CAOS in a former factory and, a few kilometers away, the Marmore Falls and the archaeological area of Carsulae.
Designed by Riccardo Morandi and completed in 1962: his 120-meter-high centimeter was then the largest in the world; today it is among the highest arched bridges in Europe.

A seaside village on the Gulf of Sant'Eufemia, along the Riviera dei Tramonti: one of the best kitesurf spots, with strong wind and deep water all year round, and a promenade with equipped and local establishments. Each year it hosts the Kite Foil Youth World Champion.
A masterpiece of Lotto in a small village.
A chapel dug into the rock.

Ancient autonomous municipality, today a hamlet 7 km from Castignano at the foot of the Mount of Ascensione: it preserves walls of the XV-XVI century and a Romanesque-Renaissance bell tower 52 meters high, built in 1518.

Park of about three hectares around the villa, originally with vegetable gardens and citrus groves and from the sixteenth century scenery of musical and theatrical performances; in the eighteenth century Pompeo Litta enriched it with monumental fountains and at the beginning of the nineteenth century Luigi Canonica inserted an English grove. It hosts numerous species also exotic, kept in Liberty greenhouses in iron and glass, and has been awarded among the most beautiful of Italian public parks. Italia.it indicates opening every day 8:30-19:00.
The story of Bari in a house-tower.
The Sardinia of the nuraghi.
The painting of Nicodemus of 1159.
Hermitage of the late eighteenth century decorated with frescoes, bas-reliefs in plaster and tapestries.
For motor enthusiasts.

City of foundation of the Agro Pontino inaugurated on December 18, 1935, with the original nucleus intact, the Museum of the Agro Pontino and, on the Appia, the Roman state Ad Medias in Mesa with the eighteenth-century Palazzo della Posta.
The Calabrian parks in a hall.
A Tiepolo in Camerino.
The summer residence of Carlo Felice.
Monastery built between 1506 and 1560, with cloister with two loggias finished in 1560 and refectory of 1549; portal and oculus were carved in local stone in 1539 by Francesco da Milano.
A rococo jewel overlooking the canal.
Life in the Stones.

Complex founded in the fifteenth century by Saint Bernardino da Siena, well preserved, with the porch of the church and the main cloister intact. The basilica has frescoes, including the Madonna of the Angels of 1502, and a copy of the polyptych of Moretto, whose original tables were removed in the Napoleonic age. The convent is now private, the basilica is open on request.
About a kilometer of wide beaches on the seafront, almost all free and equipped, from which you can see the Torrione.
At the gates of Naples, Casoria houses the CAM, a contemporary art museum founded in 2005 and reopened in 2025 in renewed spaces, and the baroque Basilica of San Mauro, the oldest church in the city.

The cult was born from the image of the Madonna and Child painted on a wall along the road to Somma, near the remains of the arches of a Roman aqueduct: according to tradition on April 6, 1450 a young man, angry for a lost game, struck her and the painting bled. The sanctuary was built from 1593 to 1610 on a project by Giovan Cola di Franco incorporating the newsstand and the first church, and in 1595 passed to the Dominicans; inside the choir in carved walnut, the Adoration of the Magi by Luca Giordano and the temple of the image commissioned in 1621 to Bartolomeo Picchiatti, outside portals with biblical scenes in copper. The complex, with a portico cloister and crypt, preserves a rich collection of ex vows (the oldest probably dates back to 1499) in museum spaces with entrance from Via Romani; every Monday in Albis come the fujenti, the pilgrims dressed in white with red and blue bands.
A baroque villa became the library of the city.

Fortress on the morainic hill used by the Visconti and the Venetians, divided into Rocchetta and Main Quarter reached by a drawbridge; in front of its walls Napoleon defeated the Austrians in 1796. National monument since 1912, belongs to the Ugo Da Como Foundation; the ticket includes the immersive room with 360° projections and the Ornithological Museum. Free visit every day 10-18 according to the Municipality.
The stone benches where the fish was sold.
The golden ceiling with the 42 canvases of the Guarini.
A Renaissance hall remained as the day of the opening.
The fortress of Frederick II.
Ancient parish church of the 11th century, coeval to the birth of the castle of Monterubbiano.
The most panoramic path in Conca.
Next to the cathedral.
Red marble and hidden frescoes.
Popular devotion.
Florentine silvers of the seventeenth century.

In the diocesan centre of pastoral activities: sculptures, paintings, frescoes, fabrics and sacred furnishings from the VII to the XX century by the churches of the diocese, with works by Pordenone and Pomponio Amalteo.
The bridge over the Montone and, a little further, the "beach" of the Chiusa, with a waterfall and large slabs of rock where to sunbathe.

The temple of 1525, Santa Croce with the Baroque interior, the Blessed Annunciation and the Madonna dell'Ulivo, perhaps the oldest church in the country, with a terracotta Madonna considered miraculous.

The houses of the village are located next to the abbey, with streets and paved square with the traditional "Rizzato" and the farmsteads and granges that were the agricultural centers of the monastery.
The castle of the red towers.
The Palladian living room.
The church on the temple of Neptune.
For those seeking adventure in the water.

Small nucleus between the waters of two streams, at the confluence of the valleys Brandet and Campovecchio: the houses are wooden fir cabins with blockbau joints, which recall the Walser residences, and the village is crossed by wooden bridges.
The fire of the forge lit by water.
The village of fairies with sea views.

The harbor promontory, the most significant and suggestive part of the city, has recently been the subject of a recovery program. The fortified promenade offers clean beaches and at dusk animates clubs and restaurants.
The rocks excavated in the tuff and reachable by a path; from here come six frescoes of the 13th century today exhibited in the archaeological civic museum.
The baroque triumph of the square.
The parish church that dominates the square, in 19th century style, rebuilt between 1829 and 1837; in a chapel preserves the talking crucifix of the films.

Municipality scattered on the slopes of Pratomagno, with the capital Strada in Casentino, center of the working of the serene stone dominated by the castle of the counts Guidi; to see the Romanesque parish church of San Martino a Vado, Piazza Matteotti with the Logge del Grano, the village of Borgo alla Collina and the two antennas of the Ecomuseo del Casentino.
The treasure of the Norman Cathedral.

The seventeenth-century complex on Via dei Tribunali with the upper church, with free entrance, with works of Stanction, Jordan and Vaccaro and the winged skull of Dionisio Lazzari, and the hypogeum of the cult of the souls of Purgatory with the museum, which can be visited with a ticket.
The way to get to know Framura: starting from the highest village, Castagnola, and walking down the Costa, Setta and Ravecca to Anzo.
Among the collections, the laboratory of the luthier Ansaldo Poggi.
The center visits to understand the Majella before walking there.
The king's gardens.
A pearl of the Catalan baroque.
Turin, city of the car.
Two road tunnels transformed into spaces for exhibitions, installations and historical multimedia routes, reachable on foot crossing the bridge over the Adige.
the MiC card reports the museum closed every day; check at tel. 0123 55257
In the historic center of Antagnod, recognizable for the long wooden balcony and the cylindrical climbing tower.
The smallest Sacro Monte in Piedmont, on the Valdiana.

On the top of a hill to the south of Velino, it appears in 1080 when its church is registered near Montecassino; in 1485 it received defensive tower and walls designed by the architect Berardino Clario, whose name is engraved on the main door. There are still sections of walls, buttresses and doors, and in the oldest spontaneous architecture of the fifteenth century; in the center the mother church of Santa Maria delle Grazie and, just before the village, the rural church of San Sebastiano.
The battle of 1943 told as at the theater.

On piazza del Comune, built between the Five and the seventeenth century on a project by Pompeo Floriani: in the atrium and in the courtyard from the middle of the eighteenth century the Lapidary with honorary statues and Roman inscriptions. On the east side the 13th century Civic Tower.
The last tower of the Venetian fortress.
The church of the patron, between frescoes and baroque.
A world record of vintage petrol pumps.
The medieval center with cobbled streets, noble villas with painted facades and the commercial pedestrian island.
The symbol of the city and its view of the river.
Idese (MiC) indicates the temporarily closed entry, without reason; telephone 079 3403119.
Hydro-electric basin built in 1954 at 297 meters, about 3 km long on 66 hectares: fishing place (trot, carp, tinche), rowing and canoeing, with regattas on the summer weekends.
A little shade under the fortress.
Built by the Accademia degli Imperfetti, founded in the sixteenth century and active until the mid-nineteenth century; inaugurated in 1807 with 600 seats.
The most beautiful view of the city.

In via Mazzini there are the church of San Giovanni Battista, a 14th century building with a frescoed vault in the 18th century, and the church of San Giuseppe and San Pantaleone, which preserves a wooden choir from the late 15th century.

Museo d'impresa founded in 2002 by Fondazione Museo Agusta, with motorbikes MV Agusta, helicopters, aircraft engines and mechanical and avionic components of Agusta companies; the motorbike section recalls the models of the Motomondiale and pilots such as Giacomo Agostini and John Surtees, that helicopter the evolution of vertical flight, with a simulator of 129 on the first floor. The visit is accompanied by former workers' guides from the Agusta Group. The nearby Villa Agusta, built in 1935, furnished with antique furniture, houses Historical Archives and Library and can be visited on Sundays with the same ticket. Times indicated: Tuesday and Wednesday 14-18, Saturday 9-12 and 14-17, Sunday 9.30-12.30 and 14.30-18; reduced for 14-18 years, over 60 and groups, free up to 14 years; recommended booking on weekends.

Promontory in front of Capri that closes the Sorrento peninsula, the heart of a protected marine area with about 40 km of coast. A flat path of just under 2 km starts from the hamlet of Termini and leads to the fourteenth-century tower built on the site of the ancient temple of Athena-Minerva; near the grotto of the Sirene with an inscription in the Osk of the II century BC discovered in 1985. The return can follow the via Minervia, in part still paved.
The centre of the Val Bormida, probably of Roman origin and mentioned as Bugile in 998-999; it houses Villa Maura with the museum of the writer Anton Giulio Barrili Garibaldi and the Alpine Museum.
The seventeenth-century church that incorporates a previous building and preserves a late-Gothic portal in the Catalan-Gothic style, decorated with the coats of arms of the Cardona.
A Liberty theatre waiting for restoration.
Roman countryside with ancient tombs a stone's throw from Rome.
The Paladini-Enriquez residence was built in 1627 above a previous castle, of which traces remain on the eastern side.
From the sea to the highest peak of the area.
Silver, gold and baroque statues of the parish.
A walk from fairy tale to the waterfall, with giant bench.

Fortified building of the sixteenth century, originally isolated, with two high square towers at the corners, the eighteenth-century court on two levels towards Piazza del Popolo and the rustic portal surmounted by the coat of arms and two statues; the Protonobilissimi, marquis in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, transformed it into a marquisal palace. Today it hosts exhibitions, shows and conferences.
Where time has stopped.
Neoclassical frescoes.
The Romanesque among the chestnut trees of the Amiata.

Large piazza porticata and scenic, the ancient Piazza Maggiore of the sixteenth-century village, with the Collegiata, the bell tower of 1616, the monument to the Fallen by Giuseppe Graziosi and, to the east, the entrance to the Rocca. A 1563 regulation fixed the height and colorful decorations of the houses.

On the eastern side of the jar, just over a kilometer from the village: the Sa Fogaia corridor nuraghe, born as protonuraghe with a plant at Y, a prehistoric village with a workshop of the obsidian of Mount Arci, holm oak and spot with over 150 plant species along the path

Via Vittorio Emanuele is called "Via Sacra" for the five religious buildings that flank it among noble palaces: the Church of Carmine, with facade that unites doric and ionic order; the Mother Church, with the oldest preserved municipal coat of arms (1763) on the portal and inside full of stuccoes; the Church of Santa Maria, already convent, school and prison, with a wooden crucifix by Friar Umile from Petralia of 1633. In via Umberto civil buildings unite Baroque and Liberty.
The wooden skis that accompanied the birth of Sestriere.

The ancient center preserves palaces of the Aragonese and Spanish era with portals in piperno and travertine and baroque masks; among the ancient places the Municipality remembers the castle of via Castello, today via Genoino, and the district of via Miseno, linked to the tradition of the funnels.

Built in the 12th century and consecrated by the bishop of Novara Litifredo, three-nave brick with three semicircular apses with blind arches; it preserves the most ancient frescoes (1132-1151) with angels and apostles on the tibury and saints of the sixteenth century, while chapels, stuccos and Baroque frescoes (Francesco Belloto, workshop of Carlo Antonio Morino) date back to the late seventeenth-seventh century; facade of the second half of the eighteenth century with bezel of Clemente Salsa, bell tower of 1756. Open on Saturday afternoons and Sundays (parish house 0321 985469).
The "Urbs Picta"
The Roman roots of Diano, on the Via Iulia Augusta.
The eighteenth-century college ruin.

A single nave church built in 1778 on a Romanesque chapel of the 12th century, dedicated to St. Audentius, friend of St. Julius. It has two bell towers: the Romanesque bell tower on the north side, among the oldest of the Riviera, in pebbles with slits and mullioned windows, and one in 1792. Inside the Adoration of the Shepherds by G. Cesare Procaccini and restored frescoes, including the Visitable during the time of the Masses.
A Roman city on the Martani ridge.
Vespasian's mother's house.
A temple flies over a hut of the Iron Age.
A show in a movie theater.
The tombs of Azetium.
Skiing on the World Cup slopes.
The day and evening market.
It retraces the stages of contemporary art in Terra di Lavoro from the post-war period to today with a permanent collection.
The house where tradition wants Giotto born, with materials on his work and the reconstruction of the workshop of a painter of the fourteenth century; near, the bridge of the encounter with Cimabue.
The mosaic to walk.
The sunshine of May 25.
The sixteenth-century fortress that dominates the city.
The city of fairs.
Santa Maria Scala Coeli has two frescoes, one of which is attributed to the school of Perugino; the church of Saints Peter and Paul was built in 1290.
Spargi's white coves.
Juvarra Castle.
It documents Roman sites and finds of Republican and late imperial age of the territory.
The scenic staircase of the village.
The beach of the founder of the Costa Smeralda.

The center is divided into the districts Castello, Calcinate and Cassebba, with houses mostly whitewashed joined by alleys (caruggi) and stairs. The arch of via Solferino, the most visited place of the village, was the entrance of Casa Porcile, one of the most important families of the colony; in the village also Palazzo Rombi, eighteenth-century residence of the French consul, and the promenade where fishermen still shelter the nets.
The oldest nucleus of Vizzini, at the top of the hill of the same name.

With original objects, photographs and plastics, it tells the life and the environment of Lessinia: prehistory, alpine pasture, haymaking, milk processing, production of coal, ice and lime, carpentry, spinning and weaving, popular religiosity. It has two separate sections a few kilometers away, the Baito della Coletta and the Jassàra del Gritz. In autumn open Saturday and Sunday, Christmas and summer every day except Monday; guided tours by reservation.

Built between 1899 and 1902 on the Spanish ramparts of the Sperone and the Mint, with the large terrace Umberto I and the highest one of Santa Caterina: you walk up from Piazza Constituzione or elevator, with views of Marina, Stampace, port and Poetto; on Sunday morning market of handicrafts and collecting.
Managed by Combonian missionaries, it is a study center that promotes African culture.
The village of the round tower.
The famous weekly market in Piazza Galimberti.
A thousand nativity scenes from over 130 countries in a private collection.
The memory of the mining basin of Valdarno.
Open from May to early November on Wednesday 8-18; key at Haus Sigmund
Simple single nave church dedicated to St. John the Baptist, patron saint of the village, built in 1597 by Prince Giovanni Natoli.
A Roman villa surprised by the eruption.
The hill mentioned for its elegance and views of the gulf.
Small emissions of gorgling mud, already known in Roman times and used by the Middle Ages as healing mud for the skin; in Berzora also a house-tower of the seventeenth century.

Panoramic village called "balcony of the Apulia" overlooking the valley of Ofanto and the National Park of the Alta Murgia; the historic center, the "Scesciolia" is a labyrinth of tuff and white facades, with the Duomo, and at the foot of the town opens the Cave of San Michele, a place of thousand year old worship.
The bikes of the legend MV and the Agusta helicopters told by those who built them.
The oldest church in the city, commissioned by Matilde di Canossa in 1082: circular and matroneo plant with traces of Byzantine school frescoes.
One of the most famous beaches on the island.
A less known page in Sienese history.

Opened in 1987 in the third cloister of the former cloister of the Poor Clares, already hospital of pilgrims going to Rome, in the Rocca district, the highest point of the village: bronze sculptures, paintings, sketches, archive and working instruments of the sculptor and Roman painter Guido Calori (1885-1960), including the bronze Italica Gens awarded at the Venice Biennale of 1930. Open Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10-14.

On the saddle between the hills of Guasco and Cappuccini, overlooking the port and the old town, it dates back to the Augustan age and was expanded under Traiano; you visit only with guide, departing from the National Archaeological Museum.
Clement Zamara's Renaissance wooden latency.
A castle of the Doria still inhabited, with prisons and legend.
A painting attributed to Palma the Younger in a mountain village.
The castle dominates the village.
The Teutonic portal.

Church consecrated in 1492 on the site of a more ancient Romanesque church. It keeps the altar with carved doors in chestnut wood and gilded with pure gold by the sculptor Sveto Hans Schnatterpeck in about eight years and consecrated around 1511: about 14 meters high and 7 meters wide, it is indicated as the largest Gothic altar in the Alps, with a rare Throne of Grace between the life-size statues of Peter and Paul. It was paid by about 800 inhabitants of Lana.

Country of the Vercellian rice plain, seat of the Natural Park of the Blades of Sesia, established in 1978 to protect the wetlands left by the river: here you can visit the Ornithological Museum of the park and the surviving tower of the fifteenth-century castle of the Arborium of Gattinara.
The basilica of the vote.

Borgo della costa Ionica, feud of the Knights of Malta, with the historic center of Sciangài, the Mother Church in carparo and the Palazzo del Commendatore; on the coast the dunes of Campomarino and the Tower of the Ovo.
The pebble climb and the rock of the witches.
A medieval crypt along the stream.
Around the village gardens, woods and paths on the slopes of the valley of the Conca, where you can meet squirrels, hares, deer and hawks.

First Lombard Dukedom in Italy and stop of the UNESCO site "I Longobardi" in Italy: the Temple of Santa Maria in Valle, the Altar of Ratchis in the Christian Museum and the Devil's Bridge on Natisone, among the Eastern Hills of Friuli.
The UNESCO Dolomites run by a millenarian community.

Terracotta village in the valley of Cesano, with the ancient spiral nucleus of pink brick houses closed by the medieval walls and the Franciscan monastery of Santa Vittoria (1216), home of the Museum of Terracotta; in the village the workshops of the cocciari, active for centuries.

On Mount Calvario, at 853 meters, a small chapel whose oldest part dates back perhaps to the seventeenth century, built with square re-utilization stones, in a site that offers a wide view and perhaps housed the matrix church of Santa Balbina. Next remain the ruins of the station of the optical telegraph Bourbon, for which the area was sold in 1850 to the Real Telegraphic Body: perimeter walls, an oval observatory and an underground cistern.
The cycle of Cambellotti on the reclamation.

At the slopes of the Monticelli hill, just over a kilometer from the village, look over the valley of Fasanella and of the heat up to the Gulf of Naples on clear days. The origins of the cult are dated back to the sixth century; the name Selice comes from the mule track that led to the first sacellus. The present building, rebuilt in 1960 after a landslide on the original plan, has a single nave covered in travertine, mosaic rosette, stained glass windows with the seven sacraments and a stone bust of the Madonna in Byzantine style; next, the ancient stone fountain called "Moccio" . It has been a diocesan shrine since 2016 and the festival falls on Tuesday after Pentecost.

At the top of the village, it is the most important building in the village: for centuries it was the noble residence of the Nemours family, then Sacchi-Nemors, counts of Frassinello, whose coat of arms is still in the floor of the salon of honor.
The Romanesque green stone of a mountain fraction.
The pond of rare species.
A piece of twentieth century architecture signed Gardella.
The luxury of the Roman villas on the gulf.
The large modern church in Palma Square.
The castle-residence of Cardinals Pallotta.
View of the Trieste Karst to the Vipacco valley in Slovenia.
The town hall in Piazza del Popolo 10, the political heart of the city on the Fontana Masini square.

The name comes from Arquata montium, for its position on the slopes of two hills; the medieval system is intact, with paved streets, porticoes and palazzetti in Venetian style. Via Roma, with shops and buildings from the 13th and 14th centuries, leads to Villa Alessi, an ancient bishop's seat that today hosts events and concerts.
The altar of peace of Augustus.
In the area of ancient Siponto, four sections with tools and objects of domestic life, agriculture, crafts and fishing, and recorded dialectal voices.

Built in 1721, it has a semi-elliptic façade designed by Biagio Scaramuzzino. Inside the ciborium of Cosimo Fanzago and Andrea Gallo, the apparition of the Virgin to St. Bruno by Paolo De Matteis (1721) and the Death of St. Anne (1645), attributed to Reynaud Levieux; the bronze outer door is by Giuseppe Maria Pisani jr. (1961).
Craft shops, fountains and views of Montiferru.
The great mosaic of 1980.
Gaudenzian frescoes in a small country church.
The village with the castle on top of the hill, panoramic terrace on the Valdinievole.
The neoclassical temple with the altarpiece of Delitala.

Founded in 2003, it organizes exhibitions, fairs, conferences and concerts every year; it is located in the center, next to the Town Hall, in a bright and transparent contemporary building that creates a light room around the exhibition spaces, dedicated to the memory of Giuseppe Lazzareschi.
The catacombs on the Appia Antica street, among the places of Christian Rome of origin.
Mar-dom 10-18:30, Monday closed
Hiking the Sibillini.

A village built in neo-Medieval style at the beginning of the twentieth century by Giuseppe Visconti di Modrone, recognized as an art town in 1986. In the centre of the Biscione square, with the Palace of the Institution, the Hotel of the Biscione and the well; in the Cortevecchia, under the long porch, a small museum of agricultural tools; the statue of Aloisa recalls the legend of the ghost of the village. Closed to traffic, with two large parking spaces at the entrances (free in the weekdays, paid on weekends); artisan workshops open all year round, the houses are private.

Sanctuary in the hamlet of Mezzana, linked to the legend of a 13th century Marian apparition among the branches of an oak, scene that Michelino da Besozzo frescoed in the vault. Pellegrino de' Pellegrini enlarged the structure by designing the current sanctuary, with a large altar in front of the small original apse that leaves the fresco visible; the facade is decorated with statues.
Visits can jump for rehearsals and shows

Also known as San Giovanni Piedimonte or Capodacqua, it was built in the middle of the 11th century by Bishop Pandolfo, who laid in 1059 the relics of the Saints Martyrs; in 1223 it was the only church spared by Frederick II in the fire of Celano. On the architrave of the portal is an eagle nymbata, symbol of St. John the Evangelist; on the side is the portal of women with cruciform rosette of the 11th century and the coat of arms of the Berardi. Inside a fourteenth-century holy water and frescoes of the 14th-XV century on the vaults.
A Sol LeWitt ceiling in the library.
On the hill that dominates the village, among oak woods, holm oaks, cypresses and pine trees, it preserves traces of the Aldobrandesque walls and a church with Romanesque foundations.

Naturalistic collection of the Collegio di Celana, constituted at the end of the nineteenth century by Don Bernardino Gavazzeni, a science teacher, who preserves the original nineteenth-century setting with furniture, showcases and handwritten captions and important finds of the valley. The College was wanted by San Carlo Borromeo in 1578 as a seminary and became a college after the suppression of 1798, hosting gymnasium and high school.
Artificial basin formed by the barrier of the Osento stream, Site of Community Interest within the meaning of the Habitats Directive.
Schio's mother church.
A former 17th-century vow against the plague.

Small Byzantine church built between the end of the X and the beginning of the XI century by oriental monks on a spur of Mount Consolino; the name comes from the Greek "Katholikon" , the main church of a monastic complex. In exposed brick, Greek cross inscribed in a square with three apses and five cupolettes, has inside four bare columns, one with a gemstone cross and another with inscriptions in Arabic. The frescoes, discovered by Paolo Orsi in 1927, preserve the Dormitio Virginis, the Ascension and figures of saints; since 2006 the site has been nominated with other Basilian places of Calabrian Heritage of Humanity.
Hot water coming out in the square.
The viewpoint on the vineyards of Barolo.
Area open in some periods with visits by reservation to the Museum
An echo of San Fedele in Milan in Valle San Martino.
In the Palazzo degli Studi, the municipal library with about 400,000 volumes and the room that takes its name from the world map made in 1713 by cartographer Moroncelli.

Probably risen in the second half of the 11th century and consecrated in 1106, with three naves on granite columns with Corinthian capitals; facade modified in 1603, eighteenth-century chapel of San Paride, rebuilt on a project by Roberto Pane after the destruction of the war.
A journey of memory through the Apuan woods.

Higher on the wooded hill, on the road to Todi: it was a Ghibelline castle overlooking the Guelphs of Orvieto. You enter from the fourteenth-century Porta Fuje, with the stone coat of arms with the eagle of Todi; there rises the abbey of Santa Maria in Monte.
The wine of the Roman patricians and the sweets of the must.

Regional reserve of 46 hectares between Neptune and Anzio: the historic villa on a hill overlooking the sea, with Italian garden, orange garden and forest of farnie, holm oaks, corks and pine trees; under the villa galleries used during the Allied landing. D'Annunzio stayed there in the early 20th century.
€3, reduced €2 (4-14 years); with the Museum of the Soundscape €6, reduced €4
The 11th century small country church that gives its name to the park among centuries-old olive trees, surrounded by the houses of the pilgrims of the novenary.

Medieval village near Potenza, at the gates of the ancient Lucanian people: the fortified town of Serra di Vaglio with the House of the Pithoi, the Federal sanctuary of Mefite in Rossano, the Museum of the ancient people of Lucania, the mother church with the octagonal Norman tower and the snowshoe on Mount Jupiter.

The mining district of San Martino Monteneve, reachable only on foot from Val Passiria, includes a mining village at 2,355 m and the extraction area, inhabited and worked in very harsh conditions from the Middle Ages to 1967: it was the most important deposit of lead and zinc in Tyrol and between 2,000 and 2,500 m is presented as the highest mine in Europe, with over 150 km of tunnels. Today there are refuge, exhibition and mine adventure, with half day or full day excursions with the train of the mine; guided tours (Tuesday and Thursday 9:15, Saturday and Sunday 8:30) only by reservation before 16 of the day before, from the car park of Monteneve Bridge.
The villa of Paolina Bonaparte.
A high-altitude sanctuary between peaks and alpine lakes.
Jacopo Bassano and Canova together.
Library open Monday-Friday 8-14 and 15-19 (Common).
The civilization of the chestnut told by its tools and houses.
Panorama on the Friulian plain.

Built between 1937 and 1947 on a project by Mgr. Spirit Maria Chiapetta, modified by Giuseppe Martinenghi, next to the Augustinian monastery where the saint died in 1457; shrine since 1955. Interior in Byzantine style with Greek cross with works by Eros Pellini, furnishings by Giacomo Manzù, frescoes by Luigi Filocamo, Gisberto Ceracchini and Silvio Consadori, dome by Luigi Montanarini; in the chapel of the saint the body in a crystal urn of 1930. You can also reach it with the escalators from the center.
Ancient holiday resort united in Genoa in 1926: panoramic walk on the cliffs, small pebble beach and the Nervi Parks with the rose garden, home of the Nervi Music Ballet Festival.

Medieval fortified building symbol of the village, built around the middle of the fourteenth century by Mastino II della Scala in defense against Mantua, on the shore of Tartaro along the road to Vigasio; it was part of the Serraglio Veronese, the defensive system that went from Lake Garda to Ostiglia.

A relief of 528 meters behind Salò, among cypresses, olive trees and oleanders, reachable by a panoramic path suitable also for untrained walkers; at the top the church of San Bartolomeo with views of the lake and the nearby villages.
A church turned into an auditorium.
The path of the chapels to the sanctuary in the woods.
The pecorino and the life of the shepherds.
From the village to the sea on foot.
Walk on a transhumance route through open landscapes.
The memory of the 1944 landing.
The millennial fair.
The Matterhorn reflected.

Tourist station at an altitude between Artogne and Pian Camuno, born between the seventies and eighties with the first plants: the original nucleus of Alpiaz is about 1,200 m, the Plan at 1,800 m, where a statue in Corten steel 6 m high Mattia Trotta (2021) recalls the victory of Marco Pantani at the Giro d'Italia in 1998. In summer walks among the rhododendrons, excursions and bikes, including the Trail n. 721 from Plan to Rifugio Rosello and the Trail of the 3 Valleys; the ski area has about 30 km of slopes between 1,200 and 1,800 m.

Near the Orecchiella and Fortezza delle Verrucole, acrobatic paths on trees for all ages with catwalks, Tibetan and Tyrolean bridges up to 15 meters from the ground, as well as excursions, trail running and e-bike; picnic areas with barbecue, bar and playground for children.
Church and monastery erected on the northern bank of Ticino.
The village is in a beautiful panoramic position, with a medieval structure reminiscent of a fan.
Under the Villa Comunale, near the port, with equipped establishments and free stretches to swim in the city.

Parish of Schianno, is among the four churches of the municipality indicated as worthy of particular attention. It contains frescoes by Isidoro Bianchi da Campione and a fine 15th century milk Madonna.

The oldest and most beloved square of Verona, built on the Roman forum area and the heart of political and economic life, surrounded by the palaces of historical families and dominated by Palazzo Maffei.
A rare collection of Byzantine icons in Piceno.
The island between the two seas.
The early Christian Concord under the cathedral.
From Pontine to Abruzzo in one look.
The house bought by the poet in 1526, where he wrote the last edition of the Furious Orlando, with the Latin motto on the facade, the small museum and the garden.
Ancient watering trough wanted by the Marquis Simone Ventimiglia, rectangular and about 20 meters long, with two lateral stone fountains and four mouths that pour the water in sandstone cups.
The fourteenth-century frescoes of the Camerino school.
Built by the Swedish doctor Axel Munthe, it preserves the richest collection of ancient finds and works of art on the island and is the only nineteenth-century residence of Capri as it was.
A look at the daily life of the lake country.
A walk in the historical park around the pond.
The palace in front of the University, seat of the city government since the 13th century.
One of the two recently restored Baroque monuments in Via Saffi, just a few steps from the square.
Church of the center known for the majolica floor.
Stories of smugglers.
A quiet green corner in the center.
Get off at the shelters built for the workers during the bombings.
A curved baroque façade.
Small brick church of the VII-VIII century, with central plan with three absides of Byzantine-Ravenna taste, with a Madonna of Domenico by Michelino.
The echo of Pompeian frescoes in contemporary art.
X century church with frescoes of the XIII century, on origins of the sixth century remembered by Gregorio Magno.

The northernmost municipality of Friuli Venezia Giulia, in Carnia at the foot of Monte Coglians (the highest peak in the region): in the museum palace the ethnographic collection    \ Cemùot chi erin Â Â Â Â and the exhibition on the Great War, at the height of the lakes of Bordaglia and Volaia and the forre of Bordaglia and Fleons.
Dunes and migratory birds at the mouth of the Tronto.

16th-century castle seat of the city museums: Archaeological Museum with materials from Aquileia, Galleria d'Arte Antica from the fourteenth to the nineteenth century with the Consilium in arena of Giambattista and Giandomenico Tiepolo, Museo del Risorgimento from 1797 to 1866 and Museo della Fotografia with the first photo taken in Udine (1856). From the back staircase the panorama of the Carnic and Julian Alps.
The sea of the landing of Enea.

Country of the Varaita Valley mentioned in the sources written around the Mille and linked to the Marchesato di Saluzzo until the passage to the Savoy in 1601; on the square the parish church of Saints Peter and Paul with the Romanesque portal and the cycle of the Biazaci brothers, then the historical ethnographic museum with the drapes of the Baio, the sanctuary of the Becetto and the Sentiero dei Sarvanot in Rore.
The twentieth century of Ferrara.

Carnic village between 1000 and 1400 meters, on the shores of the artificial lake of the Lumiei valley, chosen by the Ministry of Tourism to represent Italy at the Best Tourism Villages UNWTO 2022: the church of San Lorenzo in Sauris di Sopra, the sanctuary of Sant'Osvaldo with the altar of Michael Parth in Sauris di Sotto, the ethnographic center and the historiographic center.

The Palazzo Boschi-Rivani-Garagnani in Ceretolo, documented from the late seventeenth century and opened as a museum house since 2020: three floors of furniture, paintings, ceramics and family memories, with kitchens, loggias, gardens and chapel.
Roman ruins on the sea.
Ancient Christianity near Amiternum.
The best view.
A few kilometers from the village in the direction of Isernia, entrusted to the Capuchins, a destination of pilgrimages; in the convent Father Pio stayed.

About 1 km from the village along the SS 128, on the Torrei river: a mill for the wheat and two galleries to crowd the wool. Sa Cracchera de tziu Bellu, made of stone with wooden cover, has roverella sweaters powered by a hydraulic wheel that beat the wet orbace with hot water to make it soft and resistant; it ceased its activity in 1975 and back to work during the visits and to "Autunno in Barbagia" .

Archaeological area in via Castello from which starts the itinerary       Â Archaeological Mesagne Â Â, with the necropolis of Hellenistic age; the route continues with the underground mill of Palazzo Guarini and the remains, partially visible, of the church of SS. Salvatore. The complex was promoted in 2022 with a virtual tour along with the Granafei museum.
Casa-grotta eighteenth century restored with kitchen, cistern, stable and manger, vintage tools and a didactic workshop.
Sculpted taurine protomes.
Wild beach between two mouths of river.
A miniature peasant world.

According to Ugo Procacci's archive research, Masaccio spent most of his childhood there (it is not the established birthplace). Purchased by the Municipality in the early sixties and renovated in the seventies, it is a contemporary art center with temporary exhibitions of Italian and European art, meetings, workshops, cinemas and concerts; the municipal collection, born from donations, includes works by Alighiero Boetti, Giovanni Anselmo, Alberto Garutti, Mauro Staccioli, Massimo Bartolini, Alberto Moretti, Venturino Venturi and Marco Airò.
The floor with the mosaic fragments.
Walk from the city to the marina.
A walk in the regular plant of a village born in the eighteenth century.

Guard station on the north side of Scalea, connected to the castle, from which the bay was dominated. According to tradition, at the beginning of the seventeenth century the guardian did not alarm the arrival of the Saracens and, captured, was hanged to a tree: hence the name; the historians also propose a bond with the nearby Jewish ghetto.
access only in time slots (Thursday afternoon, weekend with Arkeotrekking, summer calendar)
€3 (free under 12 accompanied)
The ancient Pallanza.

Sandy and rocky coves loved by surfers, divers and divers, with many summer residences in liberty style along the coast. To the south of the village, in Parco Mallorca, the wooden piles on rows of poles; from Capolinaro onwards, equipped sandy beaches prevail.
The fortress of the emperor.
One of the oldest and most evocative of Emilia-Romagna: you enter it from an iron gate with the five-pointed star and the word "shalom"; 57 burials have been identified.
Area of Monte Baldo with botanical itineraries, rare species and flowery pastures.

In the valley of Forzo, about 4 km from the provincial, inhabitants and holidaymakers transform every year the alleys of the village into an outdoor exhibition of cribs made with natural materials of the mountain tradition; the tour, easy with a few steps, takes about 15 minutes. Visitable every day, even in the evening, from 8 December to 6 January.
€3 in certain periods of the year

Built in 1317 by Count Francesco I Ventimiglia on a 12th century watch tower, it houses the Civic Museum with sections of Archaeology, Urbanism, Sacred Art and Modern and Contemporary Art, as well as events and exhibitions. In the Palatine Chapel the stuccoes of Giuseppe and Giacomo Serpotta (1684-1687) and the Skull of Sant'Anna kept in a silver reliquary bust of 1521.

Impressive Norman castle of the 11th century, erected in 1080 by Robert Guiscardo, symbol of resistance against the Saracens: it dominates the historic center and the new Ginosa, which rises from the Mother Church to the castle.
Other canvases of the Genovesino a few steps from San Siro.

The back bridge of donkey, of seventeenth-century origin and rebuilt in 1862 to facilitate navigation, combines the two villages of Cassinetta and Lugagnano; next to stands the statue of San Carlo Borromeo (1749), which passed here in 1584. Nearby the Osteria del Ponte, a stopover from the sixteenth century, and the docking of the tourist boats on the Naviglio.

In the hamlet of Sisini the nuraghe on Nuraxi has an unusual plant, similar to that of a well temple; its Nuragic finds are exhibited at the museum sa Domu Nosta. In the hamlet also Villa Aresu, a nineteenth-century residence, and the arrival of the trot races is Cuaddus de santa Vida for the feast of Santa Vitalia.
In the center of the village, with the Romanesque bell tower and the museum of sacred art.
Touring indicates closed March-May and September-November and varying periods in winter
The pine forest sung by Dante and Byron and, at its edge, the mouth of the Bevano: dunes, fresh and brackish waters on about 40 hectares.
Neoclassical building designed by Pietro Camporese in 1796, with 17th century paintings and a collection of objects related to the liturgy of Good Friday.
Walk on the trail of the valley's mining history.
Three hundred statues in heaven.
The ferruginous water that cured the Habsburgs.

Rebuilt in 1695 on the initiative of the Confraternity of Santa Croce and enlarged and made parish in 1807; the bell tower is the oldest part. It preserves a Madonna by Stefano Maria Clemente, an eighteenth-century wooden Crucifix by Carlo Giuseppe Plura, the medallion of the vault by Giovanni Enea Coda (mid-nineteenth century) and an organ by Achille Baldi from 1903.
Ethnographic museum set up in the tower, open during the opening periods.
€9, reduced €6, free under 6 and with FVG Card
The judicial fortress that dominates the Ocean.
Hall of the 19th century hamlet school with wooden counters, chair, stove and teaching materials.

Itinerary of 8.5 km (about 3 hours and 20 minutes, difference in altitude 246 m, difficulty T) from the swimming pools of Prasco to the Rocca di Visone, on asphalted country roads with two short dirt sections, also suitable for the MTB and accessible all year round. Touch the former parish church of Saints Nazarius and Celsus (XI-XVI century, in the cemetery of Prasco), the country church of the Cappelletta (XV century), the Roman bridge over the river Visone, the oratory of San Rocco and the tower of the castle Malaspina; churches and towers are visited by appointment with the municipalities of Prasco or Visone.
The "city of the hundred churches," closed by intact Renaissance walls of more than 4 km walkable and by bike, with the square born from the Roman amphitheatre; city of Puccini.

A 16th-century bastion that spans the historic centre on both banks of the Adda: about 2 km long, 12 m tall and on average 3,60 m thick. Inside the walls the Casematte, 93 large vaulted rooms once military housing, warehouses and shooting stations, all connected in a path of almost one kilometer; restored by the Volunteers Group Walls, host events and exhibitions.

Via del Mercato, considered the original nucleus of the village, is flanked by a double portico built between the 14th and 16th century where the weekly market was held; Via di Dentro, the ancient heart of the village, runs between the Tower of Porta Sottana (quadrangular plant, pointed arches and the hinges of the ancient gates) and the Tower of Porta Soprana, raised in the nineteenth century for the bells of the clock. The Via della Maiolica at the foot of the walls, the Vicolo Behind the Walls with houses built above the belt, the eighteenth-century Palazzo Tamburelli-Malaspina, now Town Hall, and Piazza della Fiera with public gardens.
visits to be agreed with the Cultural Office of the Municipality of Varazze (tel. 019 9390239)
MiC card indicates closed every day, times to check with the museum

Built between 1492 and 1494 for Ludovico il Moro, designed by Leonardo da Vinci: rectangular plan with three portico sides and the fourth closed by the façade of the cathedral; the current appearance is due to Bishop Caramuel in the seventeenth century.
A place of European memory.
The collegiate with seventeenth-century paintings attributed to Matteo Rosselli, Giacinto Gimignani and Rutilio Manetti.

The name derives from a bridge over the Lenta river of the Longobard Prince Landolfo; documents from 1064 mention the abbey of Santa Teodora and the castle. Besieged in 1138 and 1462, struck by the earthquakes of 1456 and 1688, from 1466 it was of the Carafa of Cerreto; on August 14, 1861 the troops of the Royal Army burned it for retaliation killing over 400 civilians.
The three-jump waterfall that enchanted D'Annunzio.
The Etruscan tombs of Tuscania.
Historic noble residence in the municipal public park, home to the "Roberto Allegri" Civic Library and the informal art collection of the Municipal Art Gallery.
In the former Augustinian convent on Piazza Borelli, masks of contemporary artists who reinterpret the ubagu, the impervious places at the border between the solar world and the dark world.
Closes the circle of the three hills.
The temple of Barbaresco.
The emerald of water at the foot of the Prealps.

Founded in 1903 by Austrian dentist and botanist Arthur Hruska with plants from the Alps, Himalayas, Japan, Australia, Canada and New Zealand; purchased in 1988 by artist André Heller, it combines about 3,000 species with works by Keith Haring, Roy Lichtenstein, Rodin, Miró and Mimmo Paladino, with a Japanese garden. In spring, tulips, wisteria, magnolias, azaleas and water lilies flourish.
The five-century triptych.
The balcony of high Tuscia.
The Borgolungo with its porticoed streets and nineteenth-century buildings, crossed by the Carruggio Stratto with artisan shops and bars.
The medieval square.
16th century frescoes in a mountain church.
A short walk for a great view of the valley.
€11, reduced €8, children 3-11 years €5
Small former octagonal church, built according to tradition on the site of a temple of Diana Trivia, today protected by the Superintendence of Chieti and Pescara.
The House of the Teutonic Knights on the Brenner Street.
The castle of Queen Joan I.
Entrance to floor

Gorges excavated from the Tenna, among the most suggestive of the Umbrian-Marche Apennines, with waterfalls and clear pools. The path starts from the entrance of the gorges, at an artificial gallery and the small waterfalls of the Pisciarelle, passes a wooden bridge and enters the beech wood; at the crossroads you go up to the hermitage of San Leonardo or continue towards Capotenna, the source of the Tenna, passing the hidden waterfall.
