The town of Guercino, 25 km from Bologna: porticoed centre, the Pinacoteca reopened after the earthquake and the Carnival.
Understand how the walls were born.
The circuit named after Marco Simoncelli, seat of MotoGP (in September) and Superbike (in June), with guided tours in box, pit lane and race direction.
The only whale of his kind.

Maritime villa of the middle of the first century BC, with a seafront of about 150 meters and a large apse hall; it was in restoration at the time of the eruption of 79 AD and preserves the traces of the yard interrupted.

Set up in 2003 by the Vagabondaggi group   .On the traces of Norman Douglas in the Resource Centre of the Istituto Comprehensivo .Abate Gioacchino . documents work and domestic life on the plateau: section with materials of the Arssa Historical Archives, the cutting of wood in the woods, transhumance, the cultivation of wheat and potato and the seventeenth-century Casino Lupinacci, the first inhabited nucleus of Lagarò.
The tools, crafts and popular traditions of Romagna.
Two churches superimposed in a medieval castle.

White sandy stretches alternate with cliffs and coves reachable only by boat: the beaches of Trainiti, San Giuseppe and Sant'Irene, the Safò Bay and the Cocca cliff. The promenade looks at the Gulf of Lamezia Terme and the Aeolian archipelago.

First mentioned in 1451 in a document that mentions the church of San Martino, Velva is an example of Ligurian rural architecture: the medieval fabric has been preserved because the interior of the village is almost all pedestrian, with creuze and narrow caruggi paved in stone and arches between the houses.
Inside a barn with a straw roof.

A 17-metre-high quadrangular tower built by the Normans in the 11th century, rebuilt at the end of the 14th century and renovated several times; it was a sighting point on the Itria Valley and at the top has a statue of St. Nicholas Benedict. Next to it, the Porta Grande is the main access to the old town.
A Phoenician and Roman city overlooking the sea.
The oldest trees in Europe.
Among the residences of the village the sixteenth century Palazzo Pezzoli, the late Renaissance Palazzo Galizzi and Palazzo Mosconi.
An easy link between vineyards, fountains and volcanic geology.
MiC card (Add. 2021) sign closed and reservation required; the municipality publishes valid hours until 30/09/2026 and visits by reservation at 0722 721121

Trenches, galleries, cave stations and walkways of the Austrian defensive line, active from summer 1916 to autumn 1918, connected by a ring path. Here on June 8, 1917 at 5.30 p.m. the mine exploded under the Lunetta, killing 120 Italian soldiers and over forty officers of the Catania Brigade, on the eve of the battle of the Ortigara (10-25 June 1917).

Grey stone village on a hill on the plateau, enriched by the trade of saffron (PDO since 2005), with alleys with steps carved in the rock, the seventeenth-century Palazzo Santucci and the church of San Sebastiano; in the village of Civitatenga the monastery of Sant'Antonio and the ancient Jewish ghetto.
The nineteenth-century palace belonged to the family of the mother of Benedetto Croce, who was born there in 1866; in time it has hosted illustrious personalities.
A baroque ancone carved next to the castle.

About 300 meters from the Colosseum, two overlapping churches built on Roman buildings and on the remains of a mitre: in the upper basilica the Chapel of Saint Catherine of Masolino, in the lower one the frescoes with the "Legend of Sisinno."
Woods of holm oak and the obsidian of the prehistoric.

Beyond the Ponte dei Voltoni extends the Austro-Hungarian military district of the nineteenth century, with the former Artillery House, the long Austrian Palleria (deposit of ammunition overlooking a white marble square), the Commander's Palace and the Pavilion of the Officers, built in 1856 with brick vaults separated by an embankment of about 1.5 meters against the bombings, which can be seen from the outside along the Canale di Mezzo.

Etruscan tomb of the end of the fourth century BC dug into the tuff of a wooded hill on the Montacchione stream, belonged to the aristocratic family of the Hescanas: dromos of about 16 meters, vestibule with two doors, double sloping ceiling and counter with two sarcophagi in pepper. The walls preserve a funeral banquet, a procession and winged spirit figures; it is indicated as the only Etruscan tomb of Umbria with the original paintings.
Porta quoted from 1290, perhaps the oldest of the walls, used as a prison of Andreas Hofer; just above the Powder Tower, rest of a fourteenth-century castle.
A Roman mosaic inside a baroque church.
The sacred mountain of the Montallesi and the view of the valley.

The feudal castle stands on the top of the mountain around which the village developed; enlarged in Norman times, probably for the Count of Caserta Roberto di Lauro, had square plan, fortified walls and towers and was made of stone and tuff; it was severely damaged by the earthquake of 1456. The walls, the main square tower and some smaller buildings remain.
Skiing, trekking and biking park on Catria.
Pinacoteca housed in the Town Hall which exhibits oil paintings and graphic works by the contemporary Reggiolese artist Antonio Ruggero Giorgi.
An old-fashioned printery.

Camporgiano, on the right bank of the Serchio between the Apuan Alps and the Apennines, was from 1446 until the unification of Italy dominion of the Este, which left the Fortress with the Civic collection of Renaissance ceramics. The municipality is crossed by the Via del Volto Santo and houses churches with wooden sculptures of Pisano, in Camporgiano and in the hamlet of Puglianella.
Birthplace of Piero della Francesca and Luca Pacioli, closed by the walls with the fortress of Giuliano da Sangallo.
In the female castle of the Malatestiana Rocca, the life of the Romagna countryside over time, with tools and reconstructions.
Mill of the seventeenth century, today museum, where millstones operated by the water of the King's vase still grind the cereals, including polenta flour.
The synagogue was built in 1672 and rebuilt by Pietro Marchelli in 1858 in the ancient ghetto, today restored by the municipality as a place of culture.

Two panoramic points signalled by the Municipality: the Belvedere Caduti in Mare, in via Guglielmo Marconi, looks at the islands of Procida, Ischia and Ventotene; the Belvedere Supor Mundi, in via Panoramica, embraces the coast from Capo Miseno to Punta Campanella.
The Black Christ of the Rites of Holy Week.
In the 19th-century covered market: finds from the Neolithic to the post-Renaissance age, including the wheel of the Lagoni di Mercurago, Golasecca's sets and the Celtic necropolis of Dormelletto.
At sunset, from the invaded park, the reflection in the water.

On the first floor of the Palazzo de' Pizzini there are antique pianos linked to Mozart, Schubert, Beethoven and Chopin, from the private collection of the pianist Temenuschka Vesselinova. It is not open to the general public: visits for groups of at least five people by reservation.
Along the channels.

Dedicated to the patron saint of Solarino, it was built from 1764 on commission of the feudator, under the direction of the foreman Siracusan Luciano Ali; stopped the work for the economic difficulties of the client, it was carried out with the voluntary work of the population. Opened entirely to worship in 1853, when facade and interior were not yet finished, it was consecrated on February 19, 1938 and renovated in the seventies and eighties.
Inaugurated in 1929, with iron structure, stucco and black and white mosaic floor; it houses shops and cafes.
Natural oasis with pre-Roman walls, remains of the acropolis and a medieval fortress, with views of the valley.

Country of the Val d'Incarojo, since 2022 in the network of Villages of the mountaineers: Palazzo Calice Screm, prototype of the Carnic house, and the eighteenth-century Palazzo Linussio Fabiani, the collection of musical instruments of Mozartina, the church of San Vito and Santa Maria Maggiore in Dierico, with the mountains and Lake Dimon around.
The symbol of Oliena, for trained hikers.
Landscape of vineyards of Monferrato to turn on foot or by bike.
The palace where Händel played.
The Mannerist fountain of the Castles.
Not always open: check timetables and access with the cemetery office before visiting

Near one of the springs is the Funtanazza, a rectangular medieval reservoir of about 17 by 8 meters, which contained about 1,200 cubic meters of water. The presence of stairs, not accessible to people with disabilities.
About 5,000 hectares of chalk and calanchi at the gates of Bologna, part of the UNESCO site on karst in the evaporites.

Founded by Peter of Angelerius, the future Pope Celestine V, and from 1293 Celestine's mother house; rebuilt after the earthquake of 1706, it was imprisoned from 1868 to 1993. You can visit the 18th century church on the Courtyard of the Platani, the stone staircase of the Maiella and the refectory painted in 1717-1719.
The truffle trail.
Monumental rocks in the canyon.
The stone village of the Barbagia di Seulo.
Between June and July the lavender meadows flourish at the entrance of the village; in occitan the lavender is called ""izop" and "Demonte" is compared to a corner of Provence.

Wanted in 1534 by Vicero Don Pedro of Toledo at the highest point of the city: square plan, high bastions and a 14 meters deep and 23 m wide moat; in the bastion on the right of the entrance the mammoth skeleton, currently closed for restoration.
Terracotta sketches, plasters, drawings and engravings by the sculptor and Modena painter Giuseppe Graziosi (1879-1942), on the ground floor of the Palazzo dei Musei.
The giant bench no. 261 in the Monte Menola Park offers views of the abbey of Montecassino, the lower valley of Liri, the area of Cassino and southern Lazio.
A small country church linked to popular devotion.

Just outside the village, the Franciscan monastery of 1589 has a cloister decorated with a 1618 pictorial cycle on the life of St. Francis; next to the Baroque church of the Immaculate Conception, a single nave with a barrel vault, with on the main altar a large painting of the Virgin of the Flemish Spranger.

In the center the castle of the thirteenth century, now seat of the Municipality, the fifteenth-century church of Sant'Agostino and palaces such as Palazzo Lomellini, Casa Cavassa and the House of the Meridians; there is also a synagogue.
One of the most beautiful libraries in the world.
the MiC card indicates that the enhancement project plans to expose it in the stables of the building to make it accessible: use to verify
The glacial valley of the Park, within family reach.

Remains of an 8th century abbey where St Romualdo (1011) and St. Pier Damiani (1042) stayed, remained autonomous until the 11th century, then passed under the influence of Fonte Avellana. Nearby is a small Roman bridge.

Balbido, which tradition wants refuge of witches (at the entrance of the valley were erected five iron crosses, one still visible), has the façades of the houses painted by the itinerant group murals naïf: today are 222 works with a naive technique or graffito, with themes such as the legend of witches, the dream of the chimney sweep, the stories of grandmothers and the palio of the horses of Santa Giustina.
The queen's falcon fjord.

The crenellated walls of about 1700-1800 meters with 24 torrents and the doors Vicentina, Bassanese and Breganzina, built from 1372 under Cansignorio della Scala; the round path, at 8-12 meters above sea level, runs with harness starting from the Tower of the Compagnia delle Mura.

The capital between Piave and Ardo at the foot of the Dolomites, the only capital with part of the territory in a national park: Piazza dei Martiri, the Duomo of Tullio Lombardo with the bell tower of Juvarra and Nevegal.
Sculpted double-fores of the woolenware.

Stone houses and granite paved streets around Corso Niccolò Ferracciu, Carrera Longa and Viale Roma; among the buildings the Palazzu Mannu, example of Gallura's architecture of the Sabauda era, the Fountain Nuova in local granite and the church of Sant'Anna of 1665, in granite, with a nineteenth-century painting of the saint.
Five centuries of Genoese damask, from the frame to the fabric.
The old fishing port with its small beach, the 70-metre pier and Porta Pescara, the last of the four medieval gates, with colorful boats on the sand.

It housed the corpses of 1036 imperial soldiers, exhumed in 1965 and transferred to the ossuary of Citadella. He was abandoned for years, was recovered in 2006 and renamed "Monument to Concord and Peace."
The parish of Pallanza.
A rare nuraghe is a corridor that can be visited.
The Piceni and Roman Asculum.
The oldest and most popular church in the country.

In the nineteenth-century Villino Lorenzoni, it is also the center of the Agno-Chiampo Museum System; twelve rooms, five of archaeology, from prehistory to the early Middle Ages with mainly ceramics of the Bronze and Roman Ages, and seven of natural sciences, mainly paleontology and mineralogy. Times indicated: Saturday 15-18.30, Sunday 9.30-12.30 and 15-18.30.
Malatestian history and war in one place.
A unique Venetian military architecture.

Symbol of the village, of the 11th century, Romanesque with Gothic influences: the crypt is decorated with figures of Apostles, Doctors of the Church and founders of Orders, and the church houses sixteenth-century tables and frescoes.
The Roman Concord in a 19th-century museum.
The mud that boils, healing for centuries.

Maso built in the second half of the eighteenth century by the rich family Spilzi, unique example of alpine settlement between noble residence and fortified complex: buildings around a deep court, west side protected by high walls with walkway, barn gate with wounds for the ropes of a drawbridge. The barn hosts temporary exhibitions and cultural events. It can also be reached on foot through the Ecken Biotope.
Convent built by the Capuchins in 1579, just outside the village.
The castle on the highest point.
The Mastio Scalagero on the border between Mantua and Verona.
View from the Gulf to Vesuvius from an Amalfi fortress.
Cycling in the villas.
The rare tree park.

The island is about 50 km2 and 110 km of coast which is part of the municipality of Porto Torres: it was quarantine station, penal colony and prison camp in the Great War, and since 1997 it is national park, with marine protected area since 2002. The white donkey, symbol of the island, mouflons, wild boars and horses live in the wild; it is turned by train, jeep, bus or bicycle along the 25 km road, while Cala Sant'Andrea is a complete reserve with forbidden access. The crossings start from Porto Torres and Stintino.
2,500-year-old wall with a view of the plain.
The first Italian museum to promote a public collection of modern art, born in 1863: four floors from the nineteenth century to the contemporary.
Beach and bike.

Erected between 1922 and 1924 as a sacred enclosure with a bronze copy of the Alata Victory of Brescia, it was then expanded with the ossuary that houses the remains of 847 Italian soldiers, eight Austro-Hungarian soldiers and, in a crypt, five unknown soldiers found in 1964 on the Lobbia Alta glacier. Since 1983 the Ministry of Defense has entrusted its care to the Municipality of Ponte di Legno.
The Otricoli Jupiter and the Medusa mosaic seen closely.

Palace where Felice Peretti lived, today the seat of the Reliquary of Montalto (Imago Pietatis and Scenes of the Passion), masterpiece of Parisian goldsmiths and precious stones donated by Sixto V to the city in 1587, the second year of the pontificate; the Region indicates it currently visitable.
Ass-back bridge built in 1740.
Erice's largest viewpoint.

Park of about 33 hectares in the south-eastern part of the municipality, on the border with Cernusco, obtained from a sand and gravel quarry active since the sixties: the environmental recovery began in 1985 and in 1987 the area passed to the Municipality. The lake occupies just under half of the park; there are cycle paths and two parking lots.
The Sardinian fauna up close, with deer and deer in front of the door.

Established by regional law of 27 March 2019 at the request of the Municipality, it exceeds 5,000 hectares and coincides with the municipal territory, between 600 and 1,669 meters of Monte Legnà, with the peaks of Monte Carmo, Antola and Porreio. More than three quarters of the area are beech and chestnut woods; there are arid grasslands rich in orchids, species of Alpine wrecks, the southern tulip, a stable population of wolves, six species of bats and 94 species of butterflies. It is described as the only example in Piedmont of Mediterranean-mountain silvo-pastoral habitat.
Large cisterns dug into the rock by the 2nd Partic Legion to supply the field with water: five naves on 36 pillars, capacity of about 10,000 m3, still functioning and fed by Roman pipelines.
From above, the city and the Sangro valley.
Small bays edged with lava rocks.

In the old Episcopal Palace, with a renovated route in 2024, it contains about 150 sacred works of art saved from the abandoned churches of Sabina: an eighteenth-century canopy in Chinese style commissioned by Cardinal Annibale Albani, the standard processional painted on two sides by Plautilla Bricci, silver processional crosses (the oldest of 1306) and a room of the masters of the sabino baroque like Vincenzo Manenti and Girolamo Topo.
On the wide Galluppi, among Baroque buildings, the church preserves a chapel of the fourteenth century.
Industrial archaeology and nature.
The 9th century crypt with Byzantine frescoes.
A walk between art and nature.
A baroque façade out of the ordinary.
Squares and palaces of a Savoy-Carignano city.

On the hill of Genna Maria, about 400 meters, the original tower of the fifteenth century BC was surrounded in the thirteenth century by a four-tower bastion with courtyard and well partly dug into the rock, then by an ante-mural with six towers; between bastion and ante-mural rose in the early Iron Age a village abandoned in the eighth century BC. From the 4th century BC, mast and courtyard became a place of worship, with about 600 votive lamps, until the 7th century A.D. From the top the view ranges from the Gulf of Cagliari to the Gulf of Oristano to the Gennargentu.
Visitable with the castle, inhabited by the last owner of the manor.
The villa of Elisa Baciocchi, sister of Napoleon and lady of Lucca, which gave her the present appearance in the nineteenth century, with its large park.
An intact noble residence in Friuli, with its paintings.
A city of textiles from the elegant medieval old town, with the Duomo of Filippo Lippi and Donatello, the only Swabian castle in the centre-north and the Pecci Centre for Contemporary Art.
The daily life of a 4th century BC Latin colony
The senator's village.
A Roman dwelling outside the walls.
Contemporary art in the old market.
Dedicated to the Body of Christ and to San Bernardino da Siena, it houses a Madonna and Child of the late fourteenth century and a reliquary belonging to the same Saint Bernardino.
Hiking in a Biosphere Reserve.

At the entrance of the village the source dated from an inscription to 1265; the neighboring underground tunnels form the Water Path, which can be visited by reservation at the municipal tourist office.

The high village, rebuilt quickly after the earthquake of 1783, rich in picturesque views, with the small garden  "U chianu" used for shows and conferences and, not far away, the statue of San Gerardo Maiella.

Domus de janas neolithic excavated in low calcareous outcrop in an oak wood on the slopes of Mount Corona 'e Teula, identified by Hercules Contu in 1969 and excavated since 1984; the Tomb Major has 21 environments with triple corniform pattern, false doors and double sloping ceiling, the Tomb of the Clessiddre owes its name to the geometric motifs of the antecella.
The stone of Matese in the heart of the country.
Hot water used by the Romans.
Eufronio's crater at home.
The 13th-century mast with Mount Vettore in front.

Medieval village of Roman origin in the Sabbia Valley, 778 meters on the road between the lake of Idro, Maniva and the plain of the Gaver, known for the Carnival, transhumance and cheese Bagòss: in the center the parish church of San Giorgio, known as the cathedral between the mountains of San Rocco, with frescoes fifteenth century and the Via dei Portici.

The village was formerly a bulwark guarding the valleys of Bussento and Mingardo; in the chapel of the castle the effigy of the Virgin is venerated to which is attributed the "Glorious" added to the name of Rocca.

Among the most populated villages of the Valle San Martino, on the banks of the Adda, Calolziocorte preserves the Monastery of Santa Maria del Lavello, founded by the Servants of Mary at the end of the fifteenth century, and the church of San Martino with its high portico; from the village start the cycle path along the river and the paths to Valcava and Mount Treasure.
A corner of Holland in the lagoon fishing valleys.
The Franciscan cycle of the cloister.
A Luca Giordano in Val Borbera.
The fortress in the rock and the view from the tower.
Church of Borghetto, neoclassical reconstruction of 1759 of a Romanesque church of the 11th century dedicated to Santa Maria; it contains two frescoes from the fourteenth century.

Municipality of western Lessinia, Sant'Anna d'Alfaedo is linked to the Ponte di Veja, the natural arch of about 40 meters that tradition brings to Dante and that Mantegna painted in the Chamber of Sposi, and to the Palaeontological and Prehistoric Museum, where is exposed a Cretodus fossil shark from the quarries of the Stone of Prun; on Mount Treasure stands a fort today owned by the municipality.
Museum-workshop of artistic stained glass.

The 14th-century Fortress houses the Enoteca del Consorzio dei Vini Colli Lanuvini, the best place to taste the wines of the area, a small museum of rural traditions and the watchtower, symbol of the village, with panoramic views.
Nineteenth-century stuccoes and high reliefs.

Designed by engineer Pietro Pernigotti and inaugurated on May 2, 1838, it has three orders of stages, the curtain of Luigi Vacca with Orpheus and Eurydice and the medallion of the Muse on the ceiling; closed in 1952, was reopened after the restoration on May 2, 1990.

Hosted since 2013 in the sixteenth century Palazzo Pretorio, it tells the archive that since 1984 collects diaries, letters and memories of ordinary people. Four rooms: an installation of cupboards and drawers to be opened to listen to and see selected stories, the corner dedicated to Saverio Tutino, the Room Rabito on the autobiography of the street Ragusano Vincenzo Rabito beat by car, and the room of the sheet on which the peasant mantua Clelia Marchi wrote her own life.
Built in the 11th century on a raised hill near the river Oglio, it preserves an altarpiece with the patron saint.

House with arched windows and internal garden along via Landolfi, inserted in the Network of the Historical Houses of Lazio; here Montale visited his friend Landolfi in 1937, before writing the Elegia of Pico Farnese. The writer, who died in Ronciglione, is buried in Pico.

Exhibition halls at the end of the eighties in the former barn of Villa Soranzo; since 1993, with the artist Ausilio Cattaneo, they host an intense activity of exhibitions, with artists of international and local importance. It was named on 22 February 2009 at the Councillor Cesare Belossi and resumed its activity in 2019 with a new management committee. It does not have a permanent collection: we visit it on the occasion of temporary exhibitions.

In a fifteenth-century building on three levels along Via San Francesco: religious iconography and expressionism in painting, sculpture, lithography and engraving, with works by Valerio Trubbiani and emerging artists. The interior is inaccessible after the earthquake of 2016; it remains a path for images.
In the Hall of Jupiter of Palazzo Bentivoglio, documents, paintings, sculptures and engravings of the Naïf painter who lived in Gualtieri, including a Gorilla and a self-portrait.
From the cathedral a spectacular view of the plain of Palermo.

The granite overlooks walls, paved walls, alleys and squares; historical toponyms such as the Aldia, an ancient guard and toll booth, and the Piazza di li Baddhi, the square of the dances are found. The stone houses are considered one of the most beautiful in Gallura.

A path that descends from the village to the hamlet of Intermesoli (770 meters), an ancient hamlet of wool in the woods, passing through the public wash-house, the remains of the church of the Madonna and the old mill on the Rio Arno; in Intermesoli the churches of Santa Maria, San Lorenzo and San Rocco, with the parish church from the Baroque altars, and in October the chestnut festival.
Alleys, arches, noble palaces and four castle doors that tell the medieval past.
The Lombard Gothic overlooking Piazza Cavalli.
History and traditions of the village told in a contemporary key on the walls of the village.
Vigliaturo glass in the palace of princes.
A protected wetland with rare species.
The herons in the Tronto valley.
The Giants of Mont'e Prama.
The church of Purgatory, dating back to 1631 and with a remarkable façade, is now home to the Museum of Sacred Art.
The art gallery in a Palladio palace.
Open only Tuesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 8.30-19.30 (VisitLatium, from 6 November 2023)

In the Palazzo Celestini, in the heart of the historic center, tells the local ceramic manufacture favored by clay deposits, from the falisco period to the modern age: excavations from 1984-1985, pieces of the factory  "Ceramica Bassanello" (active until 1978) donated by the Misciatelli family and statues of Giulio Francesconi. Vasanello is with Civita Castellana the most famous town of Tuscia for ceramics, and its potters are called "cocciari" (cocciari).
The parish church of the twentieth century has a Latin cross with an elegant portico; in front of it stands Villa Bernabei, a half-nineteenth-century residence.

White church from the red roof on the slopes of Mount Lancia, above the village, documented by 1312; in 1485 the hermit Bergamo Baldessarre de Pluzana rebuilt it to live there, with the permission of the prince bishop John Hinderbach and the support of the communities of Rendena, and was guarded by a hermit until 1850. Inside, prayer benches and a small altar with a painting of St. Martin.

Borgo dei Monti Northern Dauni at 654 meters, near Mount Cornacchia, with the Mother Church of 1507, the Arch of the Earth, the alleys of the stonemasons, the still active straw oven and, at the slopes, two nineteenth century water mills restored with the Museum of Ancient Art.

Castello dei Malaspina from the twelfth century, strengthened in the thirteenth century and transformed by Alberico I into a Renaissance residence with a new body in the sixteenth century; baroque façade of the seventeenth century and, since 1805, seat of the Academy of Fine Arts; in front of the monument to the Carrara sculptor Pietro Tacca.
Imperial Rome underfoot.

Dedicated in 1983 by the Municipality to migrants, the work of the architect Mario Montalto; the country, more than 4,000 inhabitants in 1960, has today about 2,000 of them after the waves migrating to the Americas and Europe.

In the historic centre, with a pre-Roman section and a Roman section on the ancient Lanuvium: a Augustan fresco with a Dionysian theme, marble fragments of the group of Licinio Murena (first century BC), a parapet with winged grifo of the Antonian age from the theatre, archaic and Hellenistic architectural plates and votive from the Sanctuary of Juno Sospita and the former anatomical vows of the Pantanacci cave, linked to the cult of the serpent of the goddess. The remains of the ancient balineum are incorporated into the exhibition spaces; the epigraphic section includes an inscription of the third century BC by Lucio Ocra on the bathroom works.
The Brettii of Cosenza.

Late-Gothic environment entirely frescoed in the cylindrical tower of the current town hall, once Castello Sottono, a favourite residence of the Marquises of Saluzzo; the pictorial cycle of the early sixteenth century was wanted by Margherita di Foix.
the museum is not accessible: building in general renovation (the site of the Municipality)
The sacred wood of Diana on the lake.
The museum dedicated to the symbol of Calabrian cuisine.

Iron mine mentioned already in 1819, gathered in 1870 in the Società S. Aloisio, passed in 1886 to Terni and then to the Tassara Group, which since the 1930s transformed it into a modern mining site; closed in 1984, it is reopened to the public in 2003. You enter with guide, helmet and torch for about 2.5 km of tunnels (8-10 °C, very high humidity: warm clothes and hiking shoes) between roasting ovens and miners' tools; there is also an adventure park suspended in the gallery, 85% indoor. Open from the end of April to October (Sundays; in summer Saturdays and Sundays; every day from 8 to 23 August), 10-12.30 and 14-17.30, mandatory booking; not accessible to disabled people.
The furnishings of Enotri and Lucani and the Roman statues of Athena.

The clock tower of 1212, rebuilt in the fifteenth century, next to the gate of San Lorenzo in 1250: collapsed with the earthquake of 2012, with the dial of the broken clock in the middle became the symbol of the earthquake.
One of the oldest Romanesque bell towers on the lake.
An intact alpine village, suitable for families.
Built with materials of Roman buildings, damaged by the earthquake of 1456 and largely rebuilt after that of 1805.
Opened in 2015, the center dedicated to Italian and international photography.
A fortified residence in the heart of the country, today city hall.
The scientific instruments of the Medici and Lorraine: the telescopes and relics of Galileo, globes, watches and machines.

Founded by Byzantine monks and rebuilt in the mid-nineteenth century, it is dedicated to the patron saint of miners; around it grew the most recent part of the country. The feast takes place at the beginning of June and is repeated on July 10 along with the goat festival; the faithful reached the sanctuary for a long path in the woods.
The wrought iron author in a unique gallery in Italy.

Set up in the former barn to protect sacred works of art of the nearby churches, after the thefts of the sixties and seventies: among these a Madonna enthroned in 1430 and the original statues of the altar of San Nicolò di Caminata.
A small museum linked to the history of medicine in Valnerina.
The castle from which the village was born.
Testimonials of the mining and industrial past related to lime and cement.
The two ancient gates of access to the village, the Melangolo Gate and the Olive Gate, enter the center built in dark basalt around the castle.

According to the historian Iacobilli founded in 1017 by San Romualdo, who spent the last years there; of the ward remains the Romanesque church in square stone to T, with an ogival barrel vault, altar in travertine of the thirteenth century on 14 columns and a crypt straight from a single column with Corinthian capital, perhaps of the sixth century. Reduced to the farmhouse after 1861, it returned to the monks of Fonte Avellana and was restored in 1972.

Mill still in operation, where are found flour ground with natural stone. In the village also the bread of the Roofs cooked in the wood-burning oven and the Dranoresi, chocolate praline with rum liqueur cream.
In the background of the Château Blanc glacier, with views of the Mont Blanc profile.

Cittadina della Bisiacaria seat of the regional airport: the neoclassical Villa Vicentini Miniussi with the photo library of the Monfalconese Cultural Consortium, the Roman villa discovered in 1987 with its Antiquarium and, on the Karst, Mount Six Busi of the Great War.
A place of silence on the hills.
The Madonna of the Impolata.
The baptistery of the Aryan cult of Theodoric, octagonal and now partly underground, with a baptism of Christ in the dome to be compared with that of Neonian.

Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Pieve, about 3 km from the village in the valley of the Erro, before the Mille and practically rebuilt in 1694, destination of pilgrimages, with avenues that go up to a Via Crucis. The stone portal is by G. B. Solar; on the main altar a Renaissance statue of the Madonna, the vault and the apse frescoed in 1859 by Tomaso Ivaldi of Toleto, canvases of the seventeenth-seventh century in the lateral altars and a silver reliquary of the Astigian goldsmith Bernardino Badino. Free access during functions.

Fortified house built in 1458 by Lucrezia d'Alagno, beloved of King Alfonso I of Aragon, who withdrew there after the death of the king; rises outside the Aragonese walls, just behind the Casamale, in front of Mount Somma. He replaced a more ancient castle near Santa Maria a Castello; among the subsequent owners was Prince De Curtis (Totò), and in 1998 he bought it to make it a museum and library.

A small single nave chapel in Palazzo Tondi-Vignola, built in 1789 where a well was the destination of those who had been bitten by poisonous animals. Until a few decades ago, at the dawn of June 29, the feast of Saints Peter and Paul, arrived there the "tarantate" to ask for healing and drink the water of the well: a ritual linked to the origins of the pinch. On the altar, after a long restoration, the canvas of Saint Paul by Francesco Saverio Lillo is back. Info: IAT Galatina, tel. +39 0836 569984.

Municipality of the Macerata Apennines linked to the Da Varano di Camerino, with the octagonal church of Santa Maria di Varano, the sanctuary of the Madonna of Col di Venti, the hermitage of Blessed Rizzerio and the villages of Massaprofoglio and Costafiore. According to the regional portal historic center, monuments and museums are partially usable.

Born in the fourteenth century on an oratory of the 11th century and built on the site of a Roman basilica (remaining visible at the apse in Via Colonna), it was transformed by the Cesi and restored in 1761; a single nave with eight chapels and works from the late sixteenth to the late eighteenth century. In the funeral chapel of the Cesi rests Frederick Cesi       ...

The heart of the city, overlooking the medieval Palazzo dei Capitani del Popolo, the Church of San Francesco, the Loggia dei Mercanti of the sixteenth century and the Caffè Meletti; there you run the Quintana on the first Sunday of August.

The ancient Akragas founded in 581 BC: the Valley of the Temples UNESCO heritage with the Temple of Concord, the Garden of the Kolymbethra and the Museum Pietro Griffo; on the hill the Arab and Norman city with the cathedral of San Gerlando, Santa Maria dei Greci and Santo Spirito; at the Chaos the birthplace of Pirandello.

On the plateau overlooking the artificial lake of Licodia, about 5 km from the village, a small late Roman sepulchre (end IV-inizi V century A.D.) of about forty were covered with sandstone, on the right bank of the Dirillo, partly covered by the waters of the dam Ragoleto.
The oldest tombs in Montiferru.
One of the most evocative ancient cities in Sicily.
A circular village with medieval towers and houses, enclosed by fifteenth-century walls.

The historic centre rises along the ridge; the medieval walls, which had about twenty towers and four gates, remain Porta dei Greci (or Porta Ecana), Porta Nuova opened in the fifteenth century and part of Porta San Giovanni near San Domenico, with the Fontana Nuova in Piazza Mazzini. On November 1st the village is filled with the carved pumpkins of the festival "Fucacoste e cocce priatorje" .

The Etruscan Caere: the necropolis of the Banditaccia excavated in tuff, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004 with Tarquinia, the national museum in the castle of the Ruspoli with the crater of Eufronio, and in the surroundings the village of Ceri and the waterfalls of the Ceriti mountains.
Maragliano and Bocciardo in the parish of Vado.
The peasant life of Lomellina in two thousand objects.
A ghost country around the cathedral.

The Pontis stretch of the route to Sotto il Monte (paths 897 and 891, locality Il Canto) starts from the cemetery, runs along the Vallette with their streams and rises among woods of chestnuts, ash trees and wild cherry trees, passing through the sixteenth-century farmhouse of San Bartolomeo with its large bell tower and the church of Santa Barbara, the only surviving building of an ancient village on a plateau. The whole route measures 8.1 km, 2 h 45 min, +340 m, difficulty And with some steep stretches.

Born as a hunting casino of the noble Mozzoni (first body before 1440), it was enlarged after 1530 and in 1559 decorated with frescoes by the brothers Campi di Cremona and their school; from the marriage of the daughter of Ascanio Mozzoni with Giovan Pietro Cicogna was born the family Cicogna Mozzoni, whose descendants still manage it. U-shaped plant with courtyard and Doric colonnade in Viggiù stone, twelve frescoed and furnished rooms (dance halls, four-poster beds, coffered ceilings, library). The Italian terrace garden wanted by Ascanio in 1560, with fish pond, double row cypresses, fountain with mask and secret garden, continues beyond the viewpoint in the romantic park. Season 2026 from 29 March to 25 October, Sunday and holidays 9.30-12 and 14.30-19; groups over 20 people also weekdays by reservation.
Requalified park hosting outdoor art exhibitions.

On the ground floor of the former convent of San Domenico: works from the early twentieth century to the seventies by artists such as Grumo, Chieco, Di Terlizzi, Sacco, Brandonisio and van Westerhout, and the graphic collection by Domenico Singer with aquariums, etchings and lithographs; space for exhibitions and cloisters for events.

Inaugurated on 16 September 2000 in Palazzo Polcenigo-Fanna, it gathers about 400 photographs, documents and objects in twelve sections on the emigration of workers in western Friuli, the "Pal Mont": flows and destinations, crafts such as mosaicists and terraces, work abroad and life of communities emigrated, with a path curated by Javier P. You're big. A room is dedicated to the drawing school of Cavasso with elaborates by master Ernesto Calligaro. Managed by ERPAC; open Thursday and Friday 10-13, Saturday and Sunday 10-13 and 15-17.

Reserve of 19.8 hectares established in 1995 and managed by CAI Sicilia, which protects the cave and part of the Rocca di Entella, isolated chalky outcrop: the cavity, excavated in the macro-crystalline plasters of the Messinian, develops on three levels of tunnels for over 700 meters, with chalky and carbonate cavings and rare iron-manganesive deposits; on the surface dolines and karrens, rock vegetation and steppe, bats and raptors nesting on the walls.

One of the most important Etruscan centers: the necropolis of Monterozzi with painted tombs, UNESCO heritage since 2004, the Alati Cavalli of Palazzo Vitelleschi and the medieval town of the towers, between the salt pans and the sea.

The lake, once the largest in Tuscany, was drained with works begun at the time of Cosimo I and with the reclamation of Leopoldo di Lorena between 1824 and 1859; today it is a vast agricultural plain between Monti Pisani and Cerbaie, and the drain has returned Etruscan and Roman remains.
In the Masseria district, a cubic building of Byzantine style.
The heart of the historic centre, with a spectacular brick façade.
To see the mosaic as today's art language.
Axel Munthe's house above the sea.

Municipal Gallery dedicated to the artist and critic Filippo Scroppo, who curated contemporary art exhibitions from 1949 to 1991; preserves a civic collection of Italian contemporary art since the 1950s, presented with annual exhibitions, and hosts the festival "Una Torre d'Arte."
A 17th century convent church.
It preserves a marble ancon with 23 bas-reliefs on the life of Jesus, work of Gian Domenico Gagini dated 1542.

Well FAI since 2012: the Romanesque church with façade in hut, rosette and portal in Lecce stone houses Byzantine frescoes; around a farm with mill, oven and mill.
One of the most characteristic streets of the center, with the arcades and the ancient taverns of the city, between Ponte Nuovo and Sant'Anastasia.

Sulcitan farmhouse of the early 20th century in the center of the village, with bedroom, dining room, kitchen and anteroom furnished, a wooden frame still working and tools for weaving, dyeing of wool and processing of linen; in the courtyard with the well the tools for cultivation, bread, wine and breeding, plus a room on the local handicrafts. On the morning of the Marriage the bride dresses there.

Consecrated on March 16, 1113, rebuilt after the Turkish invasion of 1558 and made baroque around 1700; of the fourteenth century remains the portal with two columns of pink marble. Inside the fountain where Torquato Tasso was baptized, with reliefs attributed to Andrea Pisano, the pulpit of 1573, the paintings of the Malinconico (1711), the choir inlaid by Sorrento artisans (1936) and a fifteenth-century Nativity of Sienese taste. The bell tower rests on four ancient columns and has on top the watch in 18th century majolica.
opening only with mandatory booking

A thousand roses in front of the Palatine.
The Romanesque cathedral of Lanfranco and Wiligelmo consecrated in 1106, with the reliefs of Genesis on the facade, the Porta della Pescheria and the crypt of St Geminiano.

The village is known for its brown, roasted on the fire in the traditional pan at the festival of late October; in the table polenta with truffle, sheep sauces, goat and sheep cheese and the Cesanese del Piglio DOCG.
From 1878 to the upper floors of the Palazzo dei Priori, it is considered among the most prestigious Italian art museums, with numerous paintings by Pietro Vannucci, the Perugino, and his students.

Born in the seventies from the collections of fossils and minerals donated by enthusiasts (Geo-Paleontological Group Vogherese), it has sections of zoology (birds including flamingos, herons and raptors), paleontology with a humerus of plesiosaur found at Zavattarello and a skull of Megaceros, mineralogy with 221 samples on display and a botanical section in preparation. It is located in the former Cavalry.
