A hermitage in the rock above the valley of Sacco.
An unusual mining landscape.
The battlefield that ideally opens the Risorgimento.
Created at the end of the nineteenth century by Onorato VII Caetani with Mediterranean and exotic species; prehistoric traces were found in the area of Villa Fogliano.
The MiC card (updated 2020) indicates closed every day, while the site of the Municipality says visitable every day from 9 to 12; contact tel. 0827 96066
The peasant life of Langa told by the country itself.
A natural swimming pool in the green.
Walk under the arcades of Via Emilia.

Walking path of medium-low difficulty, with about 400 steps and about an hour of walk, which connects Minori and Maiori passing from the village of Torre to the church of San Michele, between lemon gardens (including the Sfusato Amalfi, lemon IGP Costa d'Amalfi) and views of the promontory between the two countries.
Inside the fortress, dedicated to the local tradition of straw weave: it preserves baskets, kitchen utensils and straw dolls, wicker and natural materials.
Clear sea at the foot of the abbey.

The Monte Capoliveri, in the Tuscan Archipelago National Park, offers hiking and biking trails with wide views; the Monte Calamita Exploring route proposed by Visit Tuscany is about 12 km and 6 hours, and the paths of Capoliveri Bike Park cross the mountain.
The nineteenth-century chessboard bari.
Roman theatre and amphitheatre in the mountains.
Look at the stars under a petal dome.
The remains of the early Christian basilica of Santa Tecla and the baptisteries of Santo Stefano and San Giovanni alle Fonti are located under the cathedral and the churchyard.
The valley of the stars.
A little church of shepherds with a view.
16th century church with pseudo-Romanesque bell tower, indicated by Turismo Torino among the main points of interest of the village.
The adventure path in the underground: cisterns under eighteenth-century arches, shelters of the Second World War and a final stretch in the raft on the slope.

Dedicated to the physician and scholar of antiquity Vincenzo Laviola, it traces the population of the High Ionian from the indigenous cultures of Bronze and Iron to Greek colonization. It exhibits the collection Laviola (metal objects and protohistoric ceramics of the XII-VIII century BC) and the findings of the excavations of the Superintendence coordinated by Juliette de la Genière: necropolis of Paladino and Mangosa and archaic settlement of St. Nicholas (late VII-VI century BC, about 20 hectares), from which come over a thousand weights from the frame, some with female names in achean alphabet. Two multimedia stations in four languages.

Small church in the woods in Vicaretto district, annexed in Norman times to a Basilian cenobio (founded in 1090): Romanesque exterior with rose window and ogival portal, remains of Byzantine frescoes inside. The forest of Vicaretto is suitable for walks.
Alpine railway station Orange Flag at the confluence of Vermenagna and San Giovanni, with a historic center in stone and wood almost intact around the Gothic San Pietro in Vincoli.

The Park of the springs of Timone, a tributary of the Flower, has over a thousand plant species, including the rare Etruscan artemisia and the saintly, and 39 species of wild orchids; there is a waterfall and old hydraulic pumps that supplied Cellere. Along the path of the brigand you will meet the Grotto of Mercareccia, the hideout of Tiburzi and his companions; the  "Sentiero bandito" (Whipped Path), marked and in five stages, starts from the museum and crosses the park to Pianiano.
To be combined with the Paper Museum.
The parish church of the village.
The '900s pompei, open-air memory of the war.

Municipality of the lower Val di Susa at the entrance of the valley, where remain the ruins of the castle of the Count Verde (Château of Caprie) linked to the Longobard Churches; on the mountain of the valley of Grave, between Mocchie and Frassinere, the ethnographic museum        . La Ghindana , the rock engravings and the parish church of Santo Stefano, while in the former Officine Moncenisio is located the Museo valsusino della Resistance.

Borgo del Pinerolese of Roman foundation that preserves the walls of Filippo d'Acaja with tower and four doors, fifteenth-century houses with gothic windows in terracotta, the church of San Donato of 1220 and the chapel of the frescoed Boschetto; it houses the Regional Museum of Migration and the Museum of Gusto.
The devotion to Saint Anne under the castle of Letters.
A "spring ritual" of Valconca.
One of the wooden masterpieces of Trentino.

The origins date back to the 9th century, when there was a Benedictine monastic cell of which remain sculptures in Longobard-Carolinge interweaving; the current building is from 1120 and the Baroque façade was added after the earthquake of 1695. It preserves frescoes of the XVI-XVII centuries restored in 2017 (Saints Paul, Andrea and John the Baptist), the Annunciation of Jerome Topo, pupil of Carlo Maratti, coming from the convent of the Clarisses, a Deposition and the Decollation of the Baptist; since 1855 it preserves the relics of Saint Procolo.
For local history.

Casino of hunting commissioned in 1629 by Cardinal Girolamo Colonna, with a tomb dug into the rock attributed to Gneo Scipione Ispalo (176 BC). It is only admired from the outside: today it hosts hospitality, catering and events.
Rebuilt in the mid-eighteenth century and consecrated on June 3, 1794.

The two adjacent squares of the medieval heart: that of the Cisterna, triangular, with the well in the center and the houses-towers around, and Piazza Duomo with the Collegiata and the public buildings.
16th century church on the Palazzo di Città, with bell tower dating back to 1610; it houses a marble statue of Domenico Gagini, father of Antonello.
Cathedral of the thirteenth century Romanesque-Pisan with Sienese arch, on top of a staircase on the star square: Romanesque font, rosette, a Gothic reliquary and a Madonna attributed to Duccio.

Sand cordons that mark an ancient line of coast: from the Etruscans to today the Po, advancing in the Adriatic, has left seven lines of coast, each with its dunes, largely destroyed by erosion, agriculture and sand extraction; those remaining are protected. You can see the phases from the sandy dune to the gray dune with junipers, holm oaks and sea pine trees, and nesting there beggars and marine acorns; old roads on the dunes, used in the Roman and Middle Ages, report towards the Po di Goro.
One of the tallest balconies on the Sibillini.
The giant telamone.
Valley of about 30 km2 with woods and streams, inside the Natural Park of the Friuli Dolomites, closed by Mount Raut (2,025 m); trails and excursions of various difficulties.
Etruscan necropolis with tombs carved into the rock, in the area of the thermal springs; Castel d'Asso is identified with the ancient Axia cited by Cicero in the Pro Caecina.
Easy pedaling.
The charming Roman amphitheatre entirely dug into the tuff.
Documented from 1287, it was renovated and enlarged with a major altar and choir from 1737 to 1744; it has a baroque façade and four altars. It is open on Sunday evening for Mass.
The best preserved walls of Abruzzo.
Large stone plate, 235 cm long and 95 cm high, with the fossil of a fish of about 30 million years ago, with a 30 cm rostrum, testimony of the marine environment of the Miocene.
Churches and chapels scattered among the woods of the upper valley.

In an 18th-century brick building, with the typical crutin excavated in the sandstone. The wine of the village is the Cisterna DOC, red from croatine grapes (traditionally called Bonarda); among the local specialties Meliga biscuits, apple pie, honey and grape mustard.
A large mountain church at almost a thousand meters.
The history of the Italian flight on the lake.

Municipality of Valdambra between Florence, Arezzo and Siena, border land since the Roman age and the gate of Chianti: the Tower of Galatrona with the parish church of Della Robbia, the castle of Cennina, the Badia a Ruoti and the Museum of the memory of San Pancrazio.

Founded in 1996 by Superintendence and Municipality in the restored premises of the San Francesco complex, it collects materials from the territory from prehistory to the Roman age: the lithic industry of Ponte di Pietra (Super Paleolithic, about 20,000 years ago), the finds of the moat of Conelle (IV millennium BC), Cava Giacometti and Monte Croce-Guardia (XII-X century BC), the Gallic necropolis and the sanctuary of Montefortino, as well as three cippes with the gate finger. Times indicated: mon, mar, ven, sab, dom and festivities 8:30-13:30; wed and Thu 13:30-19:30; closed on the second Sunday of the month.

Housed in the former eighteenth-century convent of Sant'Antonio, it is one of the main attractions of the village. The ceramics of Cerrete lived the golden period in the eighteenth century, after the earthquake of 1688, when Neapolitan workers joined the local ceramists; it was also appreciated at the Bourbon court.

Small Jewish cemetery linked to the presence of the Cantons, one of the most important Jewish families in the country; there is buried the writer Alberto Cantoni (1841-1904), friend of the painter Gerolamo Trenti (1824-98), among the main Lombard landscapers of the nineteenth century.
The Lambertini castle, the family of Pope Benedict XIV, rebuilt in 1475 and in the seventeenth century, now the town hall; the 25-metre-high Clock Tower was prison.

Opened in December 2003 in the former Convent of Sant'Antonio, complex of about 1645, to enhance the art that has made known Rapino in the world: exhibits about 180 ceramics of authors, eras and different styles, including works of the Maiolic masters Bozzelli, Vitacolumna and Bontempo, in part as permanent exhibition of the Municipality and in part rotating in temporary exhibitions, with multimedia posts. The MiC card indicates opening Saturday, Sunday and holidays (winter 10-13 and 15-19, summer 16-20), but is updated to 2020: times to be confirmed (tel. 0871 800642).

Remains of the medieval fortress Securana above Popiglio, probably built on a Roman settlement of the second century BC, grown in Lombard and Carolingian age and under the Counts Guidi, passed to Pistoia in the thirteenth century: it guarded the border with Lucca. Two square towers remain, the one upstream at about half the original height. You can reach it with a short path in the beech forest from a nearby car park or with the Way of St. Bartholomew.
The Marian shrine in the heart of the Quadrilatero, of ancient origins: originally dedicated to Sant'Andrea, existed already in the 10th century.
In Palazzo Sanguinetti, six centuries of music: ancient instruments, autograph scores, the portrait of Bach of Gainsborough, the workshop of the luthier Otello Bignami.

Municipality of Apennines Alessandrino a few kilometers from the sea, seat of the Natural Park of Capanne di Marcarolo: in the village Capanne the Ecomuseum of Cascina Moglioni and the ruins of Benedicta, shrine of the partisan massacre of April 1944; above, Mount Tobbio with the small church of Madonna di Caravaggio.
The Gothic-Lombard church in terracotta built between 1278 and 1363 for the Ghibelline Umbertino Landi, with rosettes, spires and rampant arches.
A Norman testimony of Eboli.

Today's exhibition room, it contains frescoes from the 13th to the 15th century, some of Byzantine style, and a fourteenth-century cycle attributed to a student of Giotto; next to the monastery of San Francesco and the Torre Bulgarini.

The town is 22 km from Rome, which combines the medieval village of Montecelio, with the Rocca dei Crescenzi and the Civic Museum Rodolfo Lanciani, which houses the Capitolina Triad, to the town of Fondazione Rationalista of Guidonia gathered around Piazza Matteotti; to the south opens the Regional Natural Park of the Enviolata.

Centre of the lower Parma, from the seventeenth century summer residence of the dukes of Parma: the Reggia redesigned by Ferdinando Galli Bibiena with the historical garden, the Aranciaia with the MUPAC, the ducal chapel of San Liborio with the organ Serassi, the Cathedral of Santa Margherita and the oratory of the SS. Annunciated.
In the Villa Floridiana since 1931, more than six thousand works of decorative arts: porcelain, majolica, avori, glass and coral.

Gothic-Romanesque cathedral in alberese and green marble of Prato, with frescoes by Filippo Lippi on the stories of Santo Stefano and the Baptist and the Chapel of the Sacred Cingolo, exhibited every year in September.

Founded in 1928 in the center of the pond of Sassu reclaimed, renamed "Mussolinia di Sardegna" in 1930 and called Arborea since 1944. It has the typical regular plan of the founding cities, with liberty and neo-Gothic buildings and, along the avenues, the offices of the reclamation. The parish church of Christ the Redeemer, in Tyrolean style, overlooks the main square.
The great palace-city of an emperor.
Fountain of 1898 in the main square, from which opens the view of the lake and the mountains.

Small museum in the premises next to the sacristy, born as an oratory. It has sacred vestments of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, sacred statues, reliquaries, candelabras, sacred vases, coins, prayer books, crosses and liturgical objects, as well as ancient texts including an edition of 1832 of the "Promises Sposi" (Promises).
Founded in 1444, with facade designed by Bartolomeo Genga (1563); preserves paintings by Giuseppe Bottani including the Guardian Angel.
The votive church of the plague.
The colubs from the sea.
can be visited only by appointment for groups on weekdays (FAI)
The medieval castle overlooking the ancient center.
Built in 1573, it has a wooden crucifix from the 16th century.
Deep engraving up to 30 meters, flowing with an average flow rate of about 300 liters per second; it is reached from the CAI 141 trail and faces from a walkway with parapet along the edge.

Terramaricol village of the medium Bronze age extended about seven hectares, between the sixteenth and the twelfth century BC; the oldest nucleus, of about one hectare, was founded around 1500 BC. It is the largest and most studied site in the province of Reggio Emilia: during the summer excavation campaigns the area is open with free guided tours that introduce to the culture of terracing.
Ionian sea with views of Mount Etna.
Fossils spectacular, good with children.
The walled village and its thirteenth-century palace.

The city of the Mexican was born between the rivers Idria and Longano, with the ancient nucleus of Pozzo di Gotto, the Cave of Santa Venere of Byzantine age, the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, the Basilica of San Sebastiano, the church of San Giovanni Battista with bulb bell towers and two large museums of artisan workshops, the Park Museo Jalari and the Museo Nello Cassata.
From the Renaissance to Picasso.
Dolomite panorama reachable even in winter.
The puppet theater.
Damaged with the City Hall by the 2016 earthquake; contribution for the reconstruction work re-established in January 2023
Half a century of contemporary art on paper.

Born in the seventies on the initiative of the primary teacher Dino Gregorio, who with his pupils gathered the testimonies of rural life that were disappearing. It preserves tools of peasant and handicraft work, objects of use of peasant houses and the memory of dialect words, stories and proverbs remembered only by the elderly.
Groups only
Ethnographic Museum with about eight thousand traditional objects from the 18th to the 20th century.

A previous chapel is remembered by an inscription of 1504 by Geronimo Centurione; the current Baroque church was built between 1615 and 1632, with late presbytery (between the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries), and houses a 17th century wooden statue of the Archangel Michael.

A sighting tower wanted by Carlo V in the middle of the sixteenth century against the Saracen raids, one of the Spanish coastal towers between Trigno and Tronto; around it grew the first inhabited. It houses the Antiquarium of Castrum Truentinum, an archaeological museum with exhibits from prehistory to the Lombard age excavated in the area of Colle Marzio.

A seaside resort north of Rome, called "Pearl of the Tyrrhenian Sea" with summer liberty villas, rocky coves and the marina of the ancient Punicum; in the hamlet of Santa Severa the castle on the sea rises on the site of Pyrgi, Etruscan port of Caere, and houses the Museum of the Sea and the Ancient Navigation.

The city of the Salerno Medical School: the Norman cathedral with the baroque crypt of St. Matthew, the Minerva Garden, the Longobard complex of St. Peter in Corte, the Castle of Arechi on the gulf, the provincial museums and the maritime station of Zaha Hadid.

It is located in Palazzo Trabia, one of the most important noble palaces in the area, and exhibits an interesting collection of ceramics: italia.it defines it as a true temple of the traditions of Santo Stefano di Camastra, where it traces the entire ceramic history.
The medieval village of the Rito dei Serpari, from the top of its tower.
One of the palaces that testifies to the Renaissance heritage of Rieti.

Twenty caves dug from the sea in the cliffs, accessible by boat, canoe or SUP and some swimming: the Palazzese, the largest, under a palace today hotel with restaurant; that of the Archbishopric, which is said to be connected by a passage to the bishop's palace; of the nuns, of the Rondinella, Ardito (with a natural column), Stampagnata (without roof) of Sella with a natural bridge and Chiangella.
The battlefield that named the Rue de Rivoli.

A small town of the inland of Palermo called "Of the hundred churches" dominated by the twin fortresses with the Castle Soprano and the Castle Sottono; a few steps from the center the canyon and the Cascata delle Due Rocche, in the village the Civic Museum "Pippo Rizzo" and the CIDMA, and in the hamlet of Ficuzza the Real Casina hunting of the Bourbons on the edge of the Bosco della Ficuzza.
One of the rare prehistoric tombs painted in Sardinia.

Castle on a hill with origins in the early Middle Ages, gods from Varano from 1240 to 1434, then Maurizi and finally Pallotta, still owners; at the end of the sixteenth century Cardinal Evangelista Pallotta transformed it into summer residence and hosted Clement VIII in 1598 (and then Cristina of Sweden in 1666). You enter from Porta Camerte and a drawbridge; the museum has weapons from the 13th to the 17th century, carriages from the 19th to the 19th century, salt with antique furnishings, ceramics from the Marche and a frieze attributed to Simone De Magistris, and in the park a pine planted in 1598.

Late Baroque church with Greek cross in the highest part of the country, with a sixteenth-century marble altar by Giandomenico Gagini with four scenes of the life of Jesus, seventeenth-century wooden statues of the saints Cosmas and Damian and two statues of saints attributed to Filippo Quattrocchi by Gangi. Next door, the Loreto viewpoint.

The first stone was laid on 23 February 1003 by Guglielmo da Volpiano, in the presence of the Marquis Arduino; at its apogee, between XII and XIII century, the abbey had 85 churches in Italy and housed up to 1,200 monks. In 1770 the abbot Carlo Vittorio Amedeo delle Lanze had the church and Romanesque monastery demolished, saving only the bell tower, and the new church (1766) was designed by Vittone and Quarini between Baroque and Neoclassical. Under the floor the excavations of 1979 brought to light the foundations of the Romanesque church and a mosaic of 1066 with two griffins, which can be visited from 2004 in an underground path (fresh, cover). Closed in summer; being parish, it is advisable to telephone (338 4128795).

The Church of the Visitation was commissioned in 1738 by banker Antonio Fico to Bernardo Antonio Vittone for the peasants of his fund, placing it on a pre-existing building. The frescoes are attributed to Pier Francesco Guala; in the sacristy remains the sixteenth-century fresco of the Madonna del latte, attributed to a painter near the Macrino. The original altarpiece and the palace attributed to Piffetti are kept at the Opera Pia Faccio-Frichieri. Visitable Saturday and Sunday 10:30-12:00 and 14:30-17:00; guided tours by reservation at least two weeks in advance.
The parishioner.
The monument designed by Marcello Piacentini (1926-1928) in progress Freedom, with the exhibition itinerary opened in 2014 on its history and the period between the two wars.

Dedicated to the Italian Liberation Corps, the unity born in the South after the armistice of 1943 that fought alongside the Allies until September 1944, is based in Scapoli, where was the Allied command and the operation of Monte Marrone was planned. Seven rooms trace the birth of CIL, Montelungo, the Mainarde sector on the Gustav Line and the advance on the Adriatic, until the visit of Aldo Moro to Scapoli in 1968, with original documents and films.

The highest village in the Pollino National Park, once called Torricella and refounded in 1633 by Prince Alessandro Pignone del Carretto, from which it takes its name and surname; among its churches stand out St. Alessandro and St. Vincenzo Ferreri, and on the last Sunday of April in Spinazzeta is celebrated the feast of Pita.
The noble living room of the city.
A rock church in the countryside, with frescoes and Arabic inscriptions.
A wild canyon under the sanctuary.
Church of early Christian foundation with the 12th century pavement mosaics depicting the cycle of the months and the zodiac.
The sea in squares.

Fortress of the thirteenth century on the rock ridge that dominates the village, transformed into a Renaissance residence between 1573 and 1587 by the counts Brancaleoni, lords of the place from 1213 to 1816. The courtyard of honour is Baccio Pontelli, the staircase is inspired by the Doge's Palace of Urbino; the Greek Chamber was frescoed in 1585 by Giorgio Picchi with stuccoes by Federico Brandani, author of the decorations of the Sala del Leon d'Oro; the clock tower turns counterclockwise. The Civic Museum has sections of uses and customs, speleology and geo-paleontology (more than 5000 fossils and the skeleton of a cave bear), ornithology, archaeology and numismatics. Open Saturday and Sunday 9-12 and 15-18.
Built by Emperor Frederick II between 1232 and 1240 on an ancient fort, at the extreme tip of Ortigia.
Villages, caves and monumental trees in Calvana.
The architrave of mysterious figures.
A walled city of the sixteenth century still entire.
The oldest cable car in the world, which goes up to the mountain village of Colle, from which trails start towards the Virgolo.
The renowned wine centre between Perugia and Assisi, along the main course overlooking Palazzo Graziani Baglioni.
Baroque overwhelming.
The monumental entrance of the only legionary camp near Rome.
A hot outdoor bath.
Wind, sails and a labor village on the lake.

In the thirteenth century Palazzo della Comunità on the main square, tells the ancient Signia from prehistory to the Middle Ages on two floors: necropolis sets, ex-vote in terracotta (tones, statuettes, a head of newborn in bands), figures of Minerva, Hercules and Venus, sacred and funerary Latin inscriptions, ceramics, architectural fragments and reconstructive plastics of the city. It runs the urban archaeological park; the specialist library is visited by appointment.
Canyon excavated from the Rio Fleons, reachable from the marble quarry of Pierabech; the spring is at 1,350 meters.
A tiny village transformed into an open-air art gallery.

Under the Fortress a natural park with about 400 plant species, part of the Nature Reserve Rocca and Sasso, covered by trails including the one that connects Pisenze and Dusano. It includes the Riparo Valtenesi, a natural terrace at the foot of Mount Sasso overlooking the lake, a place of worship since the Copper Age (3000-2500 BC) and then a burial area with collective hut tombs.
Bay surrounded by vegetation, looking wild but with some facilities and parking nearby.
Ancient Maritime Republic and university city, with Piazza dei Miracoli UNESCO heritage since 1987, the Lungarni and the city of Galileo.
The crypt with the oldest altar in Piedmont.
In the former religious complex, works by Tiziano, Giovanni Bellini, Lorenzo Lotto and Cima da Conegliano, an archaeological section from prehistory to Roman age and local history.

Napoleonic Museum and the Risorgimento in the center of Rivoli, on the site of the battle of 14-15 January 1797: exhibits weapons, uniforms and documents of the time and a plastic that reconstructs the battle.
Single ticket €15, reduced €10
Four centuries of wine.

Municipality of the Piacenza plain with the church of San Pietro from the medieval bell tower and the romantic park of Villa Raggio, which houses the Serra Theatre; in the territory the Castle of Paderna, visitable, and the fifteenth-century castle of Muradello.
Necropolis of the final Neolithic dug into the rock on the valley of the Riu Mannu: twelve domus with 21 rooms, vestibules and traces of paintings in ochre.
open only on extraordinary dates (in 2026 before Sunday of the month, April-October); calendar 2027 to be verified
Nuraghi and sacred well of the Bronze Age in the territory of Sorso.
The terrace on the Dolomites.

The historical centre contains the most remarkable buildings of the village: Palazzo Filomarini, also known as Palazzo della Principessa, the church of the Immaculate Virgin and the Matrice Church, parish dedicated to Santa Maria della Snow.

Mining country of Canavese: the mines, closed in 1964, closed a cycle of twenty centuries and are told in the museum of Cà ad Martolo; on the high ground dominates the parish church of San Michele Arcangelo, consecrated in 1545.

Municipality of the Friulian plain near the Tagliamento: in Coderno stands the birthplace of the poet friar David Maria Turoldo, example of rural construction in the pebbles of the river; the capital preserves a castle of the Bronze Age and Gradisca its ancient fortified "centa" with the church of Santo Stefano and the portal of Pilacorte.

Walls built and reinforced between the 12th and the 16th century, with a perimeter of about 2,418 meters and the gates Cuprense, San Domenico, d'Agello and Monte Antico with its tower; the Complex of the Sources (XV-XVI century) has a courtyard that houses an outdoor theatre.
A road covered by stone vaults on the inner side of the western walls, where the portam castri opens: a rare example of castle architecture of the thirteenth century, with a defensive function.
Medieval walls and noble palaces in a few steps.
From prehistory to the Middle Ages, the story of Ginosa in one path.

From Lateis, reachable with a challenging climb, you can enjoy the panorama; between Ampezzo and Sauris you pass the Pura pass (1425 m) with the Tita Piaz refuge next to, and the Tiziana Weiss nature trail climbs up to almost 2000 meters.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione della Valle Vigezzo, the gateway to the Val Grande National Park, where the history of the valley is told through the ollar stone.
The life in the trulli told in a farm of the eighteenth century.
Sulky's story in four rooms.

Medieval castle known as the Madonna's Castle, with irregular polygonal plan with large moat crossed by a bridge; baroque entrance with round arch, niches with statues and a clock of the eighteenth century. Local stone walls and framed windows in Bagnoregio stone. Fortress of the Monaldeschi until the sixteenth century, then feud of the Spada princes.

Founded in 1972 on the initiative of Edy Romani, it exhibits more than 14,000 crystals and minerals from the surrounding valleys and from all over the world, with a naturalistic area that reconstructs the mountain environment with flora and fauna; annexed a laboratory of hand working of the hard stones. Open every day 9-12.30 and 15-19.
Bernini in every detail.
Just outside the center, it rises on the site of the ancient castle, already in ruins and abandoned in the seventeenth century, of which are visible ruins of walls and towers.
Fans' pilgrimage.
The teenage Michelangelo.
The center of the village and its most photographed corner.

Opened on September 18, 1981 around the ancient refectory, it preserves works recovered after the earthquake of 1980: a silver cross of Aragonese age, Neapolitan cups, the fifteenth-century vestments of Diego I Cavaniglia (farsetto and giornea), a St. Francis in ecstasy attributed to the workshop of Solimena and a lunette with Annunciation attributed to Francesco da Tolentino. The remaining works will have to be re-arranged in a new venue.
The bread of the village.
The furnishings of the necropolis of Monte Tabor.
All about the return of the wolf in the Ligurian Apennines.
Walk in the streets of Feltria romana under the square of the Duomo.
Beach described as an oasis of peace and serenity away from the crowd, recommended to nature lovers.
Vigonese baroque.
Ribera and Pietro da Cortona in a thirteenth-century monastery.
The Baroque obelisks of the Immaculate Church in Piazza del Gesù Nuovo, San Gennaro in Piazza Riario Sforza and San Domenico in the homonymous square.
MiC card (updated in 2021) is closed every day: check opening before visit
Museum dedicated to the peasant life of the valley.

The main religious building of the city, along the Via Emilia: interior with Baroque and neoclassical decorations, stuccoes and side altars; preserves the Assumption of Guido Reni and a Madonna with Child by Modena Adeodato Malatesta.

In 1619 the Duke Carlo Emanuele I donated the castle of Riva to the favorite Margherita de Roussillon, named marquise; from 1734 he passed to the counts Grosso di Brozolo, who in 1738 had him rebuilt by Bernardo Antonio Vittone. The decorations form a unique cycle: in the atrium the trompe-l'oeil transform the corridor into a gallery of archaeological finds hung in grappa on a fake stone wall. Today it is the seat of the Municipality; recommended booking (tel. 011 521 1788).

Collections of shells, insects, reptiles, minerals and fossils, a large ornithological collection, a permanent exhibition of paleoanthropology and a herbarium with sections on the Mediterranean scrub, aromatic herbs and aquatic plants.
A baroque cathedral in a mountain country.
Culture and theatre in a medieval convent.
Ancient university seat, with courtyard and loggias covered with coats of arms. On the first floor the Anatomical Theatre in carved wood (1637) and the Sala dello Stabat Mater.
One of the most romantic gardens in the world, at most in April and May.
A seventeenth-century convent became a municipal home.

Castello dei Canossa, where in 1092 the Emperor Henry IV stopped; then he passed to Visconti, Estensi and from 1603 to the Gherardini, who in the seventeenth century transformed him into a noble residence. Since 1796 the town has been home; the community bought it back in 1884 for 14,000 lire and since 1978 it has been restored. You enter from a massive tower with two ogival doors, one for the wagons and a pedestrian, and the wounds of the drawbridge. Today it is home to the Town Hall, accessible during the times of the municipal offices.
The residence of the de Sangro overlooking the Dauni Mountains.
A fortress on the hill.
The first amusement park in Italy, born for the agricultural exhibition of 1953.
Visit by reservation at the San Vigilio Foundation, tel. 0463 751301.
A fifteenth-century forge still moved by water.
The kits of ancient Aequa.
No (yes for guided tours)
A century ago in the Oltrepò, room by room.
The source indicates frescoes in critical state and sacristy in bad conditions, without visiting times
The ancient sanctuary on the Martesana.
The Duomo of the Borghese.

Brick complex rebuilt in the fifteenth century on the oldest ruins, for over 650 years home of the Marquises Rangoni. The Municipality bought it in 2005 and restored it since 2011; in the Courtyard of Honor is the Court of Taste, a space dedicated to typical products of the territory.
The hamlet of the record-breaking flower.
The church of the ...Piazza di Pallanza, recognizable for its large staircase to low steps.
The temple of cyclists at the top of the ascent.

At the highest point of the city, next to the ancient Cassero, it is one of the main examples of Romanesque-Gothic of the Marches: nucleus of the eighth century enlarged in the XII-XIII centuries with naves, apse, crypt and protyro; in the crypt the sarcophagus of the Saints Martyrs with relief in lunese marble of the fourth century. In the seventeenth-century baptistery the bronze source of the brothers Jacometti of Recanati.
The house of English romantics.
Square and crenellated tower, the only intact remains of the ancient castle started by the Cremonesi in 1133; in 1525 the king of France Francesco I of Valois was imprisoned.
visits only by reservation, without fixed times, according to In Lombardia and Museimpresa
The most complete village-factory liberty at the gates of Turin.

Uninhabited granite island of about 134 hectares about 4 km from the coast, a site of community interest where they nest herons, seagulls courses and marangoni from the tuft; on the highest point, about 50 meters, the Spanish tower of San Luigi, to the north the large cliffs of Variglioni with natural pools. You can reach it by boat or by excursions from the port of Villasimius, landing in Caletta d'Approdo.
A tour of the ancient sources of the country, including a sulfur.
Walking through the Balzes.
Hydraulic engineering over 2,000 years ago.
Civic museum dedicated to Duilio Cambellotti, the artist of the cycle on the redemption of the Agro Pontino.
The village of Leonardo: the Leonardo Museum in the castle of Conti Guidi and the birthplace of Anchiano, among the olive trees of Montalbano.
To be checked: ticket on the Labyrinth website

In the building of the Valdese Cultural Centre in Beckwith Street, it documents the origins of the Waldensian people with a historical and ethnographic section; it is also an introduction to the Waldensian museums of the valleys (Rorà, Rodoretto, Ghigo di Prali, Balziglia, Pomaretto, Angrogna). The exhibition includes the permanent collection of Paolo Paschetto and the archaeological collection Ippolito.
The medieval castle overlooking the lake.
Locri's pinakes.
frescoes of the fifteenth century at 1760.
One of the smallest theatres in Europe, founded in 1795: oval hall with 22 stages and about 200 seats; Puccini and Ungaretti attended.

It houses two frescoes of the Pordenone used as altarpieces: the Madonna on throne with the Child of 1525 in the right aisle, with the inscription of the clients, and the Martyrdom of San Sebastiano among the Saints Rocco, Stefano, Niccolò and the archangel Michael in the chapel of San Sebastiano, paid between 1527 and 1535. The documents were discovered in 1967 by the parish priest Don Vittorino Zanette.
Closed for restoration works since March 2024; reopening not yet confirmed (some sites still indicate dates already exceeded)
A 16th-century church along the Ete.
An ancient stone bridge in the woods.

It exhibits the results of the ongoing research on the territory and tells, with original materials, graphic reconstructions and a plastic, the history of the settlements in the ancient beehive of Lake Bientina from the Paleolithic to the Middle Ages: wood, stone, metals, ceramics and coins. The strong pieces are the remains of a Roman bridge and a medieval piroga used to cross the lake. Educational activities for schools and temporary exhibitions.

Church probably of 1491, dependent on the monks of Farfa, along the Rio, the main tributary of the Fluvion; it belonged to a monastic settlement of which only partially recognizes the complex. There remains a 9th century crypt and a 15th century bronze bell with Gothic inscriptions.
The small lake overlooking the village; on the lakefront a monumental elm.

Cities at the north gates of Milan, rich in delightful villas: the main is Villa Ghirlanda Silva, with one of the first English parks of Italy and home of the MUNAF - National Museum of Photography; the territory is between the North Park Milan and the agricultural park of the Grugnotorto.

Franciacorta municipality known for the Borgo del Maglio, group of rural buildings among small streams with a fifteenth-century forge moved by a hydraulic wheel still working and the Museum House Pietro Malossi; on the hill of Goiane the church of San Michele, with frescoes of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries and views of the plain.

Medieval village in white limestone in the Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga National Park, marked by the Medici's domination in the sixteenth century: the Medici Tower rebuilt after the earthquake in 2009, the door with the Florentine coat of arms, the churches of Santo Stefano Protomartire and Santa Maria in Ruvo and, just outside, the Madonna del Lago.
Built from 1515 instead of the early 13th century church, of which it uses some decorative elements; characteristic the Baroque bell tower.
Village in a large basin of pastures, indicated as an example of Alpine architecture; it houses the house-museum of smuggler.

A fifteenth-century building just outside the center, built on Roman remains that legend binds to the tomb of the console Flaminio; it preserves a painting from the ancient Hospital of Santa Maria della Misericordia, attributed to the Pinturicchio or Perugino.

Among the places of worship of the historic center the Church of the Holy Spirit, recognizable for the domes Â Â trullo Â, the Church of San Domenico and the sixteenth century church of the Madonna of Constantinople.
17th-century shrine, Romanesque roundabout and small lake of the apparitions in a single complex.
The architecture of the 1930s.
Borgo dei Monti Ernici about 100 km from Rome, known for the Certosa di Tsulti, a national monument since 1873, for the karst caves of the Bambocci and for the great chasm of the Well of Antullo.
Stone, alleys and views of the valley.
The Procession of the Whites of 1401.
The ancient nucleus of the village, between castle and Codacchio.
360° panorama of vineyards, hazelnuts and lavender.
The Masaccio Trinity, the first perfect perspective.
The Study Centre keeps documents and testimonies on the life and works of the writer, born in Pescina in the house today museum, and organizes every year the Literary Prize Silone.
The symbol of the city on the river.
Vanvitelli's masterpiece.
Underwater archaeological park and marine protected area around the two islets united by a bridge, with Roman villas submerged for bradisism, to be explored with the visits organized by the park.
The objects of St. Louis and his family.
A still active monastic spices.
The Marian shrine of the Capitanate.
A jewel of Piedmontese baroque.

In two rural buildings of the ancient fiefdom of Fontanabona, on the last hills before the plain, it collects rustic furniture, ceramics, household objects and agricultural tools and craftsmen: a working frame of the first half of the nineteenth century, the samples of the textile company Spezzotti (since 1857), tools for the stable, the bachiculture and the harvest and a large collection of ploughs. He's got a specialized library. It is normally open from April to November by appointment.
The Renaissance waterfall on the source sung by Orazio.

Sant'Angelo in Vado is known as the capital of the white truffle, celebrated with the National Exhibition in the last three weeks of October and in the first of November; in the village the Experimental Center for truffle cultivation is also located.
The largest panorama of the Pontina Plain.
Cast Gothic gold into a country monastery.
To figure out the tanes before you go down the throat.
Eight centuries of a family.
Gothic and Stava's memory.

Built in 1655 by Lorenzo Tadina, the last lord of the castle, when the plague killed more than half of the inhabitants. He preserves paintings with the apostles, an Annunciation with the banner of the Bonzani donated by an emigrater and recent decorations of the painter Vagliani; at the feast of the village the statue of the saint comes out in procession.
The country hamlet with ancient farmhouses of the eighteenth-nineteenth century and the typical warehouses with a roof of tiles.
The Aggius rug fabric in front of your eyes.
The peasant life of the valley in the twentieth century.

In the former Bishop's Palace of the late sixteenth century, renovated in Renaissance forms with interventions by Francesco di Giorgio Martini, Gerolamo Genga and the stonemasons of Sant'Ippolito. From the lapidary you pass to the rooms of silver, vestments, Madonnas and the metauren mannerists (Federico Zuccari, Giovanni Giacomo Pandolfi, Claudio Ridolfi) and to a section of majolica that documents the production of Castel delle Ripe, Casteldurante and Urbania from the XIII to the XX century. Italia.it indicates opening from Tuesday to Sunday 11-13 and 16-18.

Valico at 1039 meters on the state road of Cisa, once bordered by the Duchy of Parma and the Grand Duchy of Tuscany, with the ancient post station; on top of a staircase the neo-Romanesque and neo-Gothic sanctuary of Our Lady of the Guard, of 1921.
Medieval village of Valtiberina along its steep "ruga"; under the walls, June 29, 1440, the battle that Leonardo painted in Palazzo Vecchio.

At 2,757 meters between the region of Ortles and Bormio, it is the highest road pass in Italy: the road, 49 km long and called the "queen of the Alpine roads" was built between 1820 and 1825 and has since almost unchanged, with 48 hairpin bends on the South Tyrolean side; it is a challenge for cyclists and motorcyclists and stage of the Giro d'Italia. At the pass, in the Stelvio National Park, summer glacier skiing is open six months a year. During the Stelvio Bike Day, at the end of summer, the road is closed to motorized traffic.
Around 400 hectares of sulphur mines active from the end of the eighteenth century to 1987: limestone, descendants and castles of extraction in an open-air museum of industrial archaeology.
The 19th century Lombard, from Cremona to Belloni.
Two rationalist examples of Frezzotti, the Casa del Combatente and the National Opera Balilla, and on the same square the Cathedral of San Marco.
A house from the Middle Ages.

A navigation basin on the Sile built around 1680 diverting the last stretch of the river, with doors built between 1682 and 1684; next is still exposed the stone plate of Istria of 1684 with the tariff for boats. It was the real center of Portegrandi until 1960; near there is a large marina from which you can reach the lagoon and its islands.

You enter the medieval village from the ancient arch of Piazza Garibaldi; traces of the walls with defensive towers and Renaissance residences remain. Fifty artistic tiles of the  "Narranti Villages" (with QR code) let the stories of the elderly hear in the places where the facts took place.
The last flooded forest of the Ionian Sea.

For almost two centuries the capital of a branch of Gonzaga, with the sixteenth-century plan still legible: the Doge's Palace with the City Museum, the cathedral consecrated by Carlo Borromeo, the statue of Ferrante Gonzaga of Leone Leoni, the Maldotti Library and, just outside, the millennial Basilica of the Pieve.
The oldest church in the village, next to the river.
Three centuries of pottery found in the wells of the Fortress.
The canal port designed by Leonardo in 1502, the historical boats of the Marine Museum, Casa Moretti and the beaches of the Riviera.
Parish church of the first half of the nineteenth century in classic Tuscan style; on the façade, on the sides of the portal, two niches house the statues of St. John the Baptist and St. Bartholomew.
Small church just outside the Porta di Maremma, with frescoes from the fifteenth century; behind it opens the panoramic space of the Cassero.

In Tobia, near Gionghi: hives and instruments from various parts of the world, explanations on the hierarchy of the hive and on the dance of the bees, educational workshops and guided tours, with sale of honey of the Highlands and derived products.
From prehistory to the Longobards of Flaminia.

From the 13th century, it is the oldest sacred building in the historic centre and the smallest Franciscan church in the village, with simple lines, with ceiling decorated in â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â â Villa Salvo with the coat of arms of the house is nearby.

The oldest street in the village crosses the center between the two ancient doors: at number 27 a small building with portal in pepper and cardinal's coat of arms attributed to the Chigi, between 24 and 26 a painted porcelain Virgin of the eighteenth century. Beyond the medieval gate, the village wanted by Andrea Giustiniani in the seventeenth century, with Palazzo Savelli and the church of San Filippo Neri (first half of the seventeenth century, four altars, wooden ceiling, Madonna della Pietà); in the Oratory of the Confraternita della Santissima Trinità a banner by Francesco Ciaci.

Founded in 1823 by Canon Carmine Fontò and then curated by Emanuele Barba, who created a zoological cabinet: weapons, costumes, fossils, works by the Gallipolin painter Giovanni Andrea Coppola, sarcophagi and messapic vases with inscriptions, portraits of illustrious Gallipolini and a numismatic collection. It also includes the Museum of the Sea and the Coppola Collection Hall; open from Tuesday to Sunday.
Finalmarina's heart.
Museum on the life and works of Abbot Joseph-Marie Trèves, native of Emarèse and eminent figure in the history of the Aosta Valley of the twentieth century.

Mother church and cathedral until 1818, already mentioned in a bull of Pope Stephen IX. From the external stairs to the lateral aisles you go down to the crypt, restored in 1984: under the marble altar a urn has been guarding since 1095 the remains of St. John, bishop and patron; there are two frescoes from the twelfth century with St. Nicholas of Bari and St. John of Montemarano, a wooden bust of the saint and a crucifix of the fifteenth century.

The village of the low Cremona river on the banks of the Po, known for the Paleoanthropological Museum of the Po, which collects hundreds of fossils of the Quaternary recovered along the river and a frontal bone of Man of Neanderthal; in the hamlet of Isola Pescaroli, on the bank of the river, stands the sanctuary of the Madonna of Trust, Queen of the Po.

Basilica built in the first half of the seventeenth century and rebuilt in the nineteenth century; it houses a marble statue of St. Vitus of the sixteenth century, a seventeenth-century painting of the Blessed Savior within a wreath of flowers and a marble saint of the late seventeenth century.

The wax museum was set up in 2001 at Palazzo Morcaldi, home of Mayor Francesco Morcaldi, friend of Padre Pio, who in the 1920s opposed his transfer: ten scenes tell of the main moments of the life of the saint, chosen by a committee of historians with the advice of the Capuchins.

Seasonal stream that flows from a cave and flows into Lake Como, flowing only in spring; it is indicated as the shortest river in Italy. The botanical garden of Villa Monastero extends along the shore to this hamlet. In 1887 the painter Vittore Grubicy de Dragone painted "Fiumelatte" from the railway underpass.
Church of the village of Someda, rebuilt after a fire in 1883, with altarpiece and frescoes by Valentino Rovisi.

Logudoro-Meilogu village 400 meters on the slopes of Mount Sant'Antonio, about 30 km from Sassari, home of the singer Maria Carta and writer Gavino Ledda: in the territory the nuragic complex of Monte Sant'Antonio, the medieval churches of Santa Maria di Bubalis and Sant'Elia di Monte Santo and the volcanic craters of the Meilogu.

A nineteenth-century factory where from 1835 to 1960 the Parietti family produced tiles and bricks with the clay of the nearby quarries; restored with contemporary architectural solutions, it preserves the octagonal gallery oven with 16 vaulted rooms. In the Fornace park there is a giant bench accessible to people with motor disabilities, among the first in Europe.
The museum that houses the Majesty of Ambrogio Lorenzetti.

The first settlement was built in the first half of the 16th century around the Florentine monastery; the village, the largest in Sila, is known for its wood and wrought iron processing and for its hand-knotted Armenian carpets.
Arte Abruzzo del Novecento in a castle.

Church isolated on the hill of Nemi, mentioned already in 1218 among the appliances of the Pieve di Bovigliano; it preserves a series of images of Paolo da Visso of 1447 and a painting of the Boccati with the Madonna crowned with the Child between the Saints Matteo and Macario.
The city told by the water.
The craftsmanship of the straw of the village.
A waterfall in the heart of the rock.
Animals, fossils and history of science.

In the third floor Fraporta, home to the museum and the civic library: it preserves the Coronation of the Virgin by Domenico Ghirlandaio and the Annunciation of Benozzo Gozzoli, commissioned by Cardinal Bernardo Eroli, and an archaeological section.
The remains of the amphitheatre of the second century wanted by Hadrian, the most important of the region, with a little smaller arena than that of the Colosseum.
The Moroni's shovel and the Fantoni's woods.

A hilly town of the Brianza Lecchese of pre-Roman origins, known for the complex of Villa Belgiojoso with the large garden terraces and for the headquarters of Merate of the Astronomical Observatory of Brera (INAF), with the domes of the telescopes Ruths and Zeiss open for visits.
The pine forest offers more than 22 km of pedestrian paths; the cycle path of Val Seriana crosses it and leads to Piario.
Grey sandy beaches on the Etruscan sea, the northernmost coast of Lazio.
The life and crafts of the Friuli mountain.
From the bastions you can see the whole Chianti.
The Baroque church of Francesco Borromini on the Quirinale, at the crossing of the Four Fountains.

Also known as Santa Maria Annunziata and considered a national monument, it replaced a small medieval church on whose façade was a fifteenth-century painting by Giacomo Busca with Our Lady and the Crucifix: according to tradition, on June 2, 1511 a shepherd saw the Virgin move her eyes and cry tears of blood. A unique nave in five bays, a façade with a rose window, renovated at the beginning of the twentieth century on a project by Giovanni Muzio. Above the right entrance is hung an embalmed crocodile of about three meters, documented since 1594.
Every August 5th it is the end of the centuries-old procession at the Madonna delle Snow.
The calluses of the Sun Island.

About 500 m from the walls, on the ridge between the valleys of Otricoli and Magliano Sabina, rises with the convent of San Berardo, the friar of Calvi converted by the preaching of St. Francis in 1213 and martyr in Morocco. The church, documented in 1291, is a single nave with a barrel vault and ten side chapels; in 1527 the Lanzichenecchi plundered and burned the oratory. In the cloister, with a well of the thirteenth century, there are 17th-century frescoes with stories of St. Francis.
Church of the XI-XII century, rebuilt in the sixteenth-sixth century, with source of 1590, Robbian terracotta and a group of the Annunciation.
The stairway of the Capitol.

Along the whole coast of Grisolia grows the sea lily (Pancratium maritimum), a rare plant with white flower with petals similar to orchids, which blooms from mid-July to the end of August; the seeds, enclosed in a very light corky mass, float and are brought by the seaside along the coast. The FAI invites to protect it with the native vegetation from erosion and the spread of the shores.
Oratory in the medieval old town.
Free archeology in the center, perfect on a rainy day.

At Vettignè the Canale Cavour, built between 1863 and 1866 and 82 km long from Chivasso al Ticino, passes under the Elvo stream with a syphony tomb tunnel, while the nearby Canale Vanoni climbs over it with a bridge-channel; at the entrance door 110 m3/s, which go up to 180 with the Farini and the Naviglio d'Ivrea.
The summer palace of Frederick II of Aragon.
An easy walk to the sanctuary.
Built by Prince Mirelli after the collapse of the castle in the earthquake of 1694, reusing materials of the castle, including the majestic portal on Via Roma that was once its entrance.
Of Norman origin (XII century), with nineteenth-century interventions.
The route of line 1 along the Grand Canal, among the ancient palaces overlooking the water.
A stop of Sigerico with Longobard capitals.
The four-arched bridge.
The underground mill where Vico's oil was born.
The pastures under the Grand Combin.

Erected in the fifteenth century by the prior Antonio Migliorati, with eighteenth-century façade and Gothic portal; the bell tower was completed in 1464 by Pietro Lombardo. Frescoes from the beginning of the twentieth century by F. Ferranti; behind the high altar the urn with the remains of Blessed Antonio.

A territorial park established in 1990 and managed by the Municipality of Colledara, extended for over 80 hectares between the stream Sazza and the Fosso San Paolo, with inside the medieval village of Castiglione della Valle, where according to tradition stayed Lucrezia Borgia fleeing from his brother Cesare. Along the river grow willows and poplars, with reeded and raft marshes, small waterfalls on the Sazza and, further away, woods of roverella, cerro, orniello, black hornbeam and a querco-carpinet of glacial origin; there live green woodpecker, barbagianni, badger, faina and skunk. The easy botanical trail of the old mill has four thematic boards and cards; the Visite Center (2005), just before Castiglione, is a didactic workshop with herbarium, insectary and xilothotheque, and there is a refreshment point. Information and guided tours: Municipality of Colledara, tel. 0861 698551.
The history of South Tyrolean wine between presses and cellars.
Alluvial woods along the Rhine, on the Rhine Cycleway.
At sunset the salt is dyed pink.
18th century villa with facade of the architect Venanzio Marvuglia.
Small stone church recently restored, already existing in 1743 and originally outside the walls of the village; on the portal the inscription "Sant'Antonio" .

the Rocca Sforza is closed for restoration works since March 2024 and the reopening date is not yet confirmed. Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 3 of the 9 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Houses built on the rocks of the landslide.

The Roman city buried by the eruption of Vesuvius of 79 AD, less extensive than Pompeii but better preserved, with upper floors, woods and charred food: it is part of the UNESCO site of the archaeological areas of Pompeii, Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata.
Antonelli's Cathedral.

To the south of the village, where the Roman farm villa and the primitive village stood, the church has a rectangular apse and frescoes from the 15th century; in the same place, along the ancient mule tracks, there are other frescoed chapels.
The seventeenth-century cycle of the Baptist, to the completion of the basilica.

Born as a simple newsstand to protect a painting considered miraculous, it passed in 1120 to the Chapter of St. Cesidius; of the time remains a wall with a trilobed arched window on the north side. Restored in 1741 and 1747, it was extended to the present dimensions at the beginning of the twentieth century by the initiative of Fr Ercolano Ciofani.

The pedestrian zone connects the parish church of Sant'Ulrico to the church of Sant'Antonio, between historic hotels, small shops, bars and restaurants with local specialties; the families of carvers of Ortisei make sacred sculptures, statues of saints and altars at least from the seventeenth century. Just outside, the church of Sant'Anna and the cemetery are reminiscent of characters like Luis Trenker and Ludwig Norman-Neruda. Ortisei hosted the 1970 Alpine Ski World Cup.

Behind the coast, mountain park of rocky hills, woods inhabited by deer and mouflons, canyons, gorges, rivers and archaeological sites; inside the Arch of the Angel, natural arch of pink granite with panoramic view over the entire valley of Castiadas.
One of the best preserved Visconti castles.
The water of Vibinum under the village.

The city of Stradivari and violin, with one of the most beautiful medieval squares in Italy: the Duomo, the Torrazzo, the octagonal Baptistery and the Palazzo del Comune; then the Violin Museum, the gallery Ala Ponzone and the Renaissance palaces of Corso Matteotti and Corso Garibaldi.

Private museum opened in 1999 in the eighteenth-century Palazzo Pomarici Santomasi, where the restoration brought to light frescoes and ceilings in hand painted paper.
