Built between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries in the hamlet of Colle Soglio, in a panoramic position on the valley, with a porch adjecting a trasanna and a high sailing bell tower.

Built in the second half of the 12th century on the ruins of a church destroyed by a fire, with three naves: pulpit with Romanesque reliefs of the childhood of Christ, the Nolfi Chapel frescoed by Domenichino (1618-1619) and a altarpiece by Ludovico Carracci.

Castle on three floors that dominates from the cliff the historic center, of the Massimo of Rome for over four centuries; it preserves frescoes of the late sixteenth century commissioned to the Zuccari and of the eighteenth century to the Benefial, a collection of weapons, the Sala del Trono and the Chapel of San Filippo Neri with part of the cosmatesque facade. In the basement there is the ancient oven, the storehouses of food and oil and the prison; around woods and an Italian hanging garden.
The noble residences of Valtellina.

Narrow streets crossed by water and old mills, with Palazzo Fullini Zaia (XVI-XVII century) in Piazza Plebiscito, the Scolari-Salice and Zaro palaces, the sixteenth-century theatre born as the Theatre of the Counts of Polcenigo and the church of Santa Maria della Salute. Just outside the oratory of San Rocco (XIV century, rebuilt in the seventeenth century) and the churches of Ognissanti (1371), San Lorenzo (XIII century, with the altarpiece of the Trinity attributed to Tizianello) and San Giovanni (with paintings by Egidio Dall'Oglio). Each year in early September, for more than three centuries, the center hosts the fair of Thèst (cest).
The façade, the baroque altar and the wooden statue of St. Christopher 4,60 meters high are remarkable.

Castle mentioned in the XII-XIII centuries and renovated in neo-Gothic style in 1866; it is linked to Maria Elisabetta Ferrero della Marmora, who had the neo-Gothic Serra and the Round Tower built and transformed the Italian garden into a 6-hectare park. Restored since 2007, it hosts temporary exhibitions, concerts, shows and educational activities. The park preserves over 1,740 trees of about 70 species, crossed by irrigation channels; free entry with Museums and Torino+Piemonte Card subscription, recommended booking.

Founded by the Arabs around 860 A.D. on the edge of the village, it retains the Arab village's layout with narrow alleys, steep stairways, terraces and houses with plaster walls, including the "dammuso" , the typical Sicilian house in one compartment; many successive stratifications covered it, but the neighborhood design is well read from the hill. It is the scenery of the living nativity scene.

The rural house of the end of the sixteenth century of the Mondoni-Bazzoni families, purchased by the municipality and opened in 2006 as a museum collection recognized by the Lombardy Region: original vaults and limestone, tools for fields, viticulture and winemaking, breeding and crafts, and clothes, weapons, helmets and armour of the Santa Crus. Outside there is a horizontal lever press. Open Tuesday, Friday (14.30-16.30), Thursday (9-12), Saturday and Sunday (14.30-17.30); groups by reservation.
Collections and exhibitions in a palace returned to the city.

The museum tells the local chestnut culture with a three-section itinerary: the first dedicated to the history of chestnut and the tools used for processing, the second with the reconstruction of the interiors of mountain houses, with furnishings and household objects, the third didactic-scientific cutting with paper and computer archives.
One of the collections of the Fondazione Giacomini Meo Fiorot housed in Villa Mazzucchelli.
The only surviving Romanesque church of the city, mentioned already in 1124, with three naves with octagonal tiburium and a Madonna with Child attributed to Giovanni De' Campo.
Closed to the public for restoration works

Built in the first half of the eighteenth century on an existing building and modified in the nineteenth century, it passed to the Florio at the end of the century, which held it until 1947; then it was college, school and finally property of the Municipality. The tripartite façade has a central rustic body with balcony and tympanum; the landscape park of the second half of the nineteenth century, attributed to Giuseppe Rho and surrounded by a crenellated wall, descends on the hill with a boulevard of palm trees and exhibits Eagles finds collected by Francesco di Toppo. Here on May 7, 1933 the first regional wine fair opened, which the villa still hosts.

Along the sandy coast with numerous bathing establishments equipped with catering and entertainment for children; there are two areas reserved for dogs, Rocca Priora a Mare and near the station, with bathing area signposted.
Stalactites and underground lakes in one of the first tourist caves in Italy.
The archaeological area crossed by via dei Fori Imperiali (1932) and the Museum of Imperial Forums in the Trajan Markets, with multimedia reconstructions and views of the Forums.
Medieval frescoes under the cliffs.
On Napoleon's camp.
The most representative image of the Cosentine Ionian coast.
visits only with guided tour

Not a traditional museum but a laboratory of experimental archaeology: with an archaeologist, objects are handled and people's gestures of over 10,000 years of prehistory are re-created. Times on request.

Gothic Church of the fourteenth century with nine painted altars; in the convent, with the frescoed cloister, the library and the Museo dei Bozzetti Pierluigi Gherardi with 700 models in plaster of sculptors from all over the world.
The public gardens created in 1864 on the site of the fourteenth-century Citadel, with statues of the Reggia of Rivalta and the Roman funeral enclosure of the Concords.
Built in 1671 on a 15th-century building, with a major Baroque wooden altar and cemetery with ancient stone tombstones carved by local craftsmen.
A hermitage dug into the rock, with a view to Corsica.
Parish of origin of the 11th century, dependent on the Sacred, rebuilt in the 18th century on a project by Bernardo Vittone.
For a slow walk.
Route between red sandstone walls crossed by the river Uria, in the territory of Zagarise.
Historic carnival.
The complete story of the Greek Gela.

Dedicated to fighting for Col del Rosso, Col d'Ecchele and Monte Valbella, from the Strafexpedition of 1916 to the battles of January and June 1918 to the last Italian reconquest in October 1918. In summer it hosts exhibitions, conferences and screenings.

Borgo sul Tevere enclosed by medieval walls with Porta Maior and Porta San Severino; at its feet the Archaeological Park of Ocriculum, a Roman city on the Via Flaminia with theatre, thermal baths, amphitheatre and necropolis, whose findings are told in the Antiquarium of the Palazzo Priorale and in that of Casale San Fulgenzio.

The village has developed within three circles of concentric walls, each with four doors; the best preserved part is the civic tower of the XIV-XV centuries next to the Town Hall. In the centre there is also the church of Sant'Agostino with the adjoining convent and the church of San Gregorio Magno of 1615.

The balcony of the High Ionian Sea, on a plateau overlooking the sea: historic center with the sixteenth century belt against the Saracens, the Mother Church of St. Nicholas of Mira with the Byzantine domes and, in Broglio, the mycenean remains and a Hellenic necropolis.

The Colombera is located in a Lombard courtyard between Corso Garibaldi and Via Del Gigante, near the church of San Domenico. Built in the mid-15th century as a hunting lodge of the Lampugnani, on two floors, it had frescoes of Roman history and rural life and coats of arms of the Lampugnoni, Visconti and Annoni families; the surviving fragments, noted by Guido Sutermeister in 1934, were detached and relocated together with Renaissance frescoes of wooden palaces, and today the tower also exhibits Renaissance paintings of demolished buildings in the twentieth century.
General nature reserve of about 195 hectares on the Serre di Burano, on the border between Marche and Umbria.
Tower of the late 10th century in the center of the village, one of the oldest in the region, seat of the Natalino Sapegno Foundation and the Bibliomuseum of comics.
An ancient monument outside the city.

Etruscan tombs in the countryside, excavated in limestone, an ancient seabed of about one million years old, with an ear of rabbit and two V-shaped chambers divided by a false column; remodelled in more recent times. Frequent guided tours, especially in summer, with the Proloco di Bibbona.
Basilica wanted by Theodoric: along the aisle run the processions of martyrs and virgins on a gold background.
The Romanesque sanctuary of the patrons, overlooking the valley.

In Solda, about 1,900 meters at the foot of the Ortles, an underground museum dedicated to ice and glaciers: mountains of ice, Arctic and Antarctica, avalanches, skis, ice climbing and polar expeditions, with the largest collection in the world of Ortles paintings and ice tools of two centuries. Designed by Reinhold Messner with the Venostano architect Arnold Gapp, it is placed in a hillside: concrete walls bent like ice crystals, a band of windows like a crevasse and a window that frames the top of the Ortles.

Insect in front of the Faraglioni di Capri, site of community interest in the Marine Protected Area of Punta Campanella, donated to the FAI by Italsider in 1987; once limestone quarry abandoned in the 1950s, today among Mediterranean maquis, olive groves and terraced citrus groves. You can reach it on foot from Nerano (about 40 minutes downhill, 1 hour uphill, medium difficulty) passing next to the sixteenth-century tower of Montalto, or by sea with authorized boats; the FAI offers guided tours by reservation.

In the former Mother Church, severely damaged by the earthquake of 1968 and rebuilt, it tells the night of the earthquake that destroyed in a few seconds the villages of the Belice Valley, and then the emergency, solidarity and protest: hundreds of photographs of the countries before and after the earthquake, literary quotations, paintings, audiovisual, newspapers and magazines of the time from private archives and collections.
Chapel in the hamlet Voragno, with frescoes probably from the 16th century.

Inaugurated in 2019 in the Town Hall, it is dedicated to the Madonie fir tree, endemic conifer rediscovered by botanists in 1957: five multimedia environments with video projections, sounds and an interactive panel, the last two rooms dedicated to the few natural specimens that grow between 1400 and 1650 meters in the Vallone Madonna degli Angeli.
Neoclassical theatre restored in 1814 and again in recent times, center of the city's cultural life.
A Roman village built at the Via Flaminia and the sources of the Clitunno, 412 meters above the Umbra valley, an oil town with the former convent of San Francesco and the olive museum.
Beach among the cliffs, alternative to Marina Grande; from the Gardens of Augusto descends the panoramic Via Krupp.
The Renaissance in Bronte.
Towers of sighting against Saracen incursions from the sea: the most famous are Apprezemi the donkey, Crivi, Acquafredda, Filocaio, Santavenere and Caina.
Fra' Umile's Crucifix.
The oldest mentioned church in the village.
Puccini's lake seen from the boat.
Pine trees and panorama to the Adriatic.
The Norman walls above Taormina.

Since 1998 in the former eighteenth-century convent of the Filippines: painted from the fifteenth to the eighteenth century by churches and convents; in the Crivelli room the polyptych of the Coronation of the Virgin, the triptych of the Visitation and the Franciscan Friar praying of the Venetian master, with silvers of the Brotherhood of Mercy and a section of graphics. Full 5 €, reduced 3 €, free under 19 years.
Touch the fossils of the Apennines with hands.
The baroque stucco of the Riviera in the center of the village.
The most spectacular Etruscan necropolis in the Maremma.
Bronze statue placed on a hill to protect the country, panoramic view of the coast.
Born in the nineteenth century as a refinery for the processing of sanse, oil and soap; the central façade and one of the two original towers remain visible.

The 15th-century defence tower, built to protect the cargo warehouses of Pozzallo from pirate raids; it is the symbol of the city and rises in the historic centre. On the state property complex of the Palazzo di Torre Cabrera the Region has started restoration and valorization works      Â for full use Â (first progress cleared in November 2024).
Architecture of the twentieth century in the mountains.
The great fourteenth-century cycle of the Master of Montiglio.
The coast that opens the Quartese coast along the Gulf of the Angels; more east Capitana with the marina and the natural pools of Is Mortorius.

Small archaeological museum in Fort Sangallo with finds of the territory, especially Romans: a section of paleontology and prehistory from the Pleistocene to the Iron Age and a Roman section with salt on the maritime trade (very from Torre Astura), sacred objects, funerary finds and villas.
The story of an Alpine pass between pilgrims, smugglers and the Fell railroad.
Free, always accessible
The fortress from which the name of the country was born.
The poet of Santa Margherita in multimedia version.

Established in the school year 1937-38 at the State Institute of Art, on the edge of the Ceramic Quarter, it preserves about 300 artifacts from 1887 to today: grottaglian majolica of the XVI-XVII centuries, works of the Institute of the early twentieth century and pieces made for national and international competitions.

The museum of the Italian language in the former monastery of the Holy Conception, in the complex of Santa Maria Novella, promoted with Crusca, Lincei, Treccani and Società Dante Alighieri; mandatory booking.

Municipality of the Media Valle del Serchio among the chestnut groves: in Celle dei Puccini the family home of the composer, in Vetriano the smallest historical public theatre in the world (well FAI), in Cologna the Castagno Museum and the seventeenth-century Molino di Menicone.
The trees at the top of the tower.
An ancient medieval stronghold that dominates the valley of Alento, of which the defensive front remains; from the top the look reaches the Gran Sasso and the Adriatic.
The most important romantic garden in Emilia-Romagna.

The new section, inaugurated on July 14, 2018, runs for 2 km suspended about 50 meters above the lake on a 2.5 meters wide footbridge to the border with Trentino; with the existing track from Nanzell to Capo Reamol the track measures 12 km. Illuminated LED, it is also possible to walk in the evening; limit of 10 km/h for bikes, cars in the car parks of the center.
A city of Magna Grecia on the sea, with its mosaics.
Inside the walls of the castle, with a cycle of paintings from 1370; at the end of September there are the most heartfelt festivals of the year.
The lion and the epigraph of Trajan.
Medieval plant, rebuilt in Baroque style.
The Verdicchio in his land.
Small village known for its murals.
The castle above the village, starting point of the path Marturano.
A concert at the end of the visit.
A place of Cagliari devotion.

The square-plan urban space of the historic centre, born in the 13th century with the abbey of Saints Vito and Salvo on a late-Roman settlement; the Museo Civico Porta della Terra collects Roman and Frentani finds, the Museo dell'Abbazia the monastic life between Trigno and Osento.
Park in the west of the country, inaugurated on June 5, 1993 and dedicated to Bruno Rabitti, mayor from 1964 to 1980.

The capital of Val Passiria on the road of Passo Giovo: at the Sandhof, the birthplace of Andreas Hofer, the MuseumPasseier; above the village the thirteenth-century tower of Castel Giovo (Jaufenburg) and the church of Sant'Ippolito in Le Coste with the only cycle of frescoes of the valley; from the bridge of the village starts the path in the gorge of Passirio towards Moso.

At the entrance of the valley stands San Lorenzo in Banale, considered the gateway to the Brenta Dolomites: alpine pastures and mountain paths in the Adamello Brenta Nature Park, starting point for trekking and hiking.
The oldest nucleus in the country.

Regional reserve of 244 hectares established in 1983, plain between the Ceriti Mountains and the sea with ponds, marshes and coastal woods: wet area of rest for migratory birds, observable from the huts. Paths of the Boschetto, the huts and the beach; in the rainy periods they can be unworkable.

Fortress documented from the 12th century, square with shoe walls and two towers, passed by Aldobrandeschi, Orsini, Siena and Florence; today it can be visited free of charge, with museum and temporary exhibitions.
A house of the Roman Concordia.
The most beautiful Baroque church of Salerno, rich in great quality frescoes.
The nineteenth-century garden with the small temple.

The square overlooking the Sasso Barisano, with access to the underground, and the Palazzo dell'Annunziata, a former convent of Dominican nuns with a clock on the pediment, seat of the Provincial Library Tommaso Stigliani.

On the main street of the historic center, it was built between 1631 and 1665 for the confraternity of the Disciplined of Saint Mary (documented from 1569), which from the early eighteenth century collected funds to redeem the Christian prisoners of the barbarians. Single nave full of stuccoes, furniture and marble; Bernardo Carrosio painted in 1665 the fresco of the facade and several internal canvases, and the right side altar preserves the relics of San Clemente and a view of Voltaggio of 1682. Open on summer weekends and oratory parties.

Town of villages at the top of the Grana Valley, in the Southern Cozie Alps, home of the DOP cheese: the San Magno sanctuary with the fifteenth-century frescoes by Pietro da Saluzzo, two small museums of mountain life, the Way of St. Magnus and the Colle Fauniera with the monument to Marco Pantani.

Mother church well maintained on the slope of the village, rebuilt in the twentieth century after the world wars, with a golden wooden high altar that Visit Molise indicates among the most beautiful in the region. A steep road above the church leads to a viewpoint over the Sangro valley, from which with clear sky you can see the Adriatic.
Nineteenth-century villa in the green of Maggianico, loved by Milanese scapigliati, now home of the Civic Music School.
A baroque corner of quiet.
Small rural church of the sixteenth century in Renaissance style, attributed to Girolamo da Vicenza, with sculptures by Silvestro dell'Aquila.
Villages of traditional architecture; in the spring Col Fenêtre, the peony blooms in an area of the Natura 2000 network.
The Tiber seen from the water.
The ladder to get on your knees.
The mother church that dominates the historic center.
The fountain of the six jets.
Secular holm oaks above the city.
The Benedictine Romanesque of Borgo Cerreto.

Inaugurated on December 7, 2019 next to San Lorenzo, in the ancient headquarters of the confraternity of the regulations of Saint Martha, it makes the heritage of the archpriest accessible. It exhibits a fresco of the Crucifixion attributed to a Lombard painter between the late fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries, the fifteenth-century cross astile (the most representative work), a Madonna with Child sculpted from the fifteenth century, the canvas of the Circumcision by Francesco Zucco, liturgical wallpapers and ex-vote painted by the church of Santa Maria Nascente di Debbio.

Open-air theatre with 2,000 places in a small semicircular quarry at the foot of the San Rocco quarry, one of the limestone quarries serving the mine; it hosts shows, festivals and cultural events every summer.
A mystery under the railroad.
Picnic and walks between Colbordolo and Montefabbri.
An isolated little church with centuries of ex-vote.
Three centuries of keyboards in a private house.

1,147 ex-vote, about 40% before the twentieth century, once hung on the walls of the sanctuary and now exposed in two large halls next to the guardian's house: testimony of the devotion and daily life of the community.

It preserves the traces of the Ricetto, the ancient fortified area then demolished; the ancient town hall houses the civic library and the School of Peace. Stone fountains, including the sixteenth century of Piazza dell'Olmo and the eighteenth century of Piazza Garibaldi.
The secular larch pines of Sila.

The centre of the Upper Irpinia on the Ofanto, heir to the ancient Compsa: the ancient village, abandoned after the 1980 earthquake, preserves the Roman forum and the cathedral in the archaeological park, while downstream the artificial lake is an oasis WWF.
A 17th century wooden crucifix.
On the monferrine traces of Christopher Columbus.
Street art international in a medieval village of 300 inhabitants.
In the former church of San Lorenzo of the 10th century, the finds of the city founded by the Romans in 218 BC and a domus of the 2nd century BC brought to light in the courtyards of Palazzo Zuccari.
The lake from above, on foot.

Owned by the Municipality and set up in 1997-98 by ANPI, which manages it with volunteers: about 400 photos, divided by partisans, alpine and garibaldini, underground newspapers, tables of deportees and internees, flags of the Star Division, German topographic maps and diaries of Ada Gobetti. Each year at the end of August the Battle of the Sevine Granges (24-25 August 1944) is remembered. Free visits by booking (museoreeistenzampantero@gmail.com, tel. 0122 32065).
The city on the water, on 118 islands of the lagoon, with calluses, canals and palaces on the Grand Canal; Venice and its lagoon are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The oldest crypt in Jesi.

The village lies on a spur of tuff; since 1883, on the first Sunday of July, the families of the village stretch out a carpet of flowers over a kilometre and a half long, recognized in 2012 by the Guinness of the Primates as the world's largest inflorate (1,642.57 m2).

Of medieval origins (XII-XIII century) and renovated from the sixteenth century, it is known for its Romanesque bell tower. Inside a six-seventh-century altarpiece with the Unbelief of St. Thomas and stucco statues attributed to the Giani.
The place of the burial of Stradivari.
Medieval village in the hamlet of Naggio, with the chapel of Santa Croce dell'alto Medievalo.
temporarily closed for restoration work
The walled village seen by the river.
Cited from the fifteenth century, it houses a table of the Madonna and Child to which are connected numerous miracles.

Established in 2007, he exhibits the protagonists of Livorno painting between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, such as Renato Natali, Guglielmo Micheli, Giovanni Lomi and Giovanni Marchi, alongside more famous authors such as Renato Guttuso, Domenico Purificato, Remo Gordigiani and Anacleto Margotti; he periodically hosts temporary exhibitions. Admission without reservation, open Thursday, Saturday and Sunday 15:30-18:30.
Parish of the eighteenth century; the feast of the patron is held at the end of June.
The city of students.
The scenic portal that gave access to the Barchetto della Pineta, Medici hunting reserve of the Royal Barco.
The Messapians of Brindisi told from their finds.

Large otium villa on a cliff overlooking the sea, buried by the eruption of 79 A.D.: the oldest nucleus, of the first century B.C., revolves around a Tuscany atrium with paintings of II style, and in the middle of the first century A.D. the complex expanded eastward with a pool of 61 by 17 meters. The excavations, begun in the Bourbon era and resumed in the twentieth century, have exposed about 90 rooms on more than 10,000 square meters, with paintings of III style like Hercules in the garden of the Esperides and gardens rebuilt with Paleobotanic studies; an inscription on amphorae the league to the family of Poppea Sabina, wife of Nero. It is the only monument of the ancient Oplontis open to the public: the nearby Villa B of Lucius Crassius Tertius, center of wine and oil processing where in 1984 were found the "Ori di Oplontis" (Ori di Oplontis) is not open to visitors.
The bridge of Etruscan origin completed by the Romans, 30 meters high, that crosses the gorge of the Fiora and connects the castle.
Municipal museums only partially usable (Let's Marche)
An eighteenth-century church that preserves the twenty sculptural groups of the Passion carried in procession on Good Friday.
Long sandy beaches alternated with cliffs, with a sea of colors that change with light: Rivabella, Lido San Giovanni, Baia Verde, Punta della Suina and Lido Pizzo.
Birdwatching in the gorge.
The five crosses symbol of the country.

Large courtyard farmhouse: to the north, along the road, an oratory with the chaplain's house and the castle, the only surviving building of the ancient court. Along the avenue of access the pigsty and the court of the housekeeper with portico; on the west side of the main court dairy with carpentry and dryer, manor house and pile; to the south the house of the farmer with stables and the beef barn, to the east a portico and to the north the new bull stable, rebuilt after a fire.
Since 1960 the Biennale del Muro Dipinto has left on the facades of the village works by Italian and foreign artists.
The city's symbol tower.
The Gothic-Aragonese in Barbagia.
Villas and gardens to discover by bike.
It preserves in a lateral altar the original table of the Madonna delle Macchie and, on the high altar, a wooden tabernacle of the last quarter of the sixteenth century.

Outside the walls, with the former convent: rebuilt between the late fourteenth and early fifteenth centuries and modified in 1707, it preserves two remarkable cycles of frescoes from the fifteenth century and is part of the city's museum circuit.

In the former renovated municipal slaughterhouse, since 2019 the exhibition "Pompei oltre le mura" shows frescoed walls and objects of the Roman villas of Cava Ranieri (Ville 1, 2 and 6) buried by the eruption of 79 A.D.: second style paintings with architectural perspectives, restored by the archaeological park of Pompeii, and the larario of the kitchen of Villa 6 with two Lari, the genius who sacrifices and two snakes. Since 2025, a new room has been showing the Terzigno Treasure of the Villa 2: silver (a situla with swan-head, a cup, a mirror, 21 coins) and three gold necklaces, one with emeralds. Free admission with a valid Pompeii ticket.
The traditional wooden houses with roofs of grey stone slabs and balconies with trellis, called "lobbies" used for drying hay, hemp and rye.
The alpine pasture with the pilgrim's oratory.

It rises on the basaltic plateau of Sa Corona Arrubia, covered with red lichens, between the countryside of Lunamatrona and Collinas, and is dedicated to Giovanni Pusceddu, historian mayor of Villanovaforru. It has three permanent sections: fauna, with eight life-size dioramas of jars, holm oak woods, riparian environments and arid pastures; botany, with mycotheque, xyloteca, herbarium and medicinal plants; anthropic, with the reconstruction of a prenuragic dwelling, reproductions of sites of the area and tools of the peasant life of the Marmilla. Outside there is a geobotanic park with educational trails; open every day 9:00-19:00, free guided tours by reservation (data updated at 8/5/2025).
A noble village to walk through fountains and palaces.

The sixteenth-century palace, symbol of Sacile and its link with the Serenissima: it was the home of the Venetian Ragazzoni, owners and bankers, and together the point of collection of the production of their land properties. It is reached through a canal and is decorated with frescoes by a pupil of Paolo Veronese.
From the old town, trails start on foot, by bike or on horseback, reaching the naturalistic areas along the Knight and Vandra streams.

Excursion indicated as easy of 7-8 km (about 3 hours) from Bocca di Selva, reached by Bosco following the signs for San Giorgio: you go up to the refuge Podestaria (1655 m) and then to Mount Tomb, with views of the Carega, the Dolomites and Mount Baldo.
A stop along the bike path of the lake.
A climb between frescoed chapels and ancient hamlets.

Medieval town on the north side of Mount Etna, in the middle of three protected areas (Etna, Nebrodi and Alcantara), built around three lava stone churches (Santa Maria, San Nicolò and San Martino) that correspond to the Latin, Greek and Lombard districts; in the Swabian Castle the Archaeological Museum Paolo Vagliasindi is located.
Church of the 13th century.
One of Napoletano's greatest contemporary art collections.
The peasant tools with the name in dialect.

Verbicaro was considered the capital of Calabrian winemaking and its wine has been Doc since 1995; it survives the crushing in the palm and in the casts, the cellars where the barrels are preserved and you find yourself eating and singing. On December 8th, the feast of the "perciavutt" opens the castuvi with tastings of cold cuts and wine.

Late Baroque building inspired by Lecce on the homonymous square: over one hundred rooms, many frescoed, with the gallery on the outside loggia and a small private chapel. Visit methods not indicated by official sources.
The Insigne Collegiata di San Leonardo, several times renovated, with the churches of Sant'Antonio, Santa Maria della Colonna, early Christian on a pagan temple, and San Michele Arcangelo.
The seat of the National Roman Museum established in 1889, with one of the most important archaeological collections in the world.
The baptismal font of 1156.

It preserves a collection on the sedentary and migratory birdlife of the Larian territory, a scientific library of over 1,500 volumes, monographs and brochures of ornithology, zoology, malacology and botany, and the epistolary of scholar Luigi Scanagatta.
The fifteenth-century crucifix of the parish church.
In a typical ancient house of Stolvizza, with a section dedicated to the local tradition of fairy tales.
A medieval lookout on Francigena.
the Municipality indicates temporary closure for earthquake damage

The village retains the molten shape, with two rows of houses to act as a defensive belt; the oldest part, on the Colle della Regina where there was a first fortified center, dominates the gorge of the Foce excavated by the Sangro. evocative alleys also portraits from Escher, the \'v'ttalÂ that from the main street descend to the ancient stables, the seventeenth-century palace of the Town Hall and the view of the Marsicano, the Val Fondillo and the chains of the Camosciara.
Traditional costumes with gold embroideries and accessories, in two sections: Albanians in southern Italy from 15th century immigration, with dolls and historical photos, and traditions in Albania.
The most famous monstrous statues of Sicily.
Regional reserve of 1,450 hectares established in 2009, with the Canfaito plateau at about 1,100 meters and its centuries-old beech woods.

Country of the Carnic Prealps overlooking the Balcony of Friuli, with the parish church of San Giacomo, a pilgrimage destination, and on the Pradis plateau the karst caves with the Orrido and the Grotta Museum dedicated to prehistory.
Romanesque frescoes between apple orchards and vineyards.
Abini's nuragic bronze and Teti's 'Venus'.

Peninsula on the southern shore of Garda, closed at the entrance from the fourteenth-century Scaliger Castle with its dock and, at the tip, from the remains of the large Roman villa called Grotte di Catullo; in the middle a historic center of churches of different eras, sulphurous spas known from the Roman age and white rock beaches.

A stone bridge with two asymmetrical arches, with parapet and rostrums of Roman origin; it is not documented, but it is believed to date back to the end of the XII and the beginning of the XIV century. It is one of the most photographed views of the village, with the houses and the high bell tower of the parish in the background; always accessible on foot.
The art of Abruzzo in one museum.
A tour of the noble residences of the country.
Small 11th century church in the upper quarter, the oldest place of worship in Veroli.
Alpine architecture rare in the Maira Valley.
Palace of the eighteenth century, several times renovated, which preserves ceramics of Tommaso and Giovacchino Cascella, paintings of Alfonso Muzii and prints of Basilio Cascella.

In the historic center, dedicated to the pine loricato symbol of the Pollino Park, which grows on the peaks of Serra Dolcedorme and Serra delle Ciavole: finds, photos of the tree in its environment and panels on the types, diffusion and scientific characteristics. From June to September 9-13 and 15.30-19.30, in winter by reservation.
Old bank and notebooks.
The house-study of a genius of fabrics and light.
The frescoes of Girolamo di Giovanni in the castle.
The theatre dedicated to the composer Jesino.
The gulf from above.
the FAI card describes the remains as dilapidated and asks for their safety; visitability not indicated

Medieval fortification from the mighty walls, on a hill overlooking the village and the surrounding landscape; born with military function, today it is a historical symbol of the country and houses exhibitions, concerts, theatre shows, art exhibitions and local crafts and an information point for tourists. According to the municipality is open Monday-Friday 9:30-13 and 15-18, Saturday and Sunday 10-18, partially accessible to people with disabilities.
Borgo della Langa del Barolo, Bandiera Arancione and the most beautiful village in Italy, with the outdoor amphitheatre dedicated to Horszowski on top of the ancient village.
A Renaissance polyptych by Andrea da Salerno.

Border town between Latin, Slavic and Germanic cultures, European Capital of Culture 2025 with Nova Gorica: the medieval castle with the village and provincial museums, noble palaces such as Attems Petzenstein and Coronini Cronberg, Transalpina Square on the border with Slovenia and parks along the Isonzo.

Born in the 13th century as the gate of Castelvecchio, the first nucleus of the city, it became a tower in 1438 under the Gonzaga with the first clock and was then raised to the present 27 meters: it is the tallest building of Castel Goffredo. Seven floors and 117 steps, with a museum path on walls, doors, moat and vellum of the two defensive belts; a spiral staircase crosses the bell cell to the Belvedere, overlooking the Po Valley, the Prealps and, on clear days, the Apennines. Open from Thursday to Sunday, last ascent at 16:45; hosts the Infopoint.
It keeps 18 well-preserved bodies, mummified naturally due to a particular mold present in the area.
In the Institute's Palace, torture instruments with explanatory panels; next to an escape room with Inquisition theme.
Medieval alleys overlooking the lake.
Alleys and arches of the ancient village.
The fifteenth-century Palazzo del Podestà and the sixteenth-century Palazzo Albertini, on the sides of the square, are the venues of temporary exhibitions.
Pilgrimage stop.

Between 1600 and 1604 the Republic of Venice dug an artificial canal of about 7 km to divert the Po southwards, in the direction of Sacca di Goro. The territory, between Po di Venezia and Po di Levante, you can cycle along the canals between hydraulic artifacts and abandoned chimneys of brick kilns.
The church of Barisano.
In a former cellar with barrel vaults in front of the castle, about 500 corkscrew from the eighteenth century to today in 19 sections.
Gothic on the waterfront.
The Medici villa on the Arno, part of the UNESCO site, seen from outside along the bike path; in the park there is the Archaeological Museum.
The two twin fortresses in the valley.
Rebuilt after the earthquake of 1688, it preserves the relics of another Saint Pius donated by the Carafa family at the beginning of the nineteenth century.
Twenty mummies under a church.
MiC card (Add. 2021) indicates the museum closed every day (tel. 0784 65508)
In the middle of the village.

A quadrangular castle built around 1130 by Guglielmo Gesualdo, relative of Ruggero II, on the border with the Pontifical Benevento, and enlarged in the fifteenth century with four cylindrical angular towers; in the mid-500s it became residence of the feudalists (Bonito, Orsini, D'Aquino, Pisanello, Garofalo) and in 1829 it was sold to private individuals. After the earthquakes of 1702 and 1980 there are two towers: the one on the Town Hall square contains paintings probably seventeenth century on the walls and on the wooden ceiling.
The fortified heart of the basalt village.
Roman hydraulic engineering under the country.
The viewpoint on Sabina.
A collection square.

Rocky site between Sortino and Ferla, at the confluence of the valley of Calcinara in that of the Anapo: settlement of the late Bronze Age (XIII-VIII century BC) with almost five thousand graves carved into the rock, the largest rock necropolis in Europe, reoccupied in the Byzantine age with cave villages and churches like San Micidario. There is the Anaktoron, the only megalithic building of mycenaean type in Sicily. UNESCO World Heritage Site with Syracuse since 2005; from Ferla you can access the entrance near the village (about 11 km).
In Piazza Ottinetti, in the former 14th-century convent of Santa Chiara, three collections on the history of the city.

Borgo all'incocco della Val di Sole, on the banks of the Noce between woods and apple orchards, entered among the most beautiful villages of Italy in 2023: the name comes from an ancient hot spring today disappeared. Castel Caldes dominates it, a Gothic castle dating back to the thirteenth century of the Thun family today in the Buonconsiglio circuit, with the legend of Olinda prisoner; in the village the cemetery church of San Rocco and a center of houses with stone portals and mullioned windows.

Triangular square, heart of the village, reorganized at the end of the eighteenth century. The Town Hall in brick has a loggia of thirteen columns in travertine and a fifteenth-century portico; the tower is of the fourteenth century and the crowning of swallows of 1924.
Much of the valley is in the park, which has its center visits to Prato, the capital of the municipality.
Five thousand years of seals.

At 2,035 meters, 17 km from the village, it is described as the highest sanctuary in Europe reachable by car. Born as an alpine shelter for pilgrims coming from Provence, it is still a pilgrimage destination: near the rock of the apparition, with the statue of the saint, tradition wants St. Anne to appear to the shepherd Anna Bagnis; next to there are the San Gioachino refuge and the ancient house of the rancher, the guardian of the pilgrims.
The ramparts hide passages used as armories and ammunition deposits; the Baluardo di San Colombano preserves two lions of the thirteenth century.
Baroque fillings and a majolica bell tower.
Sanctuary with elegant bell tower, with frescoes by Salmeggia, Ceresa, Cappella e Raggi and, in the crypt, a wooden group by Fantoni.
Fraction with 16th century tower, 18th century church and gardens once of the local nobles.
Venice seen in front.
Lakes and woods under the Ogliastra heels.
Two frescoes on a hamlet facade.

At about one kilometer above Massa, probably founded at the end of the XII century as a viewer and still in the fourteenth century guarded for the Lucchesi; it has fishbone plant Â Â Â along the main road, with the oratories of San Filippo Neri and the Company and at the end the church of San Jacopo, rebuilt and enlarged in the sixteenth century. The walls and the doors to Massa, Vecchia and Nuova remain; just outside Porta Nuova the panorama embraces the Valdinievole and on clear days Volterra and Elba.
The funnel roundabout, inspired by the Pantheon.
Benedictine memory in the Dauna countryside.
€5, reduced €2,50, family €5 (including guided tour)
Monastery founded between 1230 and 1235, with Baroque interiors and paintings by Jusepe de Ribera, Pietro da Cortona and Francesco de Mura.

Multimedia teaching hall in the former railway station, with historical archive and materials on the life of those who passed through the camp of Servigliano: built at the beginning of the twentieth century for about 10,000 prisoners, it housed about 10,000 in the First World War and about 20,000 people in the Second (followed, Jews and families helping them), then between 1945 and 1955 between 40,000 and 50,000 refugees, including Julian-Dalmati. Times indicated: July and August Mon-Fri 9-14, Sat 15-20; other months Mon-Fri 9-14 (afternoon by reservation), Sat 15-20 (morning by reservation), Sunday on request.
A De Magistris fresco.
The villa of Pompeo Mariani.
open for the patronal feast of December 4, on the occasion of events or by reservation

A country church called Madonna della Visitazione, less than five kilometers south of the village and about 1000 meters, among the highest churches on the island; described in the nineteenth century by Alberto Della Marmora, was demolished in 1976 and rebuilt. The Fonnesi families organize novena, procession and folk shows, hosted in the two rows of cumbessias next to the church.

The ring of 9 km (about 4 hours, maximum altitude 614 m) proposed by the Municipality: starts from the Piazzetta del Teatrino, runs along the Topino along the Green Route, climbs to the remains of the Roman villa and to the church of Santa Cristina, crosses the forest towards the Madonna Contadina near Carié, reaches the Castle of Poggio and descends to Ponte Rio; a variant leads to the Laghetto di Sasso and to the Castle of Gallano.
The prehistory of Salento in one museum.
Plastic of the region created by the canon Pierre Louis Vescoz between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, which can be visited by reservation.

Built between 27 B.C. and 14 A.D. on the eastern edge of the ancient city, gift of the magistrate M. Vecilius Campus; it measures about 130 by 95 meters and hosted 16-18 thousand spectators, with arena, podium and four entrances. Ticket office from Tuesday to Sunday 9-16.30.
Climb the tower to embrace the whole Trasimeno.
A church in the rock.
A 15th century triptych in the heart of the village.

Medieval village of the Dauni Mountains dominated by the Norman-Ange Tower and the Ducal Palace, with the Terravecchia district with fishbone, the Mother Church of Santa Maria Assunta and, a few kilometers away, the archaeological site of Montecorvino.
The coast seen from the sea.
Private collection in Torri, in nine sections, with tools, tools and everyday objects collected by the owner Renzo Innocenti.
A stop on the streets of medieval pilgrims.
A Roman chip under the porch.

Built in 1977 as a warehouse of excavation materials and opened with a first exhibition nucleus in 1998, it presents in six sections finds from the protohistory to the imperial age, including the statuary cycle of the Augustales sacellus in a life-size reconstruction and the funeral monument with Gladiatory relief recovered in 2006 by Fiano Romano. Tuesday-Saturday 8.30-19.30; Sunday only the first and third of the month.
The stone tomb of 1390.
Baroque frescoes.
Hand woven hemp.
16th century church in the village.
A crossroads rises between olive trees and woods to the sanctuary of Santa Maria di Laghel, in a panoramic position above Arco.
The first men of Italy.

Church of 1258 on the place of the church of San Legonziano, where tradition places the miracle of the eighth century; a single nave with a Baroque style frescoed vault and eighteenth-century organ, keeps the relics on the main altar.

Carro is the village of origin of the Paganini family and there is the house of the ancestors of the Genoese composer, the ancient pagan residence that is the background of the Paganini Festival. The regional portal announced its inauguration on 26 June, in the 25th edition of the festival, as a study centre dedicated to listening to and promoting the musician's works.
The sandstone portal.

The path no. 6, suitable for all, leads to a panoramic platform on the Laga Mountains and the ancient Via Salaria; the territory is also crossed by the Grande Anello dei Sibillini, a 120 km hiking trail completely signposted along the entire chain.
Art and nature together.
Included in the abbey visit
The oldest parish church in Carnia on the hill that gives the name to the village.
The sixteenth-century church of St. Lucia, patron saint of the village, was the private chapel of the lords; next to it stands the Palazzo Borghese, today seat of the Town Hall.
A sabauda farmhouse among the rice fields.
The boulevard that leads from the center to the golenal woods on the banks of the Po, with the area of Lido Po.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione on the hills between Misa and Nevola, called Montalboddo until 1881: Piazza dei Martiri with the Neoclassical Town Hall, the civic tower and the Theatre La Vittoria, the medieval belt of 1200 meters, the Collegiate Church of Santa Croce in the low town planned between two and fourteenth century, San Francesco with the paintings of Hercules Ramazzani and the Marian shrine of the Madonna della Rosa.
The work of Bozzola inside the walls.
The Voltaggio postcard: medieval bridge, houses and bell tower.
Drawings of great masters in town hall.
The holy painting on the palace.
Ethnographic museum, example of traditional Valdostan architecture.

Erected in 1395 on the remains of Roman buildings, for almost four centuries residence of the Acquaviva d'Aragona, today seat of the Municipality; it preserves a nativity scene of the sixteenth century.
A prismatic tower of the thirteenth century, known as the Tower of the Bishop, with stone coats of arms and the trace of a fresco by Luca Signorelli in 1474; it climbs up to the top.

In the Natural Park of Monti Lucretili, with an art journey of seven sculptures in Roman travertine made in 2011 by students of the course of environmental sculpture of the Academy of Fine Arts of Rome.
A small 19th-century theatre still active.
A Gothic church with a starry vault.
The cloister of the first Benedictine monastery of Sicily.
In September the feast of the fishing queen.

Complex of industrial hydraulics on the banks of Ticino, along the European path E1 and the river and cycle path of the waterways, with the former tollgate of hydraulic guardianship. Guided tours every Sunday at 10.30 am by reservation (limited places; other days for groups of at least 15 people); reduced for children 6-10 years, free up to 5 years and for people with disabilities; dogs allowed on leash.
The medieval fortified village, Gregoriopoli from the IX century, with the terraced houses of Cardinal d'Estouteville and the castle of Baccio Pontelli (1483-1487) for Cardinal Giuliano della Rovere.
The relic of Saint Thomas.

On the plateau above the Biferno valley, along the Celano-Foggia tracturo, stood a large Roman rustic villa (II-I century BC, enlarged in imperial age with a thermal sector), inhabited until the 5th century, with white, black and greenish tiles floors. On its ruins there was a necropolis of more than 70 crated tombs (VI-VII century) and in 1017 the churches of Casalpiano were donated to Montecassino. After the earthquake of 1456 the church was rebuilt next to the original: the new Romanesque façade with rose window, portal of the 12th century and three apses, flanked by cloister and Renaissance hostel, while the ancient church remains three well preserved apses. The site is state-owned.

Borgo dei Monti Cimini between centuries-old chestnut groves, with the Anguillara Castle, the sixteenth-century Palazzo Farnese seat of the Municipality and the Museum of popular traditions in the former Carmelite convent; on the hill the thirteenth-century church of Santa Corona, destination of a pilgrimage among the chestnut trees.
The fourteenth-century church with a single aisle guarding the body of Blessed Margaret, the blind one of the Metola, until 1808 there was the Mond Crucifixion of Raphael, today in London.
A quick lunch between mosaics.
The frescoes of the Golden Ass of Apuleio.
An architectural curiosity.
A shrine outside the door.
Medieval alleys of a mountain country.
The studio of a sculptor who remained as he was.

Centre of Alta Brianza at the foot of the Lariano Triangle, with the Romanesque Sant'Eufemia in Incino, the Hermitage of San Salvatore and the Pessina Cross above Crevenna, the Teatro Licinium of 1928, historic villas such as Villa Amalia and, in Valle Bova, the cave of the Hole of Lead with the remains of the cave bear.
The sunset on the Great Sea.

Park of 5 hectares in the center of the village, with pond and stage on the water for cultural events, lighted tennis courts, pavilion for the elderly, walking and running trails, rest areas and a botanical didactic path.
An extraordinary schedule of archaeological structures that allows to retrace the history of the central sector of the city from the Roman Age to the Middle Ages.
The baroque altar in polychrome marble.

The National Monumental Library of the Abbey preserves about 100,000 volumes; in the upper room 17 paintings by the late 16th century painter G.B. Zelotti decorate the wooden ceiling. You usually visit the second and fourth Saturdays of the month together with the visit to the monastery, with tickets bookable on Eventbrite; to climb there are about 50 steps.
Iron Age Tombs.

For the position on the ancient trade routes between north and south of Europe Bormio enjoyed long autonomy and wealth: for about seven hundred years it was a democracy in the heart of the Alps. The center preserves medieval remains and civil and religious buildings of the XIV-XVI centuries, narrow streets with portals, frescoes of the fifteenth to sixteenth century on the facades, fountains and wash-houses; in Piazza Cavour dominates the collegiate church of Saints Gervasio and Protasio, and the church of San Vitale has fourteenth-century frescoes on the façade.
The rooms of the Vanvitelli in a hamlet of the Bassa Piantina.
Contemporary Italian art in the valley.
The true story of a hidden treasure off the Elbe.

Made to be built by Count Ruggero I in the 11th century to affirm the Latin rite, it was damaged by the earthquake of 1643, rebuilt in 1737 by Bishop Michele Abati, destroyed again in 1783 and reconsecrated in 1798 by Bishop Nicola Notaris. Domina piazza del Duomo, is a cathedral of the Archdiocese of Catanzaro-Squillace and since 2015 a minor basilica.

The 12th century castle overlooking the medieval village, with four factory buildings and corner towers around a quadrangular courtyard open on a loggia; lost the defensive role became residence of royals and nobles, and on September 9, 1943 the royal family found hospitality in escape from Rome occupied. Restored in the 1970s, it is linked to the legend of the ...Torre dell'ulivo" (Torre dell'ulivo) where the new owners De Riseis planted an olive tree in peace to drive out ghosts.
The bell tower that marks the center of the village.
The view of the lake from the terrace of the Ciociaria.

On the highest hill in the country, at 281 meters: the cassero, an ancient cistern, a crenellated wall with a bifora of the XI-XV and an aqueduct of the Thirties; in the castron the excavations, a helmet, a armour and medieval weapons.
The "vera cathedral" of the Fortore and its tower-tower.

From the summit the panorama ranges from Valnerina to Greccio, to Lake Piediluco, to Rieti and Leonessa; numerous hiking trails and, in winter, a small ski area with a cross-country trail and some descents for beginners.

At Capo Granitola there are two towers built around 1553-1554, the circular-plan Mazara Tower and the Saurel Tower known as the ancient lighthouse, and the 38-metre-high military lighthouse with 153 steps, completed in 1862, visible up to 23 miles.
Wine and oil at the time of the Romans a short walk from the beach.
A 16th century building in the medieval village, it houses a Madonna of Mercy by Vincenzo Pagani (1577) and a Via Crucis by a Grottammare sculptor.
€12 whole; €8 under 25, over 65 and groups; €3 under 18; free up to 6 years
A country of crafts rebuilt outdoors.
The predator center.
Sea of the Riviera of the Cedars.
Excursions for a fee or with the Comacchio Museum Pass
The merchants' houses.
The Roman villa of the Sele plain.
The sacred heart of the country.
Contemporary art in an 18th century villa.

Municipality of the high Val Curone made of many villages: in the capital the Romanesque-Gothic parish of Santa Maria Assunta, in Lunassi and Morigliassi two museums of the peasant civilization with free entrance, in Caldirola the plateaus of Gioia between the peaks of Giarolo, Panà, Ebro and Chiappo.
A church of the twelfth century marked by war.

The urban nucleus is born from the union of the ancient districts Terra, Borgo and Casale. According to tradition, the name comes from a hunting trip by Frederick II, who had a big boar cooked for dinner: they remember the town coat of arms, with a wild boar pierced by an arrow, and the tomb in the clock Tower, one of the few surviving ancient buildings, with the inscription "coena dat et aper nomen tibi Apricoena" (inscription "coena dat et aper nomen tibi Apricoena").
The throat that opens on the Notebook.

Panoramic terrace built in 1903 by engineer Luca Betti to connect the lower square to the ancient center, to the right of the basilica; the fountain has a statue of the three hills on which the city stands and two tombstones remember the fallen in Libya (1913) and Fabio Giovagnoli (1909).
Augusta Gallery of 705 meters excavated in the tuff by the architect Lucio Cocceio Aucto to join Naples to the Campi Flegrei, with the eastern entrance inside the Virgilio Park.
The rope path.
Built around 1165 in Romanesque style and renovated in Baroque times, with portal adorned with reliefs and numerous valuable works inside.
The oldest market in Padua.

Established in the spring of 2005, in the 60th of the Liberation, and dedicated to the partisan Gian Paolo Larini, who worked as a doctor in the valley; the fruit of thirty years of research, he exhibits in chronological order, from 8 September 1943 to 9 May 1945, about 600 original pieces among objects of war, letters and photographs, over 50 oral testimonies and documents launched by the Allied planes on the Apennines.
The church inside the walls.

Cameri is one of the eleven municipalities of the Piedmontese park, which covers about 6.560 hectares along the banks of the Ticino and with the Lombardy park forms the largest protected river area in Europe, in the UNESCO MAB network and Natura 2000. The landscape alternates with forests (about 60% of the surface), meadows, farmsteads, mills, canals, grets and larch, with herons, royal germans and the rare gloomy pelobate. From Villa Picchetta cycle and pedestrian routes start.
€8, reduced €6 (groups, FAI, Card of the Duchy), 11-18 years €5, 6-10 years €3, free 0-5 years
The shrine of the August feast.

Hunting and fishing casino built between 1923 and 1928 for Mario Malvezzi on a project by Duilio Torres, which brought to the lagoon the model of the Dutch farm: main building, boat and sighting tower with external spiral staircase. In the 1930s and later, Ernest Hemingway and Salvador Dalí spent holiday periods there, and in 1976 it was a set of a film by Tonino Cervi; today it belongs to the Roncato family. You can admire it from the water, with boat excursions in the southern lagoon from Chioggia or Venice, or from the surrounding area.
It has a thirteenth century entrance to the medieval village, with three crosses that would remember three bandits hanged in the sixteenth century.
Contemporary art collection with works by Carrà, Morandi, De Chirico and Ligabue.
Painting, history and theatre machines in the castle.

Baroque city of the Iblei rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693 and among the eight centers of the UNESCO site of the late Baroque towns of the Val di Noto: the churches with façade of the tower of San Sebastiano and San Paolo, the Madonna del Laurana all'Immacolata, the Antonino Uccello Museum House and, on the hill, the ancient Akrai founded by Siracusa in 664 BC, with the theater and the rock sanctuary of the Santoni.
€3, reduced €2; cumulative €5, reduced €4
A small treasure chest of Romanesque art in Valcuvia.
Visit Bergamo indicates the church closed for restoration, without reopening date
Neapolitan Baroque and Vaccaro's last paintings.
Fraction on the hill with the typical castle, the walls and an imposing mast; 506 meters, a short walk from the archaeological area of Urvinum Hortense.
Baroque plums and pulpit.
A complex nuraghe in white stone.
The flavors of the village to take home.
An interior collected out of the circuits.

The boats "Airone" and "Martin Pescatore" run from 23 places each along the Tiber between the landing places of Nazzano and Torrita Tiberina in about an hour; a longer itinerary arrives under Sant'Oreste. Along the river you can also go canoeing.
A medieval chapel linked to the castle.
On the trail of the scientist.

In an apartment on Piazza Leandra, discovered in 1972 behind a wall during a renovation: tempera paintings that reproduce the Room of Eliodoro di Raffaello and his school in the Vatican (Messa di Bolsena, Liberation of St. Peter, Meeting of Leo Magno with Attila, Hunting of Eliodoro). The origin is discussed: the age of Raphael, the late eighteenth century or the local painter Tommaso Bigatti (1760-1834).
The relics of the Magi in an eighteenth-century reliquary.
In the Pceptory there are medieval frescoes on the Passion of Christ.
The glass island with the Glass Museum, the shops where you can see the glass and basilicas of Saints Mary and Donatus and Saint Mary of the Angels.
A large historical garden, free of charge.

Romanesque bell tower separated from the church of Santa Caterina d'Alessandria, built around the end of the fourteenth century: it is the only building of Curon Vecchia spared when in 1950 the village was demolished and submerged by the basin, with the inhabitants expropriated and forced to leave the houses in about a week. Legend has it that in the windy days the bells are still heard, removed before flooding; in winter, with the frozen lake, you can reach them on foot.
The most spectacular Liberty façade in the Val Brembana.
The diary of Baracca in a small town museum.
The historic centre, which has been developed since the 12th century, preserves facades painted in trompe l'oeil and portals in slate from the 15th and 16th centuries.

The capital of the Val di Fiemme and seat of the Magnificent Community, which for about a thousand years has managed the woods of the valley: its palace with a gallery and 19th century prisons, the parish church of the Assunta in the Parco della Pieve with the Banco de la Resòn and the Centre of Contemporary Art in a historic palace in the centre.

Church indicated by the Palace of Caserta as a significant expression of the architectural culture of the Vanvitellian school, in the country linked to the legacy of Luigi Vanvitelli and the Carolino Aqueduct.
The Renaissance mausoleum of the De Capua princes.
Colorful houses and Liberty palaces on the Gulf of Tigullio, a few kilometers from Portofino.
The double water jump of the Bregaglia Valley.

Rebuilt by Ibleto di Challant at the end of the fourteenth century and transformed a century later by Prior Giorgio di Challant into a luxurious residence between the late Gothic and early Renaissance; in the courtyard the fountain with the wrought iron pomegranate. At the end of the nineteenth century Vittorio Avondo restored decorations and furnishings.

Born in 1913 for the centenary of the Muratian village and inaugurated in 1919, since 1977 it has been in a medieval palace house with a three-storey tower connected to the Petroni Arch: documents, weapons, archive and paintings of the Tanzi family.
The mural of street artist Millo, among the most photographed places in the city.
Strong overlooking the sea that houses the archaeological civic museum dedicated to the discoverer of Albintimilium, with over 700 finds.
The Abruzzo told in one museum.
The 19th century theatre known for its extraordinary acoustics.
The work of mines, woods and looms of the high valley.
The cathedral of the apparition.

Museum opened in 2001 in a medieval castle of the 13th century, the main site of the Ladin provincial museum: it tells history, language, culture, archaeology, geology, legends, crafts and tourism development of the Ladin valleys of the Dolomites; halls and courtyard host exhibitions, concerts and seminars. Open from 1 May to 1 November, from Tuesday to Sunday at 10-18; only partially wheelchair accessible.
Romantic park of 48,000 m2, with canals, caves and paths, built in 1854 by the Jacur family in addition to the villa.
€10, reduced 7-12 years €5, groups and passport Castles of the Duchy €8
Alleys and stone portals between Majella and Morrone.
Circular icebox of 1835 designed by the engineer Curtial in the area of public streets, today home of the Pro Loco and exhibition space.

Borgo del Biellese orientale, for centuries pontifical fief of Ferrero Fieschi with its own mint: the historic center preserves the seventeenth-century Palazzo dei Principi, today municipality, the Collegiate of the Annunziata and the church of San Teonesto, the oldest in the country, among the hills of vineyards of Bramaterra.
The alpine life of the upper valley.
The hamlet of the artists and the Thursday market.
It has a bronze portal of the sculptor Cecco Bonanotte.

Wanted by Camillo Benso di Cavour and built between 1862 and 1866, it is the third canal of Italy for length (almost 85 km): it brings the Po water to the rice fields of Vercellese and Novara up to Ticino. The stone and brick gripping building is 40 meters long, with 21 lights and three orders of gates; next to the bronze monument of 1898 by Francesco Porzio to the engineer Carlo Noè, designer of the work. The interior is visited only by reservation during the extraordinary openings with guided tour.
The center of Montefeltresco and the painter of the house.
Galileo's finger, really.
Crivelli polyptychs.
Borgo della val di Vara collected under the castle Doria Malaspina, which houses the cultural centers of the village, including the Pinacoteca David Beghè and the Piccolo Museo Pietro Rosa.
A stone village suspended on the gorges.
A single nave church with Baroque interiors, wall paintings and an ancient organ; Italia.it date 1779, an elliptical plant, rebuilt in 1939 by the Salusturi Galli family. First Sunday of December.
The fifteenth-century church was modified in the seventeenth century, with a marble triptych from 1529 and a wooden triptych from the fourteenth century, on the small square of the village.

Founded by architect and artist Leonardo Mosso with Laura Castagno, his father Nicola and friends artists and architects: born as an association in 1979, became a museum in 1984. It preserves collections and testimonies of the European twentieth century and the studios and archives of the two founding artists.

Fortified tower with quadrangular plan with Norman foundations, probably built in the 14th century, which takes its name from the Pallotta, lords of Brahalla between two and fifteenth century; restored in 1991. Since 2002 the painter Franco Azzinari has exhibited there, born in San Demetrio Corone: forty works of the collection "Twenty years with nature."
Three-absid parish with five nave crypt and Romanesque portal of the 11th-XII century.
The Gothic cathedral at the top of the white city.
The medieval church of the disappeared village.

Built between two and fourteenth century between the two squares, it housed the representative of the Florentine municipality and the town council, with rooms for wheat in case of war or famine; the works of the first fifteenth century for the apartments of the vicar marked the role of St. John in the Valdarno. Portici, crenellated tower and about 250 coats of arms of the vicars on the façade, from the first fifteenth century to 1772; in the atrium frescoes and coats of arms of the fifteenth century and the Marzocco. National monument since 1909, the name "d'Arnolfo" dates back to the post-war period and the restoration of 1934. It houses the Museum of New Lands on the foundation of the new cities of the late Middle Ages.
Sacred art and Venetian leather palades.
Park with a small lake of resurgence and paths, where is located the MIRA, route among the ancient roses with 185 varieties of about 40 species.

Romanesque church of the first half of the twelfth century, probably of Tuscan-Lombard workers, in limestone, reddish tuff and basaltic trachyte; also called Santa Maria di Ulumetu, takes its name from a statue of the Madonna found in the eighteenth century among the ruins of the disappeared village of Talia. Facade with architrave portal, frescoed bezel with Madonna and Child and cross window; interior with three naves on columns with decorated capitals, the central with wooden roof. From Christmas to Epiphany, it houses a crib made entirely of bread.

Large cliff that dominates the town, also called "Dente canino della Sicilia" or "Tomba di Polifemo" . At its feet was probably a necropolis of the late VI-early 5th century B.C., today covered by buildings.

Castelvenere is considered the most lively municipality in the South, with Falanghina, Aglianico and Barbera del Sannio (Camaiola); in 2019 it was European Wine City. The underground cellars in the historic centre host the Wine Festival on the last weekend of August.

Venue of the Municipality on Piazza Matteotti, joins the Palazzo Maggiore and the Palazzo del Podestà, built from 1289 perhaps with Eugubine workers; in 1476 it was donated to Federico da Montefeltro, who transformed it into a ducal residence, perhaps with Francesco di Giorgio Martini. On the façade the Madonna and Child in Istria stone (1680) and the clock; inside the vestibule with stone stones and frescoes by Giovanni Dionigi (1563), the Hall of Arms (1889), the Courtyard of the Cosmos with the Cosmic Order of Eliseo Mattiacci and the ancient prisons.

Antimony mine active from 1880 to 1987, the most important in Italy for the extraction and processing of this metal: during the world wars its foundry, built in 1882, produced 90% of the Italian antimony. The village preserves the foundry, workshops, chemical laboratory warehouses, the canteen and accommodations; the building of the direction, nineteenth century, is a Liberty style villa with Corinthian pronaos and friezes of leaves, festivals, shovels and picks, and houses the archaeological-industrial museum with minerals, materials and equipment that reconstruct the production cycle and the history of the miners. It is reached from a avenue of pine trees; it is part of the Park Geominerario historical and environmental Sardinia.

Promontory inhabited since the Neolithic, with the ancient acropolis and the remains of the prehistoric inhabitants; it is part of the archaeological park of the Aeolian Islands. Open May-October 9-19, November-April 9-16, holidays 9-13.30.

Artificial lake created in the twentieth century just over 1,000 meters, under the Dosso di Costalta, largely in the municipality of Bedollo; the beach of Campolongo, in the homonymous village of Baselga, is among the most animated places in summer. The Civic Tower, built between 1200 and 1300, was restored after the 1984 earthquake; around there are arches of the fourteenth century, baronial palaces and sixteenth century buildings. In Piazza Umberto I, an ancient meeting place, there is the artistic fountain in neo-imperial style of 1928.

Set up in the artisan workshop of the Scibetta family, watchmakers from the 18th century to the 1980s and masters in the construction of tower clocks: exhibits watches, tools, mechanisms, drawings, photographs and a rare universal geographic clock.

In the former Meucci factory, founded in 1813 as a calificio and flanked in 1897 by a charcoal, active until 1988 and then purchased and restored by the municipality, it collects machines and textile tools from the end of the nineteenth century to the mid-nineteenth century, including a turbine still working and a rare wooden frame restored; it tells the industrial past of the Val di Bisenzio and the recycling of the typical rags of Prato. It is part of the Prato Museum Network; guided tours and workshops for schools.

It preserves a painting of Our Lady with the Child between Saints Peter and Paul, surmounted by a fifteenth-century Pietà attributed to the school of Perugino; in the crypt the relics of St. Theodorus Martyr, patron saint of the country, whose cult flourished after 1738.

In the district of Castegnate, which began in 1958 and has been a parish since 1971, it replaces the homonymous church demolished in 1953 after the damage of a flood of the river, remembered by a stele in Piazza Castegnate. Brick hut façade with white pronao and mosaic on the portal, detached bell tower, tiburium with rhomboidal stained glass windows; preserves paintings from the 16th to the 18th century coming from the Chapel of San Carlo. The three sacristies, designed by Gerolamo Quadrio, were furnished in a little over fifteen years with wardrobes, kneelers and chests carved and inlaid by the shops Fantoni and Caniana, between stuccoes and frescoes, in a passage from baroque to rococo. From the third you enter the museum, opened in 1995 in a seventeenth-century palace purchased by the Pellicioli in 1670: 14 rooms with miniature chorals, vestments, the "San Cristoforo" of Tintoretto, the "Martyrdom of Saint Peter of Verona" of Palma the Old and 44 small wooden sculptures of the eighteenth-century Via Crucis. Closed on Tuesdays; groups by reservation.

Residence and defence of the feudalist, around which the ancient nucleus of the country was born: the present aspect is of the fourteenth century, but a Romanesque window suggests a first nucleus of the X-XI century. It passed from the Normans Motta Falone to the Sangineto (1343), to the Sanseverino, to the Telesio (1616-1740) and finally to the princes of Belvedere until 1806; the perimeter walls and the cisterns turned intact under the courtyard, while the north-west wing collapsed.

Granite massif between Padru and San Teodoro, at the southern end of Gallura; from the peaks of Punta Majore and Punta Coloredda you can see the Gennargentu, the beaches of San Teodoro and Tavolara. In the woods of holm oaks, junipers and oaks flows all year round the Pitrisconi river, with waterfalls, natural pools (such as that of Pitriolu), the waterfall of Scala Taddata and a gorge in granite; a ring itinerary follows the course and there are picnic areas. In the seventeenth century he lost his defensive function and became a noble palace. In the historic center near Piazza Mazzini, in a Renaissance building, tells the city from prehistory to today following two threads, water and weaving, documented as early as the 13th century and became in the 20th century textile district. The first open section goes from the Lombard age to the end of the sixteenth century and brings together marble, silver, codes, wooden sculptures and painted fabrics. Open from Wednesday to Sunday and holidays, closed in most of August; fully accessible, with elevator.

Probably on a Roman camp and a Byzantine fortress, it became a fortress with the Normans; damaged by the Turks in 1537 and rebuilt since 1564, in 1643 it passed to the Marquises of Love who transformed it into a dwelling. In 1692 Francesco and Nicola d'Amore frescoed the first floor halls in late Baroque style with Greek and Roman myths, Old Testament scenes and word games on the surname with Venus and Cupid. Open from Tuesday to Saturday 9.30-12.30 and 18-21, Sunday 18-21.

Historical heart of the city, with a medieval atmosphere, with an ancient restored fountain; the name is linked to the legend of the sailor Leandro or perhaps to the oleander. The Church of the Stella (or the Virgin of the Graces) is one of the oldest in the city, founded in 1274 by San Bonaventura and 1688 by the Archconfraternity of the Gonfalone, with twentieth century frescoes by Ennio Galice and the statue of the Madonna delle Grazie taken in procession on September 8.

In the center of the village; the oldest part dates back to the year 1000 and the restoration of 1917 left intact the Gothic-Aragonese parts of the 14th-XV century. Inside paintings, statues, an eighteenth-century organ and an altar in polychrome marble.

In 1290 he passed to Guido d'Alment, who arrived in Italy with Carlo I d'Angiò, then to the Capanos; the present aspect dates back to the restoration of 1610 wanted by Vincenzo Capano, XV prince of Pollica, and since 1997 he is of the Municipality. The Sardinian capital on the seven hills overlooking the Gulf of the Angels: the fortified district of Castello with Pisan towers and bastions, the Roman amphitheatre, the Punic necropolis of Tuvixeddu, the Poetto and the flamingos of Molentargius.

Outside the walls, enlarged in 1521 incorporating an ancient Gothic newsstand frescoed by Vincenzo Pagani with the Crucifixion, which separates the church individually into two; it has two altars. On the last Sunday of April there is a day out with lunch on the lawn.

The village of Alghero, 16 km from the sea and 14 km from the coast, rich in archaeology: the Neolithic necropolis of Puttu Codinu and the nuragic park of Appiu on the plateau of Chentu Mannas; in the village the Gothic-Aragonese parish of San Leonardo, outside the sanctuary of Our Lady of Interrios, and on the sea the beach of Pòglina.

Nearly a thousand hectares between Neoneli and Nughedu Santa Vittoria, on the slopes of Mount Santa Vittoria: secular holm oaks and gravy among granite peaks, once a source of coal for the whole island. Since 1983, with the opening of a forest yard, it is a permanent oasis of wildlife protection: Sardinian deer, deer, wild boar, wild cat, marten and, in recent years, the royal nesting eagle again. Walking, mountain biking or horseback riding trails lead to the view of Borta Melone (almost 900 meters), to an artificial pond and to the granite rock of Sa Crabarixa, about 50 meters high.

One of the five villages of the Cinque Terre, the only one not built on the shore; near the diving site of the Franata di Corniglia.
The Baroque Palace of Guarini with its façade "a wave" where Vittorio Emanuele II was born and the first Parliament of the Kingdom of Italy, now the seat of the museum of the Risorgimento, sat.

Olivetti's industrial and socio-cultural project, founded in 1908 by Camillo Olivetti: along Jervis street the path of about 2 km of the open-air Museum of Modern Architecture among the ICO Workshops in red bricks, Talponia, the kindergarten and the canteen, with the UNESCO Visitor Centre.

Roman amphitheatre built under Claudio around 41-42 AD, decades before the Colosseum, in stone of Valpolicella: axis of 152 and 123 meters, up to 30,000 spectators; since 1913, with the Aida of Verdi, it is the largest opera house in the open air in the world.
